What a truly numbing, mornonic experience packed as a game.
With Saint's Row The Third you get a very shiny, loud and colorful experience, puffed up with  cheap tricks, tasteless humor and badly written storylines that could make a case study on how not to build a game.
Outdated textures for it's time, the lighting is mediocre and the 3D models are low-poly. The moving animations are clunky and overall it feels like as if the goal wasn't on what's the best they could do but rather on what's the least they could get away with.
It goes like this: a criminal gang is taking over the city from other criminal gangs. Period.  It's not about the nature of crime or about an insight to criminal thinking or anything really that you could call multi-layered.
Another game in a seemingly endless line of games that just can't figure out money. You always have more than you need and by the end of the game your account is represented by a long line of '9''s on your in-game mobile phone. Money in this game feels like a completely random and unnecessary feature.  I personally wouldn't have felt a difference if they had no money in the game at all.
Definitely the most unsatisfying part of the whole game is combat. I can't think of a way how they could have made the shootouts more numb, plain, one-dimensional, emotionless. I couldn't care less about who, where and what I was shooting at, the experience was so zombifying. Nor did I ever have to think about ammo because I always carried a seemingly endless stash. In a fight, I gave up lifting my finger from the trigger, as it just seemed easier and faster to get it over with when I kept shooting aimlessly, pointlessly. I also seemed to have so many guns, one better than the other at killing off hordes of enemies faster than they could spawn. The developers appraently also didn't know what to do with them so they made the UZIs light people on fire and pistols seemed to have an explosion effect that made AI's blast away. I couldn't have cared less if I were using a bazooka or a pistol, they all...killed.
Your whole apartment has a customization menu trigger on it so you'll end up going to the menu quite often when you try to open the door to exit the apartment. And of course the game asks you every time if you want to exit the menu. It's a mess. Considering how customization-heavy the game is, I was surpirsed to see how few cool outfits they  actually had. The game acts as if you've got a lot of customizing options whereas  in reality it's quite poor. And it's all just gimmicks. It matters none what car you drive or if you go into battle fully armored or wearing a bathing suit, it's all the same and feels like they added it because it's trendy, but it ends up as another layer of clutter on top of this already-heavy burden.
Here's where they built the game upside down really. When you build a game you should first define what you want to do and then build the environment and the mechanics accordingly. With Saints Row The Third it feels like they built the world and mechanics first and then tried to fit some missions into it. As a result the missions feel very similar and chained to the limitations of the environment. They lack depth and inspiration. It's as if you were using the built-in assets of the sandbox which weren't designed with any particular mission or story-enhancing element in mind.
Saint's Row 3 had ONE mission, where they actually got it to work. It was a mission where the whole neighbourhood had turned into zombies, thus attacking you on sight and you were on foot. This seemed exactly the right kind of genre this kind of sanbox would have worked with. There you find yourself forsaken and overrun - the right kind of tight spot that get's the immersion going.

One of the older Total War games, this classic is still fun to play. An enjoyable blend of RTS and turn-based strategy. You start out as one of three Roman families, and proceed to conquer the known world. The world map is turn-based. On your turn you can march your armies, train more soldiers, hire mercenaries, and send out your agents to do your bidding. You can have your diplomats trade and ally with other nations, send spies to find their weaknesses, or send assassins to remove their generals and kings (or do all three!). When your army encounters an enemy army or beseiges a city, you can fight in real-time. Soldiers move in squadrons across the battlefield, flanking and being flanked in turn, breaking when morale is low, or staying to fight when the general rallies them. As you defeat nations, they are unlocked for you to play. Parthia, Britannia, and Carthage are three of them.
There are several issues with the game. Diplomacy can be rather frustrating, with enemies refusing to make peace, or demanding you become a protectorate when you are crushing them into the dust. Anachronisms abound (the entire Egyptian roster, for example). Graphics are dated, though the map view is still pretty.
Overall, though, the game is fun, and longevity is added through mods. Some like Europa Barbarorum overhaul all the races, removing anachronisms; others like Lord of the Rings change the game from the Mediterranean to Middle-earth. In the end, if you have not played it, or you enjoy history and can't get Rome II Total War to run on your computer, this is a good classic to have.

Fishing planet is a realistic sport fishing simulator that places players on the muddy shores of locations scattered across America. Cast your line into gentle waters and reel in a variety of fish, using patience and practical knowledge to successfully bag them. A huge assortment of gear is available to purchase; customize your loadout to catch particular fish, using the right rods, bait, and line to make the catch. Earn experience from every fishing trip and level up, unlocking new areas of the map, and earning money to purchase more equipment. Catch trophy-sized fish and rise to the top of the leaderboards, showing off your dedication and perseverance.
Fishing Planet has amazing graphics. It is still in the 'Early Access' stage on Steam but has a ton of potential to be the best fishing game ever made. It needs better documentation and fine-tuning of game controls, physics, etc. But even though it's not finished yet, it's fun to play. It's free to play, with lots of extras available for optional purchase. No forced underwater views, plenty of real-life fishing spots, a ton of tackle/baits, and a wide variety of fish provide lots of replay value.
Fishing Planet Key Features:
+ 32 Fish Species:  A huge assortment of fish swim in the waters of Fishing Planet, from Catfish to Pike.
+ 7 Locations: Travel across North America and fish in varied environments, taking advantage of weather conditions to reap the largest number of fish you can.
+ Huge Equipment Loadout: Purchase new gear and equipment to make fishing easier, opening up new opportunities.
+ Leaderboards: make the biggest catch and rise to the top of the leaderboards.
+ Relaxing Atmosphere: Immerse yourself in a soothing atmosphere and relax while fishing.
Pros:
+Realistic simulator
+Large customization options
+In-depth parameter choices
Cons:
-Long load times
-Lackluster tutorial
-Some random crashes

Assassin's Creed Brotherhood offers modest but welcome improvements over the previous entry in the series, Assassin's Creed II.
Graphically, it's very similar. I did notice a new day/night lighting cycle, and greater variety in character models around the city.
However, the gameplay has been tuned significantly. I found the free-running much smoother in this game; I spent less time jumping accidentally against walls that I didn't mean to climb. Brotherhood seems to know where I want to go much better than AC2 did.
But mechanics aside, it's the new mission structure that really impressed me. Brotherhood takes a lesson from the Grand Theft Auto series -- the city of Rome is huge, and there's always something nearby that you can get involved with. The major missions come more naturally; you don't feel funneled towards them in Brotherhood like you do in AC2. You can take them on early, or muck around in the city for a long while before addressing the major story.
And - the story. The Assassin's Creed storyline is still wonderful, and improves in Brotherhood. The cut scenes are well-balanced so they don't dominate gameplay. The body models are expressive and evocative, and the voice acting is excellent. I find that I really care about these characters and what's happening in the story. Also, Brotherhood really improves Desmond's meta-story.
Last comment - Assassin's Creed has the best cities in video games, hands down. Brotherhood takes place almost exclusively in Rome during the renaissance. The city and nearby countryside is massive! But the attention to detail is remarkable. You see different NPC character models in different parts of the city, and they change between night and day. People mill about in a realistic fashion; some have places to be, others chat in the shade. The ambient noise is fantastic. And never a loading screen as you move about.
So... Assassin's Creed Brotherhood is over 4 years old as I write this, so I doubt I'll convince anyone to play it who hasn't already. But it looks great, plays great on PC with a controller, and really delivers a satisfying experience. It's definitely worth your time.

Free to play but works best with a quite expensive premium account. As a simulation it's quite amazing with different types of fish having different habits, preferring different baits, and each kind can vary greatly in size. You really need to plan your approach and know your trade to be succesful. Definitely not that easy to learn and pretty hard to master.
I can easily recommend this one, if you are prepared to buy premium, at least in the beginning, to level up a bit and have more fish to choose from.
1. It's free so you can check it out for yourself.
2. There are many different kinds of fish, including normal, young, trophy, and unique variants. Each fish has its habits and preferences so you can't use the same approach all the time, you must really tailor it accordingly.
3. While premium account really helps a lot, it is not a requirement as there is no way to simply buy levels or high-level equipment without hard work. Premium speeds it up significantly, but if you are patient enough, you will achieve the same thing. The main hindrance of not having premium account is cash - you really need to make your stay in each state profitable and this is much harder without premium account and lower prices for fish that you catch, especially on lower levels.
4. Graphics are pretty good.
5. Community is really friendly and other players can tell you how they are so succesful using in-game chat. I have not encountered even one instance of real rudeness.
6. There is a lot of gear to choose from allowing a lot of customization.
7. You can always check which fish are available at each lake, along with what to catch them with.
8. There are a lot of decent guides on Steam and YouTube so you can learn the ropes without too much trouble.
9. The game is pretty stable and I haven't encountered any game-breaking bugs.
10. I love the travelling system. You can't just go anywhere you please, you have your home state, and each trip costs some money - you really need to plan them well to make them profitable, especially at lower levels.
11. You can still catch quite a lot of fish, contrary to most reviews here, it just takes skill and luck. I can catch 35 lbs of catfish in about 15 minutes, although I never really counted it, and I don't have a very high level, nor DLC or baitcoin gear.
1. There are some graphical glitches, like people warping across the lake, but nothing annoying.
2. Premium account is pretty expensive.
3. Rooms are small, I would love to play with more other people, exchanging experiences and competing.
4. Weather changes are definitely not subtle.
Note - I do have a premium account, I bought baitcoins once, and own no DLCs.

This Saints Row part was in my eyes the BEST Saints Row and one of the best open-world games.
-This game is much fun coop but also can be fun alone
-Almost every system runs this game (I was playing with constant 30 FPS on medium settings with a GT 620 and a low tier quad core i5)
-There exists a BIG sellection of weapons and outfits
-The Story is really epic and is easy to understand
-You can decide between chapters
-There are many rides with different features (mission cars)
-The map is big, so there is enough space to mess around with the police
-The Upgrading system is really ballanced at some parts
-The character customization is really good and was a gigantic improvement from the Saints Row 2 character customization
-There are many activitys you can play in your spare time
-There is WAY too much DLC (some of them only add some outfits or melee weapons)
-This game has WAY too many glitchs (sometimes you can glitch your car in a house and can't get out) and some missions will also glitch when you play coop with another player
-You need a second player for the three coop achievements and some achievements are anyways easier to do with a second player
-You only have to buy the Genkibowl VII, the Gangstas in Space and the trouble with clones DLC, because only these have achievements
-You can play on easy, because some achievements are really annoying with cops shooting at you
You DEFINETLY should buy this game if you have the spare money (even when it isnt in sales), but ONLY buy the DLC when it's in sales, because some of them have low to almost no content.

My initial prejudice against any horror game where you CAN'T solve all of your problems with a shotgun/chainsaw prompted me to be harsh with this game. I was scoffing often about the blurry opening segments, the wussy protagonist and his feeble instructions to himself to NOT fight anything as well as his delicate psyche that rendered him a wobbling goon if he was left in the dark too long. However, once I got past the opening segments of the game and deeper into the castle, I was engrossed with visuals of the game (the beautiful and the twisted), the fun little game mechanics (blocking doors with tables, throwing chairs through window, etc.) as well as the brilliant story that stays true to legendary horror authors like Blackwood and Lovecraft. The creepy exploring and simultaneous hiding from monsters developed into a very unique system of gamplay, and the absolute isolation of the protagonist (Daniel) helped the five guys who made this game establish the mood that they were going for (to scare the bejesus out of people). I have officially eaten my words about this game and remain duly impressed.

A rather simple, and often buggy game, but a truly organic experience making an immensly replayable game, especially enjoyed with friends.
---
A game where 6 players try to escape the level, whilst 2 of them are sercetly a monster that can kill (once enough blood has been eaten) once the lights go out (after a certain amount of time). The players must work together (or in some cases go their own way due to distrust) to figure out who the monsters are and escape.
Meanwhile the monsters must perform their monsterly duties (Drinking from blood bags and killing players) without arousing the other player's suspicions lest they be "kick from the game" by way of a group execution of sorts.
Whats great though is how you achieve this is up to you - as the monster you can appear to be stockpiling an armoury to fight the monsters but you're actually just making sure the innocent players can't have them - hindering their process. Similarly you can take one of the fuses needed to escape to the next segment in the appearance that you are trying to progress, but again are actually just hindering them. has a player caught on and is acusing him of being the monster? Convince the other players he is the monster and group execute them. You can even rat on your own teammate to further your own agenda.
As an innocent - is that guy helping you get the shotgun because he wants to help, or because he wants you to lower your guard around him? Is he accusing the other guy of being the monster because he really is? Did that guy just shoot another guy because he knew he was the monster? Or because he noticed he just grabbed a flashlight and wanted to put an end to the oposition?
Rather organic gameplay, a good bit of replayability, and its now free to play.
Get a mic though - makes it 1000x better.
*Edit* Worst thing atm, in my opinion, is groups of people using discord to communicate secretly and aid people on the other team - really ruins the game when people you know are innocent start shooting you to help their infected buddies.

I just want to get out there that this game takes elements from mega man, duck tales, and super mario bros 3.  adds in some original stuff, bundles it together, and the product is shovel knight, the best indie game i've played in a long time.  The game was created by yacht club games, a group of former wayforward employees. Never heard of them? neither have I. I mean, they're an indie developer. let's get into the review.
Story: Prior to the game, adventurers Shovel Knight and Shield Knight journeyed across the world alongside one another, but while exploring the Tower of Fate, a cursed amulet takes over Shield Knight and leaves Shovel Knight outside of the sealed tower. Grieving for his beloved, Shovel Knight gives up adventuring and goes into self-imposed exile. During his absence, the Enchantress rises to power, spreading evil across the land. Upon hearing that the Enchantress has unsealed the Tower of Fate, Shovel Knight begins his journey back to it, hoping to find and rescue Shield Knight. In order to do so, Shovel Knight must fight the members of "The Order of No Quarter," who have been dispatched by the Enchantress to impede him. Now, it's not directly stated in the game, but just about anyone can infer that shovel knight and shield knight really shared something special. i give the story a 5/5. A little simple, but it's entertaining enough. (& no spoilers for the ending.)
gameplay- shovel knight allows you to control the blue bombe- i mean shoveler through a variety of hubs and stages scattered throught the order of no quarter. Each stage you complte hhas you face off against a knight of the order of no quarter. the eight knights are- king knight, specter knight, treasure knight, plague knight(who could forget his bendy straw) mole knight, polar knight, propeller knight, and tinker knight. There is also black knight, but he serves as shovel knights rival. Now, your main weapon is a shovel, but you can by relics and shovel upgrades to make yourself even more badassand to smooth out the ride. relics require magic, and you can increase your magic limit as well as your health. The gameplay definently reminds me of mega man's and the world map is practically ripped from super mario bros 3, with a hint of ducktales' fighting mechanics. though stiff controls can make platforming a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥sometimes. 4/5
graphics- perfect classic interface. Character sprites and the environments in which they inhabit really stand out. 5/5.
music- pure sex to my ears. 5/5.
controls. shovel knight controls like a dream, though he can feel stiff at times, as metioned earlier. Best played with a controller, the keyboard controlls feel weird. 4/4
All in all, i give the game a 4.5/5, it's pretty damn good.
It's not just on steam, also. it's on wii u, 3ds, ps3, ps4, and xbox one for the same price!

I got this game after watching the Game Grumps playing it, and immediately spent the whole day playing it. As someone who did not grow up with NES or SNES games, mainly N64 and PS2, I'm not the one who wipes a single tear away at the sight of the retro pixel style graphics. I will, however, say that it really does look good and definitely utilizes mechanics of classic SNES games like the downward-pogo mechanic from Duck Tales and the platforming from, oh, every classic SNES platformer ever. However, the mechanics, while not completely original, do not come off as contrived. Shovel Knight was advertised from the start as Yacht Club's "love letter" to retro games, and it is very apparent in the gameplay, yet they manage to craft their own game, with unique and lovable bosses, cleverly designed levels that each bring their own, new sets of challenges to the player, as well as interesting save point mechanics and a value of in-game currency that creates a notable risk-versus-reward factor the player takes note of. All in all, even without DLC, this game is definitely worth the  money. 10/10.

If you are skillful strategist who loves the taste of challenge, your only option is very high. Sure AI makes some nonsense sometimes but its still fun if you aren't a diehard multi veteran that needs some hardcore challenges.
The amount of playable nations and map size are preety satisfying, nothing like in paradox strategies, but you get tense "live" battles that look simply amazing. Sick game, with a mind-blowing ending, as always when it comes to AC games. Takes everything good from the previous games and just improves upon it, with perfected details and stunning graphics & environments. The combat is excellent, fluid, and has been given more complexity and variety - even the story is incredible. There is so much nuance, and a ton of humor and clever lines to boot. Especially due to the last level of the game, I have gained so much more interest in Desmond's story. Excellent game, the best of the first three in the series.
It still has a few minor flaws and some unnecessary/pointless game components, like the purchasing of buildings (which made completionist status take SO MANY HOURS LONGER >:(  ) but that barely damages it, compared to how much they have done right and improved upon. The new character customization options are nice touches, although largely cosmetic and pointless. There are some sweet easter eggs in this game as well - like a Raiden costume from Metal Gear Solid. Why in the world did they include that? Lol.
The story is much better, clearer, and more relatable than the previous ones; it is better paced and much more cinematic. The best parts of the game are, yet again, the Truth puzzles hidden throughout the game - they are so intriguing, so complex, so mysterious and revealing simultaneously, and sometimes crazily challenging. I loved that part of the game the most. It was also my favorite part from ACII, so I am surprised that the devs were able to outdo themselves and make an even better set of puzzles than before.
Sadly, the multiplayer community is dying, and it remained a bit difficult to find even a single match - I waited for 10 minutes just searching for a match. But when I got to play, it was a ton of hectic, fast-paced, heart-pounding fun. The only other big negative is the UPlay software requirement and overlay, but it's not too much of a bother to me. Except for when it kept my game from EVER LAUNCHING. I had to run the game in compatibility mode for Windows 98 to get it to work - I have no idea why it would work in "Windows 98" but not Windows 8. Absurd, especially for them not to patch something so simple, yet so frustrating to have to figure out on your own. Ubisoft, you suck.

The campaign for this game feels short, but there is a little more variety when it comes to some sequences in the levels, (i.e. nazi infiltration using a choice mechanic, saving a little girl from behind enemy lines.), and the new squad features they added into the gameplay felt nice and seemless, like they should've been there all along. Although there are still quick time events. Lots and LOTS of quick time events. So be careful of that. Anyway, the characters I felt were well portrayed, and dialouge was believable. But I feel like there should've been more moments for your character and other members of your squad to bond, as you tend to spend time talking to some more than others. Sound-wise, there were sometimes when the dialouge did cut out at the very end of a sentence, so I wouldn't get the last word a character would say sometimes, but there were minimal bugs and glitches other than that, and almost no lag. And by almost, I mean it was still there, but not often at all. I also REALLY enjoyed the setpieces in this game, they felt a lot grander than the ones in Infinite Warfare. ESPECIALLY the train, that one will definetley stick around with me for awhile. Some gripes I did have with the campaign were the fact that nazi's and reich soliders were using guns such as the PP-SH? A russian sub-machine gun? I don't know what kind of research sledgehammer did for this campaign, but I would love to check whatever sources they got their information from on the subject of THAT. On the subject of the swastika not really being portrayed that well in the game by the publishers, I felt that, while a serious historical innaccuracy, it did not affect the gameplay, so I didn't mind it much. But it definitley brings up a "war-torn" discussion (at this point) of censorship in video games, and that's a topic I don't really feel like talking about. Another gripe I had about this game was that the main characters internal conflict wasn't meshed out really well. Sure it popped up here and there, but by the end of the game, your supposed to have this moment where your past meets your present in the epilouge, and while I felt that sure, it was very weak, and I felt it could've been implemented better. I did have another major gripe with this campaign until I sat and thought about it for a moment. There was really no central antagonistic character other than some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in your squad. No central villain to defeat like there have been in previous cod games. After the weak attempt infinity ward made in last years game to make Jon Snow's villain the next Kevin Spacey (even though he had MAYBE fifteen minutes of screen time). So I was really looking forward to there being some kind of evil nazi general for us to face off against throughout the campaign and ultimatley defeat victoriously at the end. And there wasn't really one. Until I realized that the whole nazi regime was the main villain. They were all bad guys, some badder than others, but we were all fighting the same war and the same enemy, there were no standouts. There were no Makarovs, no Shepards, no Raul Menedez's, no Kevin Spacey's for that matter, but I felt like that was the point. Because the Nazi's was this big, huge force, this big blob of hatred that we just had to cut down one soldier at a time. All of them were the same, and I think that really speaks to the spirit of what the war was about. That, or there just really weren't any historically signifcant nazi characters they felt during this time period. But to each his own.
The multiplayer is same old, same old for the most part. The only thing is, the maps are smaller (expect in war, but even then they feel a little too cramped), there aren't that many guns (for historical reasons, though, this makes sense), and there are still a LOT of aim-botters. It has its flaws, most definetley, but it can still be some fun. Also, lootboxes. I don't know if they're "pay to win" yet, but that is a major flaw that will probably unfortunatley never be fixed.
I don't have much to say about zombies because for I tried for half an hour and couldn't get a solid match with three other people in it. From what I did play though, with usually only one other person, its a much more grounded in realtiy, gritty, harsher and more terrifying experience. Not for the faint of heart.
In conclusion, s'aight.

Clever girl. Basing a Lego game off of a great movie and three cash ins. Well its been done since 93, but not this well.
Let me say this is my third or forth Lego I played, and the second one I owned. Yet this is the first one I really am getting into. I accually can not tell you 100% why I like this one much more then the Hobbit. But I will try. As for Jurassic Park games. Well I think I have played and own all of them. Or almost. Starting in 93 with the SNES and Genesis. Even Tresspasser and the Game Com Lost World. Lets forget about them. God knows I try. This game is good thankfully and easily the best JP game so far to me.
The puzzles seem simpler as there are not as many characters to shift through to find one with the ability you need. The setting seems better designed. For the most part everywhere you are seems interesting, and I was concerned that it would fail on this. Seeing how the other settings have more fantasy. Like Middle Earth or Gothem. No so. Everything feels like it is from the movie, and natural. Well as natural as LEGOs can do. The combat is... Well there is not much. So that should hurt it right? Nope. They have integrated the movies and level design so well it is not a thing at all. It's like Posi-track and duct tape. It just works.
So then to graphics. Top notch. Seriously this is a good looking game. I play all high visual games and yet this one really does look good. I thought the lego dinos would ruin this game, I was wronge. They seem kiddie, but they accually seem more fun this way.
The LEGO Silliness.(Since you know the story of this) The Humor is done very well. Much more polished then the other titles I have played. They handle death well.(It is kid frienldly and how I would imagine a kid would handle it) There were even a few moments where I started laughing. (My wife heard me one time and said,"What are you laughing at?" "Jurassic Park" "The orginal?" "Yes" "Do I need to call someone?" "No." "Are you sure? Cause thats messed up.") Really done surprisingly well. If you like slap stick this is for you. I never laughed at their other games, but here it is just funny at times.
Audio is good. But as everyone has said the older movies voice over don't sound good at times. One is so bad I was just thinking. Yeah this is how you don't do it. Any game now. How bad is the voice sound. Oh its LEGO Jurassic World Hammond in the trailer bad? Wow! Yeah a new low. The rest is good and at time stellar. The music is awesome ofcourse.
Overall the game play is a Lego game, but this is exceptional Lego game. It is also a Jurassic Park game, and possibly the best Jurassic Park game. So I look at games dollar per hour played. $13 and this has easily 20 hours of good content. This is a buy, and on sale it is a deal.

Narcissu 1st & 2nd is a Japanese visual novel developed by stage-nana and written originally in Japanese by Tomo Kataoka. This VN tells the story about the residence of
Setsumi Sakura and her experience during the last moment of her life.
This game includes both the Narcissu 1st & Narcissu 2nd. 2nd being the prequel and 1st is the main story of Setsumi.
The 2nd tells the story of Himeko Sunohara as her life take a 180 degree turn when she was diagnosed with a diseased that can't be cured, thus she's moved to the 7th floor. Himeko used to work as helper in 7th floor so she kinda used to the situation, but then it all changes when she met Setsumi.
Narcissu 1st set appx. 6-7 years after 2nd. The story is focused on the anonymous Protagonist (just think of him as us) who is terminally ill & Setsumi as both of them realizes their feeling of not wanting to die in the hospital or at home with their respective families. The two of them begin a long journey accross Japan until they find that place...
I have completed the game 2 years ago and when I found this game on Steam Greenlight, I immediately vote it up as I think this
first step of introducing the Visual Novel medium to the West. Currently the game is in Early Access but don't let that bother you because the story itself is completed & translated. I'm also part of the Closed Beta tester and I could say that Sekai Project did a good job of making the game engine compatible with Steamwork.
Definitely a must have if you are an avid VN player or you are interested in this medium, even after 2 years of finishing this, I still get
moment :') a Masterpiece indeed!

There is so much praise for Shovel Knight and most of it is justified, but I take issue with a couple of things that have soured my enjoyment of it.
First, I was enormously disappointed that Yacht Club Games didn't release the game on Wii U in my region (Japan). That won't affect you on Steam so I'll skip straight to my second point...
My biggest gripe with Shovel Knight is not being able to save the game after reaching a checkpoint. I would like to chip away at a game like this, maybe working through one or two checkpoints a day. I can't spend 90 minutes or more on a single level before having the option to save. Actually, come to think of it, I feel the same way about Super Mario Bros. That's another platformer which won't let you save until you beat the stage boss.
If, like me, you're a novice gamer and/or short on time, you might want to skip Shovel Knight.
Edit July 19th, 2015: I've changed my vote fom negative to positive because Shovel Knight is still an exceptionally good game despite my criticisms above.

The Story
DOOM is a game that puts you into the boots of badass demon-slaying, testosterone fueled motherf*cker that loves killing demons more than anything you can possibly imagine. Everything in and about this game screams badass as hell, from the Doom Slayer, the weaponry, the glory kills(believe me, they are GLORIOUS), the lore, the bosses, the demons, to the pure overwhelming feeling of being an unstoppable force. Hell itself cringes in fear at the very thought of your existence. The story about is compiled of the Slayer's testaments which are written by the beings of hell because they are afraid of you. As the Doom Slayer, you were once the leader of the Night Sentinels, a group of powerful warriors who were destined to protect and serve the Wraiths - the powerful beings who ruled the world of Argent D'Nur. The forces of hell desperately sought to use the power of the wraiths to greater their own strength and power. However, the demons could not overtake the world of Argent D'Nur because of the Night Sentinels and their ferocious leader. They lie in wait for an opportunity to exploit anything they could get their claws on to gain an upper hand in the battle against the beings of Argent D'Nur, when they saw an opportunity to do what they do best - to corrupt and indoctrinate powerful creatures rather than battle them head on. They had their eyes set on one man, the DoomSlayer, who was at the time, just the leader of the Night sentinels, who had recently lost his son. The demons forged a deal with him, they would resurrect his son IF they were lead to the Wraiths to steal their power. Scarred by the loss of his son, and desperate for a way to be with him again, the DoomSlayer agreed. The demon's deal was upheld, but not in a way that the Doom Slayer could have foretold. The abomination that was before him was the Icon Of Sin, his son resurrected. Being betrayed by the demons and forced to execute his own resurrected son, he was filled with an unquenchable rage. He was adorned in armor forged in the fires of hell by an unnamed being so that he can absorb the life and rage from his defeated foes. The seraphim bestowed upon him terrible power and speed, with his newfound might, he crushed the obsidian pillars of the Blood Temples, and set forth without pity upon the beasts of the nine circles. He was unstoppable by any of the forces of hell, but then from the lowest and darkest abysses of hell rose a champion, The Titan, after a great battle of attrition, was slaughtered by the DoomSlayer. In The Titan's defeat, the demon priests of the Blood Temples laid a trap to disable the DoomSlayer. Blinded by rage, he was lured into the tombs of the Blood Keep, which was brought down upon him. Once the Doom Slayer was incapacitated, he was placed in a cursed sarcophagus and the mark of the Doom Slayer was burned upon it as a warning to never unleash the scourge of hell ever again.
The Gameplay
This game is FUN, ok? From the very first 5 seconds of the game, you are popping heads, crushing heads, and ripping and tearing. As a long time fan of this series, it is so nice to be able to play a game nowadays where the concept of the original DOOM games is put into action. Gameplay and fun is FIRST, while story is SECOND. However, the lore of DOOM is expansive, around levels you can find codices that go into juicy detail. As you progress through the game, you will discover more weaponry, weapon attachments, suit upgrades, and health/armor/ammo upgrades. Not to mention you will find a larger variety of foes from the dinky possessed scientists, to the gargantuan Barons of Hell who will tear you the ♥♥♥♥ in half. At first I was skeptical about the upgrade systems and the rune trials, but they were implemented in such a way that was able to support the gameplay and make it more fun and customizable.
Now, time to talk about the glory kills. At first, I was skeptical of the execution system as I believed it would slow down gameplay, but I love these executions, they are creative, fun, brutal, and most of all, they promote a berserker like playstyle in which your enemies are not only bullet sponges, but are crucial sources of health, ammo, and armor. Doom really revives the spirit of the older games, where you are constantly on edge, managing resources and dodging near death misses while pumping your enemies full of lead.
Conclusion
666/10

I don't review games. I don't really think anyone cares what i have to say about them. But i can't hold my tongue on this one anymore.
I used to really enjoy this one, in fact it was my go to game, until they "rebalanced" the game a couple of months ago. I could log on, kill a few hours, have fun chatting with folks and catching fish.
Since the rebalance, it is nothing more than a grind game. And a slow one at that.
Heres what I used to  like: The game worked. rod and line physics were reasonable, i could catch enough fish to make a few in game credits and didnt have to micromanage.
All of that is broken now. the fishing line is like rubber. the rods are like slinkys. The fish don't bite enough to keep things entertaining. Costs are so high that i can't see how a new player would get anywhere. Heck I'm having trouble making the new economy work at level 38. And the social aspect is ruined as well. They added stupid 3D avatars that basically fill up every fishing spot and ditract from the experience. I can't turn them off, so I fish alone to keep from having <insert name here>'s arms and rod in my line of sight.
The devs have claimed that they fixed some of the issues by lowering travel costs at certain places and tweaking the physics. I don't see any improvement.
The way i see it, its a game. It should be entertaining, and this just isn't anymore. If i want to catch only six or eight fish a day, I'll wait for spring and walk down to my dock and do it in a couple hours.
I would have recommended this game 4 months ago, now I just can't. If you want to fish, go to a real lake.

The gameplay is purely strategic and very hands-off.  You build a fleet of ships, with the resources available, and you send them on their way.  You have minimal control over how battles pan out, and there is no gameplay beyond the battles.  Additionally, the interface is somewhat slow and unnecessary time consuming to navigate.
The most disappointing aspect of GSB is its blatant premium content model.  After you have purchased the game, you will be required to purchase a number of nominally priced DLC packs to get the full game content.  By buying this game, you are essentially only buying part of a game.

Even worse, once you've got strategies that work for you, the best thing to do is save them to reuse later.  While that cuts down on the tedium of rebuilding the same thing over and over, it effectively removes one of the few things you still had control over.
Combine that with the lack of any story to keep your interest, and this game grows boring in a hurry.  Try a more active and engaging game like "FTL: Faster Than Light" instead.

Ok, I have just finished the game and I really loved it. Here are the pros and the cons of this game:
The pros:
+ Deep level-design with brilliant puzzles, require logical thinking with some laws of physics.
+ Very detail environment to describe the Aparture Facility how enormous it is.
+ Nice intro cutscene with some references from Half-Life and a little bit from Bioshock.
+ The story is very well-written and acts as the bridge between the events of Portal 1 and 2. If the Portal Comic: Lab Rat describes what happened between 2 games, then this mod will be the game version with different perspective.
+ Good voice acting.
+ Hidden secrets and easter eggs are hard to find them so keep your eyes sharp.
+ 2 difficulties for you to play: Story mode (a.k.a Easy mode) willl allow you to enjoy the game story with simple puzzles throughout the entire game. Advanced mode (a.k.a Hard mode) is the same as above but the layout of puzzles will change a little bit, make them harder.
+ As the mod of Portal 2 so the game is optimized for low-end pcs.
The cons:
- The boss fight at the end is still easy, could have been more.
The game is very well-made and i have fun times with it. I do enjoy the story of original Portal series, and this game makes a bridge between the events of 2 games, even creates more mysteries to the series. This game is free (as long as you own a copy of Portal 2) and will make a good expansion to anyone who enjoys the story of Portal universe as well as puzzles solving. ONE THUMP-UP FROM ME!!!
Final score: 9.0/10, will be 10 if the final boss fight makes you apply more different methods to fight it.

Saints Row: The Third is a really fun game, in which you play the role of leader of the Saints, a rich gang which runs amok throughout the city.
The game is quite reminiscent of Grand Theft Auto.
There's an interesting story-line to follow, which you complete mission by mission - just about all of which involve some shooting or racing around in sporty vehicles (well, maybe some are not so sporty, but they're the exceptions).
There are also various extra missions which you can choose to take on.
Or you may even just choose to zoom around the city in your fast car, doing whatever you want - shooting at other gangs, police, military, or even innocent civilians, heaven forbid.
There is a wide selection of vehicles (cars, trucks, helicopters, planes, etc.), of which you can store a limited number to keep and use again.
You can even modify vehicles to make them hot stuff.
Some vehicles have to be unlocked by doing missions.
There's even a selection of radio stations you can play in your car (although it's a shame that, unlike the later Grand Theft Auto productions, you can't add your own MP3s to the radio).
You can also play Saints Row: The Third in a co-operative mode with a friend.
All in all, it's a game of serious shooting and major mayhem (as well as some not-so-serious shooting and minor mayhem).
However, in the name of greater social responsibility, I suggest that you use your powers only for good in the game - drive your vehicles below the designated speed limit at all times, and help little old ladies across the road - of course, you may succumb to mind-numbing boredom, but that's your lookout.
If you want a fun time, then I can highly recommend this game.

Channeling the very spirit of the
series,
explores the "endless runner" genre through the lens of a new canine: the Shiba Inu. If you're familiar with your memes, then you're also already aware of where the second inspiration of this game derives from (I actually don't know if the Pugs series is an inspiration). Moving on, very much like those little Inu legs, your task is simple: run, collect, avoid, and steal underwear. Those undergarments are vital to your success.
Run to progress (obviously), collect coins to customise your character, avoid unforgiving chickens and crows, and steal underwear from unsuspecting girls. This is
.
While the chicken looks like it came from
, everything else in this game remains refreshing. The background is suitable for the kind of genre and Montaro is just adorable. You're not buying an amazingly designed game (graphics wise), but the ones present in this piece are decent enough.
In regards to the window size, you're limited to, I want to say, around a 640x480 screen (720x480 at most). If you want to resize then... well, too bad, you're "SOL".
Although I didn't hate it,
doesn't really offer anything new in terms of sound effects. Overall, with the familiar "boing" and standard chicken sounds, they lacked uniqueness.
The three songs that accompany the game, however, are nice albeit repetitive. If anything, turn the music off and just listen to your own.
+ Cute pixelated graphics
+ Shiba Inus and wondrous dogs in general!
+ Profitable trading cards and emoticons; background as well
+ Ability to customise your Shiba - prefer a husky? Say no more!
+ If you're into memes, and Doge is the one for you, then what are you waiting for?!
+ Basic gameplay that comes at a decent price (true "you get what you pay for" content)
+ Good casual game for passing some time; just requires you to click your left mouse button in order to jump
± Cute soundtrack, but it does get a little annoying over time; in the same respect, the sound effects were complimentary but standard
- Small screen size that isn't unadjustable
- Why does hitting the crow/raven from underneath immobilise it, yet landing on top of it (like in Mario), immobilises Montaro? Shouldn't it be the opposite?
- Very unpredictable; while I get these kinds of games should present some kind of difficulty, this one is just... over the top. You honestly can't prepare for anything at all. Or maybe I just suck at gaming... that might be it
- Is it just me, or is the game sometimes unresponsive? Or perhaps we're just set up to fail with some of these obstacles... sometimes it feels like the game is hard just to draw out the amount of time spent getting the costumes (repetitiveness of the game)
I can definitely understand some peoples frustrations with this game. It has its moments and does seem like "just another game" that
threw into its cramped library. The unresponsiveness and random AI generation remains just that: random, and it truly is frustrating. Regardless, this was "just another game" that I did happen to enjoy, and I can understand if your feelings remain different.

It has ADSR , Delay , Vibrato ,  draw synth , fine / pitch bend ,  Noise and arrpegiator , not really a deep feature but its enough for a chiptune song. sound sample really help as for DAW , I need to recreate the chiptune sound by playing around envelop , oscillator , noise etc.  yes there are plugin for DAW , but the plugin itself is more expensive than Rytmik (not counting steam sales) , and DAW starts at 99$.
Rytmik works via clip (like a sequencer in DAW) at maximum length of 16 per clip , use sample and add your note ,  the note is limited to 3 octave (from C) , but there are extra octave option (-2 to +2). you can have 4 individual paramater to  control per clip and 1 global fx paramter per clip. clip has 4 channel (different instrument) with minimum tempo of 30 and max of 360 (60 in half or 180 in 2x) and maximum of 7 x 8 number of clip per song. You arrange the clips in a timeline (max. 254) with maximum of 4 clip track per 1 time.
Rytmik is very limited , like maximum length of 16 (it's hard to make melody) , no custom sound , no midi input and midi export. no piano roll mode, no extra mixing / effect , and feels very limited compared to song created via DAW
Good news is , they are now developing , rytmik studio (gen3) , which include EQ3 , longer clip (more than 16!) filter ,modulation , 2x ADSR ,LFO modulation, Automation , Simple Midi Input , reverb , master EQ etc. etc.
If you think Rtymik Ultimate feels limited but DAW is too complex to start a simple chiptune song , maybe you should wait for Rytmik Studio came out.
TL;DR Rytmik Ultimate is a good place to start music creation as beginner / hobbyist and could fulfil commerical level if you have enough music capability , but don't expect DAW level effect/feature, think of it as standalone 8-bit plugin on limited DAW

This game is a fantastic game with a well told story and a creepy feel with scares that will make you sleep with the lights on after playing. You play as Deniel a man who starts the game off by yelling at himself to remember and how he regrets drinking something, you black out and wake up with Amnesia. You go through the game finding notes from your former self telling you of a man who you must kill. you will also find pages from your own Jornals from long ago. These mainly will tell you the story of who you are or once were. Places through the castle will bring back memories to fill in the blanks. This game is as close to a horror game that you will find anywhere, the scares are endless and the mansion you are in couldn't get much creepier. Behind every corner there could be something wanting to kill you, or that last bit of oil that will keep you sain long enough to escape to some place less dangerous. There are many puzzles so make sure to read every note and listen to every memorie/flashback in order to solve them all. The only thing I found strange was how there is no penalty from death in this game. When you die it is almost a good thing because all monsters will disapear once you have died. This is not a bad thing but it felt like the game was making it too easy for me. But overall this game is a fantastic game with a crazy story that will make you want to play it again.

Summary: Grinding for characters is a chore, but most other aspects of the game are quite enjoyable.
PROS:
-Performance is great, graphics options allow for lots of fine-tuning

-Like all competetive games, people in multiplayer live and breathe the game, expect to lose and get flamed
-Being forced to run the game from Uplay instead of Steam is still an annoying and unnecessary step

This game's remarkable. It's challenging, exciting and unforgiving. But it's just as satisfying once you get a feel of it.
You start out in a minimalistic world, sitting in the infamous Toyota Trueno AE86.  A brief tutorial follows, which will probably result in you crashing into walls a lot, but that's fine, as nothing else really is needed to understand how this game works! The game then releases you into a free-roaming environment with a few missions you have to do to unlock more stages.
You can then also select stages, cars and tracks once in Free-roam mode.
As you get more familiar with the controls, the stages get more exciting and challenging/longer. They also come in several formats: Lap-based drift-tracks, Driftkhana, which is a highscore time-attack inside an arena, or mountain sprint tracks.
The goal is always the same, drift gracefully, score points, interact with objects such as poles to drift past or boxes to shatter,
add that up to the final score and remain away from hitting walls or losing your combo. Sounds easier than it is..
That said, car handling is the key, each car has their own way of handling, so finding what suits you most will be the way to go.
On top of that, drifting's the deal, so going fast won't always be the key to success either. Manual or automatic shifting? How high should be the turning sensitivity? Well, all these factors will help you optimize your driving style, making it possible to reach up to be the drift king.

As I'm nearing 600 hours in this game and with no intention to stop, I think its about time I say a few words about it.
TF2 is timeless. In 2007 this game was released and now, in 2017, the same game still maintains a community of players who have stayed loyal to the community for varying amounts of time, but we're all in this for mostly the same reasons.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Music is chill and not stressful, not sure how repetitive it'll get if you end up hardcore playing this in the longrun however.
Aesthetics are appealing and don't melt the retinas.
Game is challenging, some people will find this a positive.
Now for the meat of the issue.
I'm coming from someone who's played Need for Speed Underground series and I remember how much fun the drifting segments were.  I'm not super hardcore about cars but I have an appreciation for them, and I figured I'd play some cool drifting game to relax and destress.
Welp might as well stop right there.
The car handles like a flipping brick.  There are other cars you can unlock for different handling, but the starter car can catch on fire and die for how irritating it was to try and guide it properly.  It takes forever to get it going and have the speed for good drifting, not to mention the turn radious is a joke most of the time.
On top of that, there's no way to remap controls, and if you're on a keyboard good luck.  I found it more managable on the controller but only just (mainly to control the acceleration than anything).
The camera angle makes this even more annoying.  Going into it I knew it was some weird locked isometric view, but it just makes things even more obnoxious when compounded by a brick on an ice sheet of a car.
Ultimately, only would recommend for hardcore car/drift enthusiasts or something wanting a ton of challenge.  I could just suck at the game as well since difficulty is subjective, but the Casual tag is very misleading.

There is so much praise for Shovel Knight and most of it is justified, but I take issue with a couple of things that have soured my enjoyment of it.
First, I was enormously disappointed that Yacht Club Games didn't release the game on Wii U in my region (Japan). That won't affect you on Steam so I'll skip straight to my second point...
My biggest gripe with Shovel Knight is not being able to save the game after reaching a checkpoint. I would like to chip away at a game like this, maybe working through one or two checkpoints a day. I can't spend 90 minutes or more on a single level before having the option to save. Actually, come to think of it, I feel the same way about Super Mario Bros. That's another platformer which won't let you save until you beat the stage boss.
If, like me, you're a novice gamer and/or short on time, you might want to skip Shovel Knight.
Edit July 19th, 2015: I've changed my vote fom negative to positive because Shovel Knight is still an exceptionally good game despite my criticisms above.

TL;DR
Right so now that I've got the TL;DR down I will begin a little bit more indepth and hopefully a bit more constructive.
The game is a throwback to the age of platformers on the NES. This means Megaman, Legend of Zelda 2, DuckTales and Castlevania. This is one huge loveletter to the series of platformers and it even goes beyond that.
The game itself gives you short story that seems to have no bones to it, but reveals more when you progress further in the game which would assume they have more than just a single Shovel Knight in mind.
The game puts you in the role of Shovel Knight. A knight that uses a shovel for a weapon. You fight beside Shield Knight, your love and trustful friend until she dissapears. Que Shovel Knight amazing music and you're on your way to save your love and partner.
The game gives you as little instructions as possible in the forms of text, you'll play the game and learn about it automatically ISN'T THAT JUST DANDY?! A thing of the past and yet it is the best thing to ever resurface, not having to see tireless textboxes shoved in there.
After the first level you are thrust into an overworld like Super Mario Bros 3, where there are different icons. There will be icons for all kinds of nifty things but also the icons for the areas and bosses you will need to defeat to progress through Shovel Knight.
In these levels you will collect treasure and be ready to grab everything you can because these will allow you to buy upgrades. We're talking about more health, manapoints... How about a new armor that does something different? Or how about an armour that makes you sparkle so you can go on your quest looking like the dandiest of knights there are!?
Your shovel will also attain upgrades as you proceed to buy and collect treasure and soon you will find yourself at a boss.
The bosses are like megaman, 9 bosses, 8 knights and the dreaded enchantress! + your rival Black Knight. These bosses are a delight, everyone with a deep personality that makes them feel way cooler than just having a skin and a theme. These bosses all have a purpose they want to fulfill and a reason to be in the ORDER OF NO QUARTER!*Echoing begins*
Every boss has their own stage, themed appropriately aswell, their own music for the level and boss tune which are all delightful and will without a doubt make your feet tap and your skin crawl with how good it is... They even have the composer for Megaman in on this!
Now that we've got all the positive stuff on here I would love to talk about something that really didn't bother me, but may bother some.
NOT TO WORRY! There is a checkpoint system, but I know it can be a bit troubling for some. Just try your best guys! Some of the armors are a bit meh and found myself only using one particular one through the whole game.
Other then that there really isn't anything else to say... It's just a gem that needs to stay for more games.
Oh... Did I forget they're giving us
Where we play as one of the other knights? And they'll do it for more. Completely new combat, new enemy placements and so on so forth. FOR FREE FOR FREEEEEE.
Please guys. I beg of you, buy this game and support these game developers since they're doing all this RIGHT!

There's reused character models and animations galore. And unlike an expansion, you start back at ground zero with all your equipment burning so you have to re-earn it.

AC Brotherhood is the sequel to the highly regarded Assassins Creed 2. While they didn't reinvent the wheel with this game, they certainly improved and enhanced it.
Rather than the game taking place in multiple cities across Italy, AC:B takes place mostly in the city of Rome. However, Rome is by far the most detailed location in the game up to this point. You can upgrade local buisinesses in the world, take out guard outposts and burn them to the ground, and  run a local assassin guild you build from the ground up. Among many other things. The game is also noticeably harder and basically expects that you already played through AC2 before this one. It also features V/R missions like Metal Gear Solid so you can test your skills in the combat and stealth challenges. There's plenty to do in this game and the focus on side content is very noticeable.
So if you liked AC2, AC:B is the next thing to check out. On the other hand if you haven't played AC2, or didn't really like it I don't recommend this one. It expects that you have already played through AC2 and apart from the setting and the inclusion of a few new weapons it's virtually the same game.

Channeling the very spirit of the
series,
explores the "endless runner" genre through the lens of a new canine: the Shiba Inu. If you're familiar with your memes, then you're also already aware of where the second inspiration of this game derives from (I actually don't know if the Pugs series is an inspiration). Moving on, very much like those little Inu legs, your task is simple: run, collect, avoid, and steal underwear. Those undergarments are vital to your success.
Run to progress (obviously), collect coins to customise your character, avoid unforgiving chickens and crows, and steal underwear from unsuspecting girls. This is
.
While the chicken looks like it came from
, everything else in this game remains refreshing. The background is suitable for the kind of genre and Montaro is just adorable. You're not buying an amazingly designed game (graphics wise), but the ones present in this piece are decent enough.
In regards to the window size, you're limited to, I want to say, around a 640x480 screen (720x480 at most). If you want to resize then... well, too bad, you're "SOL".
Although I didn't hate it,
doesn't really offer anything new in terms of sound effects. Overall, with the familiar "boing" and standard chicken sounds, they lacked uniqueness.
The three songs that accompany the game, however, are nice albeit repetitive. If anything, turn the music off and just listen to your own.
+ Cute pixelated graphics
+ Shiba Inus and wondrous dogs in general!
+ Profitable trading cards and emoticons; background as well
+ Ability to customise your Shiba - prefer a husky? Say no more!
+ If you're into memes, and Doge is the one for you, then what are you waiting for?!
+ Basic gameplay that comes at a decent price (true "you get what you pay for" content)
+ Good casual game for passing some time; just requires you to click your left mouse button in order to jump
± Cute soundtrack, but it does get a little annoying over time; in the same respect, the sound effects were complimentary but standard
- Small screen size that isn't unadjustable
- Why does hitting the crow/raven from underneath immobilise it, yet landing on top of it (like in Mario), immobilises Montaro? Shouldn't it be the opposite?
- Very unpredictable; while I get these kinds of games should present some kind of difficulty, this one is just... over the top. You honestly can't prepare for anything at all. Or maybe I just suck at gaming... that might be it
- Is it just me, or is the game sometimes unresponsive? Or perhaps we're just set up to fail with some of these obstacles... sometimes it feels like the game is hard just to draw out the amount of time spent getting the costumes (repetitiveness of the game)
I can definitely understand some peoples frustrations with this game. It has its moments and does seem like "just another game" that
threw into its cramped library. The unresponsiveness and random AI generation remains just that: random, and it truly is frustrating. Regardless, this was "just another game" that I did happen to enjoy, and I can understand if your feelings remain different.
If you find yourself with some spare change, then try this out. It's not too bad, but do expect some "grr..." moments.

So this is going to be my second review ever. Normally I don't review games just because I don't have a lot to say about them. They are either good or bad and so that is how I would normally rate a game. However, Siege is a little bit different. I have a love-hate relationship with this game. So I am going to break down below what I think of this game after putting in over 600 hours into it.
First, lets get all the good things out of the way.
PROS
===================================================================================
1: Addictive
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This game is addictive. I mean highly, addictive. From the way the main gameplay loop runs to the way the guns feel, to the noises and sounds that permeate the maps and all culminates into an awesome sensory experience. Siege gets this right, the feeling of being trapped into a small location with bullets flying by and tense fire-fights. This is why I keep coming back for that adrenaline rush-like experience.
===================================================================================
2: No pay to win (Yet...)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Around a year ago siege was in trouble. It had a declining playerbase and reviews were 'meh' at best. So UBI did a really, really smart thing. (I know, UBI and smart in one sentence whaaaaat) But they did! They made all the content whether it was DLC or base game content unlockable in game. Of course you could purchase renown (in game currency) to unlock them quicker, but the normal renown gain per match was good enough so you could get operators. Then they released the 14.99 game (That is the one I bought) and again that was a brilliant move. Not only did you get a game that had the full quality of a AAA title but at the price of an indie game. Personally this move was brilliant. So yeah all the new DLC items are free, maps, operators etc. You just have to unlock the operators and skins via in-game renown and I am ok with that.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note:  The reason 'yet' is up there is I am concerned what will happen with the alpha packs, if you are new and have no idea what I am talking about it is essentially loot crates but I am not sure what UBI is going to fully do with them...
===================================================================================
3. Teamwork
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
It's funny that I am putting this as a pro because I am the least team-oriented player around but there is something so satisfying after getting a callout about an enemy location and getting the jump on them or doing a double hot breach coordinated with your teammate. The way teamwork is so integral to this game is also why it works so well. You "can" lone-wolf it and sure you may get a few kills but you probably will leave your teammates in a 4v5 situation and be the last one left dealing with all the enemies on the objective. So teamwork is definitely a must and once you get the hang of giving those callouts and being comfortable with locations and certain spots on the maps the game will truly shine then!
====================================================================================
So you must be asking yourself by now, "So if you have all these positive things to say, why leave a negative review?" I am so glad you asked my imaginary reader. You see, about... hmm... 2 months ago we were supposed to recieve a new batch of content (which if you buy the season pass you get unlocked automatically, no need to spend renown, and get it a week early!) However, instead of that it was silence and then an announcment that they were scrapping one part of the DLC's promised and instead going with a new idea for 3 months. In comes OPERATION HEALTH.
Now I am not going to lie to you, I was one of the few people super pumped for this. Basically, the premise was that Operation Health (OH for short) was going to fix most if not all the significant bugs players were running into that were game breaking. (I.E. Invisible characters, improper bullet hit registration, incredible lag... etc etc).  Basically, UBI had become behind on major bug fixes and wanted to fix the game proper before new content. I am all on board with that. EXCEPT, that is not what happened. I am going to break it down below what has happened.
====================================================================================
OPERATION HEALTH : MAJOR CON (Currently)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
So we got our first 'big' update which was one-step matchmaking or basically you click "look for game" and you can still mess about in the menus before the game starts, change loadouts etc. Yes, this was a 'feature' coming to an online shooter a year and some odd months AFTER its release. But ok, cool. I am all aboard. So update releases, breaks game even more. Here is where my main negative point comes into play. Sure they also changed up the hitboxes to allow for more realistic hits and that is FANTASTIC, I know some Blitz mains who were overjoyed in that moment. However, the hit registration got immediatly worse. Getting matched in ongoing games where the score was 0-2 is more common. More weird invisible character moments, floating and appearing characters, getting shot from angles that don't exist and more happen frequently now. I will even link a video below that shows most of the things discussed here. All of this and we lost content... It is just frustrating for a game that I genuienly like to see this happen to.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TLDR; Game is more broken than before, content delayed. Not in a better place yet.
====================================================================================
Here are just a few more cons
CONS
====================================================================================
Community kinda toxic now and Too much about Pro-League
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I am sure most of us in this community are guilty of some form of toxic behavior in a game or two but it has gotten to a point that I only experienced in LoL. Which that is saying something.
Example: I am playing a game, we are losing and there is a level... 3-ish on our team. Mind you this is in casual. So another teammate is berating him all game long about how bad he is. Finally, it comes match point. This poor level 3 who probaly has only played 1 game before gets tk'd by this guy who then tells him to just quit and blah blah blah.
Bottom line, people like this are not cool and I am seeing it more and more. It sucks being low rank and for your own teammate to do that is just crappy.
Also UBI just seems to care a little too much about the pro-league scene over the normal players. Which, don't get me wrong I totally get. It is more exposure, coverage and shows that the title is an 'E-Sport' but the normal player base is what keeps these games alive. I just want to see a little more care shown for the average player...
====================================================================================
Bottom Line: Game is fun but broken 80% of the time. Wait to get until larger bugs are fixed. UBI is still being UBI....

****UPDATED**** (Original review intact below this update)
This game was originally under the name "Hexagons", but has now had the title and many of the assets changed.
The developer of this game contacted me and requested I edit my review. They explained that the game has undergone changes to remove any Unreal Tournament 2014 assets from the project after being contacted by Epic Games.
I have advised the developer to contact Epic Games as they requested and explain the changes they have made to the project. At this time there seems to be visual updates, but some of the Unreal Tournament assets are still visible, particularly in the main menus.
The developer has been very civil in conversation and I am willing to give them the benefit of the doubt that they are attempting to change the game for the better. However, until significant changes are made and the developer clears these changes through Epic Games, you should still stay away from it.
****ORIGINAL REVIEW****
I could not properly play "Hexagons" because nobody was online to try it, so take that as a disclaimer.
Hexagons seems to be an FPS made using Unreal Engine base assets with a MOBA emphasis. That's about all I've got to go on since it has an online peak of six players.
When I booted the game up, it also said "Final Battle" at the top of the screen, which may indicate the game name has been changed at least once.
After checking out the Steam forums, it seems the game might be violating some usage licenses. Multiple people have brought it up and the Community Manager for Epic Games has requested the developer email them, which can't be a good thing.
I'd advise staying far away from this game because it seems like it might be about to get in some hot water. Hopefully the developer isn't using stuff without permission, that's a big problem if they are.

The game is a throwback to the age of platformers on the NES. This means Megaman, Legend of Zelda 2, DuckTales and Castlevania. This is one huge loveletter to the series of platformers and it even goes beyond that.
The game itself gives you short story that seems to have no bones to it, but reveals more when you progress further in the game which would assume they have more than just a single Shovel Knight in mind.
The game puts you in the role of Shovel Knight. A knight that uses a shovel for a weapon. You fight beside Shield Knight, your love and trustful friend until she dissapears. Que Shovel Knight amazing music and you're on your way to save your love and partner.
The game gives you as little instructions as possible in the forms of text, you'll play the game and learn about it automatically ISN'T THAT JUST DANDY?! A thing of the past and yet it is the best thing to ever resurface, not having to see tireless textboxes shoved in there.
After the first level you are thrust into an overworld like Super Mario Bros 3, where there are different icons. There will be icons for all kinds of nifty things but also the icons for the areas and bosses you will need to defeat to progress through Shovel Knight.
In these levels you will collect treasure and be ready to grab everything you can because these will allow you to buy upgrades. We're talking about more health, manapoints... How about a new armor that does something different? Or how about an armour that makes you sparkle so you can go on your quest looking like the dandiest of knights there are!?
Your shovel will also attain upgrades as you proceed to buy and collect treasure and soon you will find yourself at a boss.
The bosses are like megaman, 9 bosses, 8 knights and the dreaded enchantress! + your rival Black Knight. These bosses are a delight, everyone with a deep personality that makes them feel way cooler than just having a skin and a theme. These bosses all have a purpose they want to fulfill and a reason to be in the ORDER OF NO QUARTER!*Echoing begins*
Every boss has their own stage, themed appropriately aswell, their own music for the level and boss tune which are all delightful and will without a doubt make your feet tap and your skin crawl with how good it is... They even have the composer for Megaman in on this!
Now that we've got all the positive stuff on here I would love to talk about something that really didn't bother me, but may bother some.
NOT TO WORRY! There is a checkpoint system, but I know it can be a bit troubling for some. Just try your best guys! Some of the armors are a bit meh and found myself only using one particular one through the whole game.
Other then that there really isn't anything else to say... It's just a gem that needs to stay for more games.
Oh... Did I forget they're giving us
Where we play as one of the other knights? And they'll do it for more. Completely new combat, new enemy placements and so on so forth. FOR FREE FOR FREEEEEE.
Please guys. I beg of you, buy this game and support these game developers since they're doing all this RIGHT!

Relaxed, snappy little drifter.
When you first jump in, Absolute Drift can be a frustrating endeavour. Drifting invariably results in crashes, and there is no semblance of control. However, this frustration feeds the learning process which is the most satisfying thing about this game. Naturally, being a driving game, you set out trying to blast through courses. But as the game reminds you every so often, the goal is not to go fast, but to go sideways. Mastering this balance of speed and countersteer, though, is seriously rewarding.
You set out on your adventure through a driveable overworld. In each overworld portion, there are a number of events - be it a spinning, donutting and other acrobatics challenge, like Driftkhana, or a downhill winding drift course with plenty of edges for you to crash into. Each event has a number of challenges - ranging from "drift for 3 seconds", to "reach a x10 multiplier", etc. These are paced very well in that the challenge is often just a little bit out of reach, forcing you to hone your skills until you hit it. Complete enough of these challenges, and you can unlock a "midnight" course. These are tough downhill drifts, in the dark, often with no edges on the track. Challenges on these certainly test you.
There are also mini-challenges scattered around the overworld. Drift between two posts, or donut around a crane. These are much more forgiving than the event challenges, and completing enough of these will unlock the next overworld section.
The 10 hour journey from total amateur to drifting hero is a wonderful experience, and once the mechanics all align in your subconscious, you'll be going sideways without thinking about it. You'll definitely realise when you've reached the "zen" mentioned in the game's title.
For the price, it's pretty good value. I wouldn't have minded a mini-DLC with more courses and challenges, as I don't feel it got "quite" as hard is it could be. However, in its' absence, I'll be looking to the developer's next game with interest!

An interesting addition to the strategy genre, GSB puts entire fleets of customizable  and unlockable spaceships at your disposal. However, insead of an real-time stragety, this game is more aptly described as a "retroactive strategy game".  This means you as a fleet commander are responsible for placing your ships in formation and then doleing out predetermined orders and plans of attack for each respective ship. The drawback being you cannot give them orders once the match has begun hence, "retroactive strategy"
This is an interesting mechanic, though sometimes frustrating as the ships will not always fare well, and you are forced to watch from the sidelines as your carefully laid battle plan falls to pieces.
gorgeous detail makes you forget the 2D format of the battlefield, and the comic book worthy sound-offs from the units add hilarity to every battle.
A damn fine indie title all-in-all, but the command scheme could use a bit more of a forgiving approach.
