PLAGUE OF SHADHOWS UPDATE:
If you thought Shovel Knight was hard before (I didn't -- full achievements), then Plague Knight's campaign will soon change that.
Plague Knight controls a LOT more awkwardly, with less HP, more knockback (almost strictly worse), has somewhat awkward attack patterns, etc... Initially.
It's one of those risk/reward things, since after I got the hang of him, I was able to pretty much fly around the map taking out enemies with precision. Mind you, this won't be easy at first, since the number of times I shot myself into spikes, or just missed/slightly overshot a platform, bumped into an enemy to my doom, pressed the wrong sequence of buttons to stop myself from falling were many. But the pay-off is very worth it -- for example, going back to fighting Spectre Knight (?.. the ghost one), he initially mopped the floor with me, but the second time around I was flying all around him, dodging his attacks/hitting him from safe angles..
All plague-knight levels are tweaked, and some include secret passages for a slightly more difficult path for (a something). The bosses play identically, however, since your movement style and attack patterns are completely different this changes things up in a nice way. This should not come as a spoiler (you had to have predicted it) but when you fight shovel knight himself, it is just great to see how they gave his boss music the epic boss fight theme that matched the happy tune of the intro level/shovel knight theme.
It is also interesting how they changed to world so you see it from the eyes of this villain (misunderstood?). The story is again mostly bare-bones just like how shovel knight tried to emulate the NES games of glory.
New Challenge Maps: There are also some legitimately difficult challenge maps which are fun little side missions. I hope they eventually release the exclusives for PC.
Overall, I hope there are more expansions (free or not), or sequels. Plague knight has been a great addition to the game (again, if you find it way too hard, stick with it, because once you figure him out it is a *lot* more fun).
**SPECTRE KNIGHT UPDATE
I'll keep it brief since the level of quality is top notch. I wondered how they would update this game without adding "just another character"... they did it, and it's amazing.
Great new remixes on the music, spectre knight plays like a charm in his updated levels (a lot more changes to the levels than Plague Knight had in his DLC), an interesting new take on the "in-between levels" (home base now, not map).
If you've already enjoyed Shovel Knight, Spectre Knight is definitely a reason to come back and see what's new.

Welcome to Boon Hill is a graveyard simulator game (which I had honestly never heard of before playing this). There is no goal to the game; no perilous situations to overcome, no goals to complete that signify completion.  “Why would I want to play this game?” you may ask, or “What’s the point of it all?” Here are some reasons why I think this game is worth your 5 bucks.
The beauty of this game is that it allows for you to create your own experience. You play as a mysterious boy or girl, wandering around the Boon Hill cemetery reading as many epitaphs (messages on the gravestones) as you please, pondering some and dismissing others. Some may come off as funny, others meaningful, and some as downright depressing. There are hundreds gravestones to read and each message is different with its own meaning. This experience is yours: you may leave when you please and stay for however long you want. While exploring, you will notice the mysterious music; relaxing one moment then suddenly eerie the next.
I would recommend this game to those who enjoy piecing together information that they collect along their way, even if that information does not fit together necessarily well. Also people who want to experience an immersive environment with many hidden insights, tragedies, and stories of success and happiness waiting to be read. If you do not like the idea of investigating the past lives of people who once lived, or walking with no seeming purpose in mind, just traveling from one grave marker to the next, you may not enjoy this game.
If you feel beckoned to explore a graveyard at any time, or are even remotely interested in visiting a graveyard, you should try this game out! It offers a similar experience, all from the comfort of your home. For only $5, there isn’t much to lose.

Welcome to Boon Hill is an indie game that at first glance looks pretty straight forward. Walk around a graveyard in search of grave stones. There are no zombies, no high score, and no guns. Why on Earth would you play a game like this you ask?
Well you quickly find there's far more depth than at first glance. I came to Boon Hill thinking "ok I'll spend about 5 minutes walking around and get bored". Well a few minutes turned into an hour and I was completely drawn into seeking out more epitaphs to piece together the stories of life and death.
The death of a child, a person that lived life to the fullest, un marked graves, even some funny little easter eggs are all you'll find in just the first hour of play. I feel like there's still more to get out of it. If you enjoy games that allow you to search for clues and piece together stories from the mundane to creepy Welcome to Boon Hill would be worth it for you.

Traveler's Tales' LEGO series, based on various licensed properties, has become somewhat of a staple in many video game collections since its inception with the the 'LEGO Star Wars' games, so after seeing 'Jurassic World' I was ready to go through the LEGO tie-in game, and after a couple of days, I've been left with a dissappointing experience.
There have been many other reviews already talking about the plethora of bugs within the game, and I ran into quite a few myself, two of which halted my progress and forced me to restart the levels I found them on, one of them prevented me from building something because I previously broke some nearby boxes, which is very counterintuitive for a bloody lego game.
However, they also included voice acting for this one, and whilst it's heartwarming to hear Jeff goldblums' laugh (and voice in general) come out of a LEGO figure, the age of the audio become apparent, since it's taken from the original 'Jurassic Park' so the difference in quality between audio from 2015 and 1993 is seen rather easily.
This leads to another problem with the game. It isn't funny. Aside from a chuckle or two I got from the raptors and their shenanigans, none of the humour appealed to me. This is partially to blame on the inclusion of voice acting, since the strength of previous LEGO titles was the physical comedy, it was probably one of the main reasons I loved the LEGO series, but it's been diminished significantly in favour of mediocre verbal comedy, which takes away quite a bit of enjoyment from the game.
The game is strangely anti-death aswell, but I won't dwell too much on that, just know that nodoby dies in LEGO jurassic world, including one character who survived being eaten by being thrown back up a short while later.
However, there is fun to be had in LEGO Jurassic World, the gameplay is as strong as ever, it's still the standard LEGO game affair, smash everything and anything breakable in sight, and attentively searching the levels for the minikits (Most of which are well placed) still manages to be both fun and challenging. A lot of detail has also been put into the open world aspect of it. There's also the option to play as dinosaurs, which is as epic as it sounds!
On the whole though, it's a bit of a mediocre experience for me, but would I recommend the game? Short answer: Probably not. If you love the other LEGO games, you'll probably like this one (If it works for you), however, if your new to the LEGO games, don't buy this one. Get 'LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga' Instead, It's not as buggy, cheaper, funnier and is based on a better film franchise.
TL;DR: Dissappointing. Weak humour, but still has good lego collectathon style gameplay. Not even Jeff Goldblum and playing as a T-Rex could save this one.
Final Score: 6/10

As another LEGO game, for the most part it's fairly good. It runs fine on less advanced systems, it looks pretty good graphically and it recreates multiple scenes from each of the Jurassic Park films rather well with an additional sprinkle of TT brand humour that we've all come to be familiar with in these games. Also you can make your own dinosaurs by collecting amber in each of the levels, which is cool.
I just wish there was a little more content than just 5 levels per movie and more open-ended hub worlds. Don't get me wrong, 20 levels is plenty for a LEGO game, heck most of the other games settle with 15! But I just don't think 5 levels was enough to draw out around 2 hours worth of film footage. A lot of the dialogue and scenes are often slightly cut or scrambled. Add 1 or 2 more levels per film segment, then maybe it could've been a little better, I'm not too sure.
As for the hub worlds, the only one I really like is the Jurassic Park hub. There's enough space to walk and drive around. By comparison, the other hubs feel too restrictive with where you can drive and where you can't, assuming you don't wanna run everywhere, same applies with dinosaurs.
Overall, it's good for the most part but absolutely not among the best LEGO games out there. I wouldn't advise against buying this game, it's still enjoyable to see the world of Jurassic Park in LEGO form (plus LEGO Jeff Goldblum, how can you go wrong?), but for a more enjoyable LEGO game, LEGO Marvel Super Heroes or any of the LEGO Batman games are right up there.

This is definintely an interesting game. While most tower defense games let you build stuff as the battle progresses, this is the opposite where you have to set up everything beforehand and hope for the best. To be honest, it's kind of refreshing just being able to sit and relax and watch the battle play out. There's a mode where actually can take control of a ship, but doing so disallows some rewards.

Some things could be balanced better. I haven't thoroughly explored strategies yet, but from what I played, Fighters are basically worthless. I'd like to see more ship classes, like the dreaded Doom Star, or even Star Fortresses and planetary defenses (Master of Orion II talk here).
Quite frankly, if they somehow were to combine this game with Master of Orion II... that would be the most amazing ******* thing ever! (Granted, Master of Orion III did *something* like this, but that game as a whole needed work, badly). With some funding and shiny 3D graphics, I think they'd have something really special here.
If you're on the fence, give the demo a try. It gives you a good idea of what you're in for.

It is a okay game. I recommend it, but you have to know that its the same old Lego formula with no innovation whatsoever.
Pros:
+ runs super smooth
+ great controller layout
+ pretty lenghty game (a little bit too stretched out at times)
+ easy to understand even for younger kids
+ beautiful graphics
+ love for detail, the world is filled with easter eggs and little nods to the Jurassic Park universe
+ local coop
+ all Jurassic Park movies were recreated
+ various characters that have different abilities, even the smallest staff member is in here
+ they didnt just recreate scenes from the movies, they actually thought out clever new levels, sceneres and additional paths for the heroes to go through, along with a faithful Lego recreation of the beloved movies
+ in the german dub, many voice actors from the original movie reprised their roles, which is fantastic
+ Nvidia 3D TV Play looks awesome. Like its meant to be played in stereoscopic 3D (even cutscenes are 3D)
+ create-your-own-dinosaur
+ replayability if you want all the characters and collectibles
Cons:
- unfortunatley its the same old formula that is being used for EVERY Lego game, destroy everything, pick up coins, build something to unlock new path and repeat, it gets old pretty fast. I was disappointed to see that they didnt even try something new
- picking up coins is a chore, its not particulary neccessary but you still kinda want to see what you can unlock, picking coins up stretches the games lenght by a lot and is just tedious
- breaking all the stuff breaks immersion a little bit, a character is in danger and you gotta hurry, but instead you search slowly through the level what to break to get all the coins.....it slows down the games action scenes by a lot
- coop partners still can hurt each
there is no reason why you could hit each other in these type of games. Especially when you are playing with a younger kid that smashes the punch button to break all the blocks in the level, comboing the partner to death....its not really coop friendly
- they approached a new open world feel, but ultimatley I whished they would have gone back to a simple level select screen, its tedious to get to the next location and its not clear where you can buy or unlock new things
- the DLCs are terrible! Absolutley cosmetic, but the text makes you belive you get to be a tourist in Jurassic World, but its just a usless skin, the same goes for vehicles, every car feels the same
Overall its a Lego game. Can be fun in coop and looks beautiful. Personally I get tired of the same game with different license, but if you like that definitley get this one too. Its faithful to the movies and universe. A fun ride to enjoy.

I wanted to like this software...  There are good and bad points about it.
It does remind me of Amiga software I used many years ago, but the bad unfortunately offsets the good.  The EULA basically says that any songs put in cloud are owned by CINEMAX, this could legally mean that if you use the song that you make commercially, they could sue you as they own a copy.  I am not saying that they "would" do this, just that the ramifications are there.
The other big negative for me is that you can't import your own audio.  This limits you to the instruments provided in the software.
Also, the instruments (loops?) provided are set up on buttons for drag and drop, but they are labeled 1, 2, 3 etc which means until you click it, you are not sure what the instrument is going to sound like (is it a drum, a lead, bass line?).
I hope this review helps. the software looks pretty good and sounds good... Synthy (if that's a word)... but good.
The fact that the dev is actively upgrading the software is a good sign, they haven't just made the software and dumped it on Steam to sell whatever they can.
I hope that they keep up the good work and adding features/fixes, but unfortunately, this software isn't right for me.
I WOULD recomend this software to people who are new to writing songs as the software does all the hard work.  I would not recomend it to a serious musician however.

I have not played this game in over a year, but I feel it's time to state that it is not worth playing this game... It is very much pay-to-win.
Under normal conditions, the gameplay is great : It encourages teamwork (for example, you can only heal in most game modes by having a teammate do the healing on you... only way to heal yourself is picking up the resupply boxes droped by kills.), it has great ideas for gameplay (It was heck of a lot of fun shooting at terrorists from the backseat of a car going at a high speed.) and under normal conditions, it is balanced.... under normal conditions...
Here is where the pay-2-win comes in... while you do get enough starting credits to buy you a perament reliable starting weapon to let you stand out in the crowd for a bit if you know what your doing (in my case, I got the combat shotgun, letting me win most CQC senarios), you just dont have the funds to keep yourself equiped for every senario at all times, for you eigher must stick to the normal gear that provides very little advantages or you can buy the somewhat better gear, which while it does give somewhat of a edge, it also is all expensive to keep as perament, as the perma price is extreamly high. (in fact, it's more expensive to buy a perament set of headphones.... HEADPHONES!... then the combat shotgun carrying the same unlimited duration)
Meanwhile, you find the whales, which are a even worse problem then most F2P games. While sometimes, a whale has only the advantage of sightly higher stats or is able to get to key equipment faster then the free guys, in this game, they are OP as heck.
Example : normal hostage match... 8v8, I am on terrorist and we are doing okey... suddenly, here comes two guys, both equiped with riot shields that have far more durability then normal, body armour that lets them survive most attacks, TMPs that are far superior then the free variant, and both with attack dogs that, also unlike their free counterparts, have body armour, making them durable enough that they dont die after taking all 6 rounds of the combat shotgun to the face as they rip the faces of the entire enemy team.
Alongside all this, the game's visuals and sound sounds very well rushed, such as old-style graphics that are PS2 era in terms of apperence (and that is not a term I use very often), the sarcastic-sounding cries for help when someone calls for a medic, and the menu layouts overall that make some simple tasks difficult. The community is also a issue, as while there are penalities for griefing or making errors... they are just too little (for example, only a 25 XP loss for running over your teammate when the average game rakes in 500-1000? Really?), and thus you sometimes get these senarios where in games where FF is on (or any round involving a car), you may encounter a guy who does nothing but shoot/runs over his teammates or hostages.
Overall... 2/10... would consider making a mod to put some stuff like this in a better built game like Counter Strike, but otherwise would not play again.

So this is going to be my second review ever. Normally I don't review games just because I don't have a lot to say about them. They are either good or bad and so that is how I would normally rate a game. However, Siege is a little bit different. I have a love-hate relationship with this game. So I am going to break down below what I think of this game after putting in over 600 hours into it.
First, lets get all the good things out of the way.
PROS
===================================================================================
1: Addictive
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This game is addictive. I mean highly, addictive. From the way the main gameplay loop runs to the way the guns feel, to the noises and sounds that permeate the maps and all culminates into an awesome sensory experience. Siege gets this right, the feeling of being trapped into a small location with bullets flying by and tense fire-fights. This is why I keep coming back for that adrenaline rush-like experience.
===================================================================================
2: No pay to win (Yet...)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Around a year ago siege was in trouble. It had a declining playerbase and reviews were 'meh' at best. So UBI did a really, really smart thing. (I know, UBI and smart in one sentence whaaaaat) But they did! They made all the content whether it was DLC or base game content unlockable in game. Of course you could purchase renown (in game currency) to unlock them quicker, but the normal renown gain per match was good enough so you could get operators. Then they released the 14.99 game (That is the one I bought) and again that was a brilliant move. Not only did you get a game that had the full quality of a AAA title but at the price of an indie game. Personally this move was brilliant. So yeah all the new DLC items are free, maps, operators etc. You just have to unlock the operators and skins via in-game renown and I am ok with that.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note:  The reason 'yet' is up there is I am concerned what will happen with the alpha packs, if you are new and have no idea what I am talking about it is essentially loot crates but I am not sure what UBI is going to fully do with them...
===================================================================================
3. Teamwork
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
It's funny that I am putting this as a pro because I am the least team-oriented player around but there is something so satisfying after getting a callout about an enemy location and getting the jump on them or doing a double hot breach coordinated with your teammate. The way teamwork is so integral to this game is also why it works so well. You "can" lone-wolf it and sure you may get a few kills but you probably will leave your teammates in a 4v5 situation and be the last one left dealing with all the enemies on the objective. So teamwork is definitely a must and once you get the hang of giving those callouts and being comfortable with locations and certain spots on the maps the game will truly shine then!
====================================================================================
So you must be asking yourself by now, "So if you have all these positive things to say, why leave a negative review?" I am so glad you asked my imaginary reader. You see, about... hmm... 2 months ago we were supposed to recieve a new batch of content (which if you buy the season pass you get unlocked automatically, no need to spend renown, and get it a week early!) However, instead of that it was silence and then an announcment that they were scrapping one part of the DLC's promised and instead going with a new idea for 3 months. In comes OPERATION HEALTH.
Now I am not going to lie to you, I was one of the few people super pumped for this. Basically, the premise was that Operation Health (OH for short) was going to fix most if not all the significant bugs players were running into that were game breaking. (I.E. Invisible characters, improper bullet hit registration, incredible lag... etc etc).  Basically, UBI had become behind on major bug fixes and wanted to fix the game proper before new content. I am all on board with that. EXCEPT, that is not what happened. I am going to break it down below what has happened.
====================================================================================
OPERATION HEALTH : MAJOR CON (Currently)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
So we got our first 'big' update which was one-step matchmaking or basically you click "look for game" and you can still mess about in the menus before the game starts, change loadouts etc. Yes, this was a 'feature' coming to an online shooter a year and some odd months AFTER its release. But ok, cool. I am all aboard. So update releases, breaks game even more. Here is where my main negative point comes into play. Sure they also changed up the hitboxes to allow for more realistic hits and that is FANTASTIC, I know some Blitz mains who were overjoyed in that moment. However, the hit registration got immediatly worse. Getting matched in ongoing games where the score was 0-2 is more common. More weird invisible character moments, floating and appearing characters, getting shot from angles that don't exist and more happen frequently now. I will even link a video below that shows most of the things discussed here. All of this and we lost content... It is just frustrating for a game that I genuienly like to see this happen to.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TLDR; Game is more broken than before, content delayed. Not in a better place yet.
====================================================================================
Here are just a few more cons
CONS
====================================================================================
Community kinda toxic now and Too much about Pro-League
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I am sure most of us in this community are guilty of some form of toxic behavior in a game or two but it has gotten to a point that I only experienced in LoL. Which that is saying something.
Example: I am playing a game, we are losing and there is a level... 3-ish on our team. Mind you this is in casual. So another teammate is berating him all game long about how bad he is. Finally, it comes match point. This poor level 3 who probaly has only played 1 game before gets tk'd by this guy who then tells him to just quit and blah blah blah.
Bottom line, people like this are not cool and I am seeing it more and more. It sucks being low rank and for your own teammate to do that is just crappy.
Also UBI just seems to care a little too much about the pro-league scene over the normal players. Which, don't get me wrong I totally get. It is more exposure, coverage and shows that the title is an 'E-Sport' but the normal player base is what keeps these games alive. I just want to see a little more care shown for the average player...
====================================================================================
Bottom Line: Game is fun but broken 80% of the time. Wait to get until larger bugs are fixed. UBI is still being UBI....

PLAGUE OF SHADHOWS UPDATE:
If you thought Shovel Knight was hard before (I didn't -- full achievements), then Plague Knight's campaign will soon change that.
Plague Knight controls a LOT more awkwardly, with less HP, more knockback (almost strictly worse), has somewhat awkward attack patterns, etc... Initially.
It's one of those risk/reward things, since after I got the hang of him, I was able to pretty much fly around the map taking out enemies with precision. Mind you, this won't be easy at first, since the number of times I shot myself into spikes, or just missed/slightly overshot a platform, bumped into an enemy to my doom, pressed the wrong sequence of buttons to stop myself from falling were many. But the pay-off is very worth it -- for example, going back to fighting Spectre Knight (?.. the ghost one), he initially mopped the floor with me, but the second time around I was flying all around him, dodging his attacks/hitting him from safe angles..
All plague-knight levels are tweaked, and some include secret passages for a slightly more difficult path for (a something). The bosses play identically, however, since your movement style and attack patterns are completely different this changes things up in a nice way. This should not come as a spoiler (you had to have predicted it) but when you fight shovel knight himself, it is just great to see how they gave his boss music the epic boss fight theme that matched the happy tune of the intro level/shovel knight theme.
It is also interesting how they changed to world so you see it from the eyes of this villain (misunderstood?). The story is again mostly bare-bones just like how shovel knight tried to emulate the NES games of glory.
New Challenge Maps: There are also some legitimately difficult challenge maps which are fun little side missions. I hope they eventually release the exclusives for PC.
Overall, I hope there are more expansions (free or not), or sequels. Plague knight has been a great addition to the game (again, if you find it way too hard, stick with it, because once you figure him out it is a *lot* more fun).
**SPECTRE KNIGHT UPDATE
I'll keep it brief since the level of quality is top notch. I wondered how they would update this game without adding "just another character"... they did it, and it's amazing.
Great new remixes on the music, spectre knight plays like a charm in his updated levels (a lot more changes to the levels than Plague Knight had in his DLC), an interesting new take on the "in-between levels" (home base now, not map).
If you've already enjoyed Shovel Knight, Spectre Knight is definitely a reason to come back and see what's new.

I don't know why I like these games, but I do. Wierd.
---------------------------------
Although I liked some of the other Airport Madness games, this one actually took a step back.
So yeah, it has a bit better graphics and the camera it situated to give you a more close-up view, though it doesn't add to the game.
In addition:
- Changes to keybinds. Old keybinds used to at least be 1-5 so as to keep all your commands close together. They changed this and moved the keys all over the keyboard thus making them almost useless. Oh and keys can't be remapped.
- Lack of control from top-down means it's very difficult when traffic gets heavy to select the right aircraft to adjust flight paths.
- Lack of top-down control makes selecting aircraft in a super busy airport a real chore.
- If you're trying to select an aircraft and misclick, you have to basically double click every time to turn off the wrong selection and then turn on the one you want. So instead of being able to select Plane A, Plane B and Plane C in 3 clicks, it would actually take 5 (or 6) clicks. This makes zero sense in a game where you need to be quick and efficient with your orders.
- Click commands are permanently in the upper left-hand side of the screen. So you have to keep moving the mouse in large sweeps to issue orders.
- They put tags on the aircraft which not only point out the individual targets but it also says what the aircraft are doing. I like this from an information standpoint. Logically you should also be able to click these tags to select aircraft. Nope. SOMETIMES you can click the tags and it will work, then other times you can't. Lack of consistancy.
I've played and enjoyed some of the other Madness games for many hours. But after playing this for one evening, I just became frustrated and angry at the poor controls and interface.
Graphically this is an improvement from the other games in this series. From a gameplay standpoint, it's a giant step backwards.

A game, in essence is a mode of entertainment in which humanity has made and evolved. Today's forms of it vary highly compared to it's base. This game, being simple, exercises the root of that idea.
If you love the idea of diving into a setting and connecting puzzle pieces that do not have to be put together then this could be for you.
I for one, love immersing myself into environments and learning the setting through the subtleties. As a graveyard simulation this game does exactly that. And if you have an imagination that has not stagnanted, you can get even more out of this.
A key aspect about this game is that there are no objectives. No orders, missions or timelines that must be met. That open flow allows one to play the game at their own pace. You literally play as yourself in that sense, going wherever your fingers want to travel and reading whichever tombstones you feel like reading. There's going to be times where you may skip a grave or times where you will read every single one and you won't get rewarded or penalzied for either or. There's a certain beauty to that.
Anywho, if you are looking for something more objective and mission based to keep your attention focused this game will not be for you. But if you would like a break from the standard, this will be a pleasurable experience.

I came in and played Welcome to Boon Hill having no idea what I should expect. Would I laugh? Would I cry? Would there be hidden zombies I have to fight? While those concepts were few and far between I came to the realization that the game is much more than what people expect from a “typical” game experience. It’s not meant to apprise to tell any set story but aims to set in motion for the user to create their own experience. To define their own meanings.
At face value, Boon Hill can seem as if it’s a modest graveyard simulator but in actuality the graveyard is as disparate as it is eerie. The music is fantastic. It absolutely gives an otherworldly feel that sends chills down your spine as you interact within the world and its muses. Though the sound is simply an undertone to the real joy of play which is the diversity in reading the epitaphs.
From the start of the game you already know there will be plenty to explore as each epitaph you come across is far different from the previous. Some are silly such as one that was simply “This sucks I’m scared of worms.” While there can be others that hit you right into the feels such as “The sun shall rise and find your eyes filled with tears for me for I know that you love me as much as I hold love for you and with the passing of enough days the tears will dry but each time you think of me know I miss you too.” Boon Hill can definitely surprise you when you least expect it.
In the graveyard you walk and keep walking. There is no HUD, there are no map indicators, and there are no mission objectives. You venture onwards unknowingly between yourself, some NPCs, and the massive amount of dead that slumber in their graves. What I take from this is that this game is about the representation of our lives. We don’t quite know where we’re going until we cross paths with something we wish to take the time to glance upon. We meet people, see things, both ordinary and unordinary. And eventually we all come to experience the humor, pain, and intrinsic oddities of what death represents to us.
Recommended.

There's not a whole lot to this. It's not a game, it's not even a simulator -- it's more like an interactive art project someone made for SVA and then figured they could sell on Steam. The music is beautiful, haunting even, and I'd absolutely be willing to pay for the soundtrack, but that's about the only worthwhile part. It doesn't feel like the makers have ever been to a real graveyard, especially not one as old as Boon Hill is supposed to be. Graveyards that old aren't as empty as this game's setting, for one thing; 90% of the "graveyard" is empty space with a smattering of tombstones in small family clusters, even though it's supposed to date back to the 1700s at least. And we're not talking "ruins" or "stubs that are old, broken tombstones, now illegible" -- it's just EMPTY. Lots of grass, maybe a tree, but that's it. Also, it feels like they never finished this "game", since many of the gravestones can't be read -- and I'm certain that's not intentional because they AREN'T blank, they're simply not things with which you can interact in the "game." Clicking on them does nothing. Most tombstones have writing that can be read, some are blank when you click on them, but this third group? Just...not there, as far as the program is concerned. That serves no narrative purpose, there's no explanation for it, and it really just ruins the immersion.  Sort of like that Spanish tombstone with the name of "Inygo Montoya" on it. Har har. Also, the Spanish tombstones? Yeah, they're pretty clearly just English things someone ran through Google translate and then incorrectly typed out. I wouldn't make fun of "stupid Americans [who] can't read [Spanish tombstones]" (that's the translation for one of them) when you can't even manage basic Spanish spelling, grammar and vocabulary. "Mayora" =/= "Mayoria." I assume the same would be the case for the ones in Cyrillic script. I'm not really sure why they felt this needed to be Kickstarted, but good on them for being entrepreneurs, I suppose.

FULL DISCLOSURE: I was one of the Kickstarter backers for this game.
Remember visiting a town in a JRPG and reading the tombstones in the graveyard? If you liked doing that and thought it would make a great standalone experience, Boon Hill might be for you.
First off, Boon Hill isn't so much a "game" as it is a narrative-based art experience. If you're expecting any action or a straightforward story, you'll be disappointed.
The story of Boon Hill is really several individual stories written as epitaphs,  some fantastic, some mundane, some comical. As you travel across the surprisingly large cemetary, stories begin to unwind. Like The Spoon River Anthology which was the inspiration for this game, some of the deceased knew one another in life as friends, relatives. lovers and enemies.
The idea for the game is intriguing, the graphics look like they were ripped from a Super Nintendo game. It can be fun trying to tie various "residents" of Boon Hill together. This has the makings of an enjoyable, if not a bit weird experience.
Unfortunately, the game is not without problems. First, it does not appear to support a gamepad. I had to make a profile with JoyToKey to use an XB360 controller (my control device of choice for most games) with Boon Hill. Also, there are some graphical glitches that detract from an immersive experience. Finally, the controls, even with a keyboard ar a bit janky and laggy. You think you're moving your character one way, but he/she ends up moving a different way. I hope that the devs will tighten up the graphical glitches and controls.
Still, the game is compelling. It's only USD 5 and I know I've wasted more on coffee, booze, and junk food many a time. If the idea of wandering a virtual graveyard and reading tombstones at all appeals to you, I think the game is worth you time and money.

I think this is one of the best games there is... as a simultor it's an excellent change of pace from 'Call of Duty' type games and with the Workshop and several mods online it can be customised to suit almost any style. This is a fairly long review so if you want the quick version - yes, it's a great game and as long as you've a good computer that can handle it, I'd say it's a worthwhile buy. And, if you want a more detailed review, here you go;
Pros:
1. Flexibilty
This is the best thing about this game. With the mods on the Workshop and on Armaholic -
- there's very little you can't achieve. While the BLUFOR and OPFOR forces are generic NATO and Soviet Bloc forces based on the American/British and Russian/Chinese armies, you can get practically any nation you want in the game, along with a host of fictional armed forces. Mods also increase the gameplay capability by adding military might not avaliable with the vanillia - aircraft carriers, cruisers, nuclear SCUD launchers, more in-depth air and artillery support etc.
2. Realism
Some people might list that as a downside, and if you're among them I would refer you to my first point. Mods can enable you to have a more relaxed experience, but Arma 3 as a vanillia game is a military simultor more than a shoot-em-up game. From a realistic aiming system to your charcter going gradually deaf from gunshots if you have no hearing protection, this game really is the best widely avaliable virtual battlefield. And, if even that isn't enough, might I suggest ACE 3 (Advanced Combat Enviroment 3) -
- the self-styled 'realism mod' for and already ultra-realistic game.
3. Editor
I know this kind of ties into my first point, but bear with me. The skill required to use the inbuilt Eden editor is miminal, and while creating more complex missions does require a base knowledge of script, you can see a lot of help online and regardless of ability you will be able to put a mission together with ease. The editor is excellent and gives you complete access to all the various maps and whatever mods you may have downloaded.
4. Community
I speak on this topic with limited experince, not having played much online. However, the online community have proved indespensible to my own editing endeavours, and I am eternally grateful to a number of modders who have created excellent representations of real-life utilities and militaries. From my limited onine play, it's a great game for multiplayer but you'll need a good system and connection or lag with be your undoing.
Cons:
1. System Requirements
It's a complex and large game, and this is an unfortunate but unavoidable by-product. You will need a powerful computer to play either online or at high quality settings. If you get certain mods they will be an additonal drain on your resources and the very large maps can test even powerful systems.
2. DLC
I do hesitate to put this in here, and yes, I've bought all the DLC. They are regarded with mixed feeling by many, and while I do think they're good and well put together, I have put them in here because I personally think they're overpriced. The full Apex edition is nearly €60, which I think is a bit expenisive considering the base game is only €35.
I know this list seems a bit biased, but aside from system requirements and the expensive DLC I honestly don't think there's anything objectively wrong with this game. Most of the other complaints I've heard about it boil down to individual preference, not any universal problem that Bohemia can correct. I'd really reccommend this game, no matter what type of military game you like there's something here for you.

Rome Total War was in many ways the best that the Total War series had to offer, it was the game that took a giant leap forward and set the standard that it's own developers have yet to break. Despite game breaking bugs and broken promises about modding support Rome Total War still manages to give you a grand experience as you grow your empire towards total domination.

For those who have never played a Total War game it has two distinct elements to it, the first is the campaign map, this is an overview map where you build your cities, train units, send diplomats and assassins to your enemies and friends and move your armies around in a turn based grand strategy style and while it has nowhere near the dept of a true grand strategy game it does the job well enough that you forgive it, especially once you start to touch upon the second, and the most important, major aspect of a Total War game, the battles.

When two armies meet on the campaign map you are taken out of the turn based strategy and thrown right smack in the middle of a real time strategy battle with hundreds or perhaps even thousands of soldiers ready to fight and die. You move your soldiers around in squads of archers, swordsmen, cavalry, etc. Each faction has a semi-unique list of units they can employ, from the various types of Roman Legionaries to the Carthaginian War Elephants to the hilariously historically inaccurate flaming pigs. Each unit has it's own skills and abilities and while there is some level of rock -> paper -> scissors involved, the majority comes down to tactics, sure Spearmen beats cavalry, unless the cavalry happens to be charging them from behind.
The game is pretty too, with a good amount of detail considering the scope of the battles, the soundtrack fits almost perfectly with the mood of the game and sounds of battle are utterly satisfying. Even the load screen are great, each one featuring a different quote from a period persona although a lot of mistakes were made by whoever typed in those quotes.
It is not all roses however, Rome has a number of problems too the first and foremost of which being the same one that continues to plague Total War games to this day. The AI is completely and utterly inept. Whether it is trying to assemble an army by sending individual units walking through your territory one by one, letting you eliminate them piecemeal or displaying it's rather uncanny ability to form a perfect battle line and then break it in half just before engagement letting you flank the enemy at will you can't help but feel that this is somehow below the standards of the rest of the game and in fact modders have proven that making the AI not suicide every battle is indeed possible.
In addition to that rather large issue there is a number of smaller ones, the campaign map is incredibly shallow and while the movement style is a big leap up from Medieval it still feels very arcadey. The squalor bug, or feature, as the developers would call it, whereby all cities automatically revolt if they grow to a certain population size. The lack of full scale modding, although Rome features a bunch of great mods there are certain things you are simply not allowed to do, such as adding more factions to the game. And despite the developers saying it's possible and banning people from their forums who says otherwise, it really isn't possible.
Also the game throws any sense of historical accuracy out the window, from the equipment to the map to the very factions very few things in the game represent the time period accurately, this is something that will bother some people while others will ignore it. For me it only becomes annoying when people take their knowledge from Rome and try to apply it elsewhere.
All in all, Rome Total War is a great game, it set the standard for all Total War Games to come and despite a number of annoying bugs and problems it still remains a great game to this day.

----Call of Duty WWII Review----
(No this is not a pay to win game like EA's Battlefront 2)
They said that this game goes back the original CallofDuty game's routes. They said that it will refresh the COD player with a more classic experience. I am here to tell you that they were right.
-The game gives the player a solid campaign with likeable characters and good mechanics.
-The multiplayer is what really takes the cake. (Cake not included) With pretty diverse maps, solid gamemodes, and the amazing division system, the multiplayer is one of the most amazing experiences that I've had with COD.
----MP Divisions----
•Infantry- Perhaps the most simple of the bunch. You unlock different kinds of rifles like the classic M-1 Garand and assault rifles. Every weapon has a bayonet.
•Airborne- With the airborne division, you get different types of SMGs. An advantage you get is more mobility.
•Armor- You get the heavy weapons with the armor class such as the MGs. With this class you have a lot of resistance.
•Mountain- The good old Sniper class. If you want stealth and more of a challenge, then this is for you.
•Expeditionary- This class is onlyy comprised of shotguns. Go for this for more close up destruction.
-----8/10-----

Having played ALL LEGO games up to date, we finally bought LEGO Jurassic World.
The difference was that this time, we moved to Steam, leaving back our old XBox 360 console.
The game is great. Read other people reviews about it.
This review is regarding the game on an unsupported OSX platform.
As besides the TV we have a mac-mini, we tried to use it, and having it an unsupported Intel HD 3000 Graphic Card we had to manually test each option within the configuration file to make it work.
The result is right here:
Or fully described below:
Hello,
I have been able to run the game with an unsupported mac mini (OSX) with an Intel HD3000 Graphic Card.
Maybe all people with unsupported Intel HD3000 (even on PC) will beneffit from this solution:
You shoud open your preferences folder through the game support home screen or go to:
On OSX:
/Library/Application Support/Feral Interactive/LEGO Jurassic World/
On PC, the folder seems to be:
Appdata > Roaming > Warner Bros Interactive Entertainment > LEGO Jurassic World
There, you'll find a PCCONFIG.txt file, which I modified to achieve get rid of the crashes.
As I disabled all hardware acceleration, the game is very very slow to load (even with a SSD Drive, so I could not imagine how would it be with a SATA drive...).
Also, the MotionBlurEnabled and such solution did not work for me.

It's not difficult to imagine that the designers of Gratuitous Space Battles are huge fans of the wargame/boardgame Star Fleet Battles. At a glance, these games seem to share many similarities.
But GSB simulates a higher command level than SFB. In SFB, you're a captain of a single starship, participating in fleet skirmishes as part of a larger team. You coordinate your efforts, but each captain enjoys his own successes, and brings glory and honor to his team through personal victories or by dying honorably. In GSB, you're tasked with assembling a fleet and deploying it for scenario combat, and then... sitting around and watching the battle.
To me, this is not particularly rewarding, or entertaining. It's hard not to just crank up the speed to the fastest setting and learn the outcome of each battle.
I quickly lost interest after the tutorial, and went straight to the manual to confirm that you get no control of ships. It's true. Not even in online play. This seems like a missed opportunity to me.

Gratuitous Space Battles is an Tower defense game. It might not look like it but that's the core gameplay mechanic. You buy and equip your ships, place them and hit the start button.
Now while the idea behind Gratuitous Space Battles is very intriguing it is not very well executed. Balanced fleets and balanced ships will lose out to specialized freaks of nature every time. You will quickly learn that the most efficient fleet composition is tanks, ships with no engines, no weapons, no shields, no systems other than armor, and damagers, ships with no engines,  no armor, no shields, no systems other than weapons. This min maxing system really hurts your enjoyment as every battle will quickly become the same grind.
The attempt to add on a campaign mode was well intentioned but unfortunately not very well thought though.
This is one of those games that you will enjoy up until the point where you figure out how the game works. Good idea, poor execution.

For those who have used any tracker software previously will find alot to like and familiarity here. The interface takes some time to get used to though, even if it looks a tad simple. It's recommended to view some of Rytmik's tutorial videos on Youtube to get the general gist.
Once you've gotten the interface down, and of course the shortcuts (which requires you to take a peek in the included manual), you can start getting into serious chiptune territory. There are a wide selection of both pre-made tunes and sound effects and the options to modify how they sound are pretty incredible - even daunting and flabbergasting!
If you feel like you don't want to make something yourself, there's thankfully also support for connecting to Rytmik's cloud and listen to what others have made. Cave Story in Chiptune format just sounds -right.
To point on negatives, there's the fact that most of what you make here is chiptune-ish. I have not seen any option to import own tunes or sound sets to vary what one make. I also miss a keyboard shortcut for removing a block instead of dragging it out of the composition. The export functionality is also a bit lacking, as it only come in .WAV-format, but lets you export up to 60 minutes of your very best (or worst) creations. One can wonder why there isn't options for exporting straight to .mp3, .it, .xm or .mod an option here? Additionally, there is no zooming in or out on the track, something that's very useful when your tune get long. Instead you have to scroll it left and right.
In other words, don't expect Rytmik to be your best pal for making feature long tracks, the interface just isn't tailored well enough for it.
I'd suggest picking Rytmik Ultimate up on sale and having a go at some of the tutorial videos and sample soundsets already provided with the software. It's pretty quick to make something that sounds half-okay without much trouble using the long list of pre-made sound snippets, and should prepare you for the step into Chiptune Country.

If you want a surprisingly engrossing 3D puzzle that requires attention to a lot of moving parts, this game is for you. If you want a detailed ATC sim, this won't fit the bill.
Airport Madness 3D has relatively simplistic gameplay -- watch for incoming planes, adjust their speed and approach runways to space them out sufficiently, and then make sure that planes at the gate are directed to the runway for takeoff. The challenge comes in synchronizing all these elements and judging various factors -- the time it takes a plane to lineup, accelerate, and clear the runway, for instance -- in order to ensure smooth operation. It sounds simple, but in practice, you can lose yourself in the game and you get a little feeling of accomplishment once you have a well-oiled machine.
One of the most unique aspects of a game at this price point is the continual updates and improvement the devveloper has made to the game first release. This has included new maps, new aircraft, new interface elements, and even tweaks to physics modeling and plane instructions based on player feedback.
As stated above, if you want a simple but surprisingly engrossing puzzle game with high replay value to help you kill an hour or so and then check out easily, this will hit the spot.

There - I had to get THAT out of the way because of the staggering number of negative reviews panning it for not being a serious ATC simulation.  If you're after a serious air traffic controller game, then move along because there is nothing for you to see here.  But for everyone else who just wants a way to release their inner insanity, this is a CASUAL game - recognisable instantly to anyone already familiar with BigFatSimulations' more casual games and especially the original (2D) Airport Madness game.  For anyone who wants a game that doesn't take itself too seriously, it is brilliant!
Gameplay is as simple as clicking on a plane and choosing one of 2-3 minimal options.  There is nothing advanced about it, and no ATC-game skills or knowledge are required.
Within about 5 minutes of starting this game, you will undoubtedly have at least three to five planes on (and off) the runway at any one moment.  Incoming planes ignore the wreckage of the previous crash you caused, while departing planes are dispatched nose-to-tail with no separation whatsoever (so yeah, DON'T fly with me).  It's ludicrous and delightfully silly, with equally-silly tweets such as: "A piece of plane has just flown past my window - #MAYDAY!" popping up on screen.  Planes arrive thicker and faster while you have no chance of controlling the rush.  Nobody seemed to mind as one plane landed over the splintering wreckage of my last catastrophe, and neither did it mind that it had another plane lining up for take-off right under its belly.  THIS is how we solve the world's crowded skies, people!
The graphics are fairly basic but they do the job.  For a game on such budget graphics, it is a pleasant surprise to find a number of flexible 3D camera views - including an in-cockpit camera for players wishing to see the mayhem they're causing first hand.  The only small gripe I have is that it can sometimes be difficult to click on the plane I actually want when on the airport apron (usually this is when the plane isn't the foremost plane in view) but other than that it's a splendid casual game and even more fun than the Airport Madness top-down game that came before it.

Absolute Drift is a top-down physics-based 'drifting simulator', developed by Dune Casu and Funselektor Labs, and runs on the Unity engine.
The game focuses primarily on the concept of 'drifting', the motor racing art of sliding a car sideways through a series of turns without traction, all while keeping the car under control and preventing it from spinning out or crashing into walls.
In Absolute Drift, the physics are more tuned to be very heavily realistic instead of being arcade-styled, meaning that instead of a simple 'tap to drift' mechanic often seen in other racing games such as Burnout or DiRT, the player must get to grips with how each car in the game handles, in terms of weight, steering, braking, speed and manoeuverbility, with each factor extremely fine-tuned to perfection. I can only imagine just how long it took for the devs to get the physics for each car right.
Because of said physics, a lot of players who play more arcade-based racing games may find it very difficult to get to grips with the game at first. This included me, as I play a lot of the previous games I mentioned. I did rage (quit) a fair bit and feel bad because I wasn't able to master the way the game feels at first, but after some perserverance and a few hours of gameplay, the physics finally clicked with me. Some other players may take more time to get used to it than it took me, but let's be honest, all the drifting footage you see on the TV and on the Internet only
drifting look easy.
The game features a wide variety of tracks and courses to test one's drifting prowess on, ranging from drifting circuits where you have 3 laps to rack up as high a score as you can, to mountain drifting (A to B courses), to Driftkhana arenas and midnight mountain drifting. Each track also has a selection of objectives the player can attempt to complete, from scoring a minimum amount of points, to holding a drift for a certain amount of time, to reaching a high enough score multiplier by chaining drifts together. Tying all these tracks together is a free-roam area, split up into a number of worlds, with each world containing a certain number of tracks and free-roam missions the player must complete to unlock the next world.
The game's graphics are presented in a very minimalistic fashion, with enviromments all painted in white, and unique objects such as smashable boxes and tyre walls painted in red or black (very reminiscent of Mirror's Edge), and neon signs in blue or yellow. These graphics work splendidly with the feel of the game, but make sure you've got your monitor brightness and gamma correction configured, otherwise you'll have a very hard time distinguishing a track's corners from the edges of the track.
The game's soundtrack is also truly sublime, featuring drum & bass and future beats from C41 and Nyte, a bunch of artists who aren't as well known as they deserve to be.
My only real complaint with the game is that records aren't saved locally, meaning you can smash your own high score on a track by a massive margin, but it gets wiped the moment you quit the course because there's no internet available for the game to be able to upload and save your records on the leaderboards.

Okay, all Assassin's Creeds have the same basic idea, but they are different usually. But, AC: Brotherhood and AC II are VERY similar in many respects, and since I haven't played them for awhile, I am literally copy-pasting the same review to both of them because I can't remember all the little things that are different, because really, they are very similar. So here we go:
I love the Assassin's Creed series. I played the first AC about seven years ago, and I played it nonstop. The basic idea of AC is that you are and assassin, and you have a city as your assassination-playground, usually multiple locations. You start the game as Desmond, a guy who uses a machine called the Animus to shoot back in time to his ancestors' history. This is accomplished from the Animus being able to use his mind as a channel for those ancestors' memories.
Then, you are his ancestor, an assassin. and you have to kill things. The story is usually deep and intriguing, and it brings you along, and the gameplay of it is awesome too. And then you can just do random things as sidequests, usually pickpocketing, or another assassination target, stuff like that.
You have two profiles: Low profile, where you don't draw attention, and just push past people, or walk. Then High profile, by holding right trigger, where then you start running and you can parkour, fight, shove through people, and sprint.
The combat is fun, and the sneaky-assassinating is satisfying. There's some flaws, but Brotherhood and AC II are probably the best out of this series. Would recommend anybody to try.

Never have I seen a game fall so far down than H1Z1. This game used to be fun, amazingly fun infact. The hit reg was bearable, the guns felt great and the lighting was great. H1Z1 was the #1 battle royale game for quite sometime.
This games worst enemy is its own developers, Daybreak games have ruined what this great game once was. With the additon of the combat update, the gun play and recoil was drasitcally changed for its core guns which left a lot of veteran players infuriated. To give a clear analogy to how bad this recoil change was:
Counter Strike (starting from 1.6) has had a VERY similar if not the exact same recoil pattern for the AK-47 for more than a decade and a half. All the core players have got this on lock giving the game a much higher skill gap. Imagine if Valve suddenly decided to completely change the AK-47 spray pattern with no logical reasoning? The outrage would be immense.
Daybreak are trying to re invent this game into something that it shouldnt be. It should be what the players want not what the developers want. The players have been screaming to the devs to revert back to the build of a previous season where the game was at its peak, but they dont listen. They say they wont do it and they dont provide any logical reasoning.
Now the gunplay is horrid, shotgun is broken, ENAS has plauged the play style and there is little to no skill gap in the game.
I really do want this game to prosper and go back to that beautiful game that it once was, but I sadly and firmly believe that it wont ever get close to what it once was purely because of the developers. If you want proof as to why I believe this, have a look at the Steam Charts and the H1Z1 Subreddit.
PUBG did not kill H1Z1, Fortnite did not kill H1Z1, the players did not kill H1Z1.
And it will never be great again.

It's written in Unity and that has certain effects, like for example if you move the window while your track is playing it will stutter until you stop moving the window.
I went into this knowing it was obviously way more limited than a full DAW and was prepared to accept that: It is after all a lot cheaper. I did expect more functionality than there was though.
Basically you have a load of samples. There are quite a lot but you can't add your own. You have one instrument type which lets you draw a waveform with 24 bars and you can adjust the volume envelope and a few other things for all instruments.
In terms of effects though there is only a delay. I expected there would be the usual flanger, phaser, reverb, filter with resonance and so on, but there isn't. Instead some of the instruments have effects on them already so you just have to use those if you want an effect and then you can't tweak it or vary it as the track plays of course. You can tweak the waveform of the drawable instrument as the track plays, in a basic way, by automating the height of each bar, but it's hard to get meaningful results.

Pros:
1. Controls are tight and responsive. It's very easy to pick up and play, and precise movement is a breeze.
2. The 8-bit-style artwork is fantastic. It keeps mostly with the look of NES games like Mega Man and Castlevania, but it doesn't limit itself to that. Think Mega Man 9 or 10, but taking it a bit farther with a bit more detail and parallax scrolling.
3. Plenty of level variety. Things never get monotonous.
4. Lots of subweapons to take advantage of, meaning multiple ways to tackle most obstacles, leading to plenty of replay value.
5. Difficulty done right. This game is hard as hell, but it is always fair.
6. If you know the code for it, the hidden Iron Man challenge is incredibly fun.
Cons: (most of these are nitpicks)
1. Some subweapons aren't all that useful in my opinion. I never use the Alchemy Coin or Chaos Sphere.
2. New Game+ isn't all that interesting.
3. Flare Wand is awesome, but a little overpowered.
4. Propeller Knight's stage is too hard for my tastes. WAY too hard. I died 186 times in my first playthrough, and I swear half of them were in that stage alone.
5. This isn't a problem in my opinion, but some may be turned off by how much this game derives itself from other games. This game does bank on nostalgia to a degree.
Overall:
This is the best game I have played in recent years. It is easily in my favorite games of all time, up there with Resident Evil 4, Super Metroid, and Crash Bandicoot 2. If you like old-school platformers and are looking for a challenge, this will be right up your alley. Plus, there is free DLC on the way, so it's about to get even more amazing content.

Saints Row: The Third is where the franchise really came into it's own. Volition probably recognized that they were fighting a losing battle pitting their more serious Saints Row titles (1 and 2) against the likes of Rockstar with their Grand Theft Auto series, and decided to take a more outlandish approach. It paid off for them. Saints Row: The Third takes the Saints out of Stillwater and dumps them into Steelport, home to it's own collection of gangs that hate The Third Street Saints.
From the get-go you know the game is dropping the gloves and is ready to deliver the most ridiculous, tongue-in-cheek sandbox experience fans of the series have seen up to this point. Throughout the game you'll collect crates full of "collectors edition" blow-up sex dolls, bludgeon folks with giant, floppy, purple♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bats also known as "The Penetrator", and compete on a gameshow where you fight for survival, killing people dressed as furries, beer bottles, and soda cans as you make your way to the finish line.
Character customization is more extensive than games passed, now allowing you to even adjust the size of your...assets, aptly referred to as your character's "sex appeal". You can give your male character a females voice, or vice versa, or give them a zombies voice, that just mumbles slurred nonsense. My handsome well-kept character, stammering through cinematics using zombie dialect was enough to make me laugh so hard it brought tears to my eyes. The non-zombie voice acting is superb as well, with Troy Baker lending his voice as one of the two available male voices.
The controls (both driving and on foot) are tight and intuitive, keeping everyone from seasoned Saints Row veterans to first time players from feeling overwhelmed.
The plot for Saints Row: The Third throws you plenty of curve balls, and has enough bizarre missions and quests to keep you entertained. Along with scouring the city for the blow-up dolls I mentioned earlier, you can collect pallets full of drug money, invest in property (which pays dividends), and participate in a plethora of activites that'll keep you entertained for hours, insurance fraud being one of my personal favorites. After beating SR3 several times on consoles I wanted to give it a go on PC a few years later and it's still everything I remember.
This third installment goes crazy enough for people to have some lighthearted fun but holds on to some of the things that long-time Saints Row fans will appreciate. My favorite installment in the Saints Row franchise!

TL;DR: There are multiple, random causes for online profile corruption, and after that the game won't play. You can't fix it, you can't get a new profile, and support is not good about resetting it.
I'm totally dissatisfied, my friends are too. I bought the game together with 4 friends, and hours after we all had the tremendous download, online play was down. The servers were down for over a day during the DoubleXP Thanksgiving weekend. We played about 35 public matches before the game broke and none of could play online anymore. There was a glitch in public online play, and I assume that this effected at least 10 people, but I know it broke the game completely for the five of us.
We joined a match and something was obviously glitched -- we were in third-person view, which never happens during a match, and there were white backpacks littered all over the ground, which we inevitably picked up and could throw, but everyone was confused and then the match -- which probably lasted 90 seconds -- disconnected and our profiles were corrupted.
I now had over 2 billion unlock tokens and prestige level over 150 million and the menu was stuck on the "Find Match" screen. I uninstalled and reinstalled the game -- that didn't fix it. Before this incident, the game played flawlessly on all 5 of our PC's. Now the game is broken on all 5 of our machines with the same symptoms.
We all talked to Activision support, and there was nothing the support reps we were able to contact could do. Disclaimer: I will continue to revise this review as I play more, because I do enjoy the game.
Let me preface this by saying that I think the gameplay elements of this game are unmatched by any fishing game that has ever been made. This is without a doubt, as the game says on the loading screen, the best fishing simulator ever. I have no disagreements with that. Fishing planet is immersive, pretty, exciting, and relaxing all in one. The fishing experience is the way it should be in every fishing game.
There are a plethora of rods, lines, reels, etc. Some of them make a real difference and others are purely cosmetic. Learning how to catch new fish is a challenge sometimes, as you figure out the right bait, drag setting, line, etc. Everything about it feels like real fishing.
However, there are some things which, while true in real life about fishing, don't make for a great experience in a video game.
The game is severely gated by the travel fees and staying fees for going places other than the free Lone Star Lake in Texas. It is EXTREMELY hard to cover the cost of the trip while on the trip, LET ALONE turn a profit.
So, the way the game plays out for newcomers for a VERY long time is like this...
1) you grind XP and cash on really small boring fish in Lone Star Lake just to save up enough to make a couple day trip somewhere to fish.
2) You go there and catch awesome fish but your net is too small so you can't make a profit or even COVER the charge of the trip.
3) You're now broke and can only fish at Lone Star Lake.
4) Because the catchable fish in Lone Star are for newbies, when that's the only place you can go back to to fish, the amout of time it takes to save up again is EXTREMELY long.
As you can see this makes for a very frustrating game experience. Now with a premium accout you can make this process easier, but of course that costs real world money. So in reality, to get the game play experience this game SHOULD have, you have to pay real money and it doesn't seem like a "free game" anymore.
I'm going to keep playing this game to see if I'm doing something wrong and find out the methods which make this easier, but as of right now I don't really see how this could play out any different.

It's so close to being a good game that I wish I could give it a neutral rating instead of a Good or bad rating.
The Good: The graphics and physics of the game are well done. The environments look and sound really good, lots of realism and depth. When you catch and reel in a fish it seems like one of the more realistic games I've played. There are a number of places you can fish and a number of species to fish for making it very diverse in the long run for someone that has reached the max level and unlocked / bought all the gear available to them.
The Bad:  Your ability to enjoy this game is completely dependant upon your willingness to spend REAL money, and how much you're willing to spend. It's also dependant upon you being able to grind. If all you did was play the free version of the game, it's not enjoyable. It's boring, too much of a grind to ever really be fun. You waste too much in-game currency traveling back and forth between bodies of water as you level up. It also limits the amount of in-game cash you can earn by the size of your stringer, which is expensive to upgrade so it's a catch-22 getting out of low level, boring areas unless you open your REAL wallet and spend REAL money on one or all of the 3 things this game pretty much forces you buy.
In game you have 2 currencies: A cash currency and a baitcoin currency. Cash is spent on average gear, baitcoins are spent on high-end gear. Both of the in-game currencies can be farmed by grinding (spending hours fishing while knowing where to fish, what to fish for, and what to fish with), OR you can skip the grind and just use real, hard-earned money to buy the currencies. The cash is cheaper than the baitcoins. Of course, this is how all free-to-play games make their money. For you to enjoy the game at the highest level you'll be spending a fair amount of REAL money on a regular basis. The game baits you into spending money on yet another near-necessity if you plan on playing a lot: A Premium Account!  A premium account allows you to grind through levels (40 of them) at a 50% increased rate over someone that has a regular account. Lets not forget that you also  make in-game cash about 50% quicker. The premium account monthly subscription is $14.99 per month, the cost of a WoW subscription. And then if you plan on bouncing back and forth between lakes fishing for "fun" fish and buying "good" gear you're going to be burning a hole in your real wallet paying for in-game currencies to make that happen. Why? Because the game charges you THOUSANDS of in-game dollars to travel to a particular body of water, but you cannot recover the thousands you spent in a single trip. So if you leave the lake, with a stringer of, say, $1,000 worth of fish, you have essentially lost money fishing there. How do you recover that money? By fishing the starter lake, which is little more than a pond, for HOURS until you've made enough to afford another trip! Or, <suprise suprise> You can just use your credit card to buy some cash to get out of the little pond in Texas and do some real fishing. Imagine that!  PAY TO WIN ladies and gentlemen. Those who pay to play will leave the average player in the dust and enjoy fishing more bodies of water for more species and sizes of fish. Its just that simple.
SERVER DISCONNECTS AND CLIENT FREEZES
I just had a server disconnect while reeling in maybe the biggest fish I have ever caught.  In 6 hours of playing I've had more than a few server disconnects and client freezes. It's not my computer. I have a custom gaming PC that I keep updated and CLEAN! I have a 300 Mbps connection, a Nighthawk router, and my NIC is a PCI-E Wireless AC1900 card with 3 high-gain antenna. In almost every game I play my ping is lower than just about everyone I play with and it's rock-solid steady.
How this could be better: Stop charging people in-game currency to travel back and forth between bodies of water! I understand, and even like, spending in-game currency on gear. That makes sense to me. But this is a video game. It shouldn't feel like WORK to have to grind out money just so you can go fish where you want to fish.  And also: Fix the server instability issues.

still one of my favorite games ever! i played this for years when games for windows live was still around, easily had hundreds of hours into it then, plus god knows how much time i've played on console, and now again on this version through steam.
let's talk about a few things.
The AI is dumb, which is both good and bad. sometimes the AI for both the enemies and your ally just do some dumb♥♥♥♥♥♥ but overall, the predicability makes it playable in my opinion. zombies typically can be predicted and you can get a nice pattern going for kills that requires very little ammo usage (if you choose to be stingy which i always am), but for as predictable as they are, you will still get hit sometimes. you still need to pay attention. this makes the game neither easy nor hard, but rather i feel gives you something to pit yourself against. can i beat the entire horde without making a mistake? or will one of those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s manage to hit me and screw up my groove?
Sheva loves to waste bullets, early game it's hard to justify giving her ammo, for most people at least, then again, you can use this to your advantage and if you play right, it really isn't an issue. When you have her in cover mode, she will pull out a handgun (weak weapon) stay close to you, and take few shots (she pretty much just watches your back). when you put her into attack mode, she pulls out a bigger weapon (pretty much anything but a handgun) and goes out actively killing zombies and grabbing items. this frustrates many as she is not ammo efficient and she gets into trouble frequently, however giving Sheva a sniper and a handgun makes her quite nice IMO. give her too many different weapons and she's constantly switching and not getting anything done, give her one "good" weapon and a handgun and you know exactly what she will do based on the command you give her. also, if you play right, ammo is never really a concern. in fact i generally save a few thousand rounds of various ammo through my first playthrough while keeping sheva well supplied most times. (hint: don't give her machine guns ever, and if you feel she's blowing a certain ammo type too much, just hold the extra ammo on yourself and give it to her only when you want her using that weapon/ let her scavenge more on her own)
this game is quite playable single-player, but it truly shines with a friend. My best friend and I have sunk hundreds of hours into this game together and it was great fun the whole time. you can give each other ammo or health items, but you can't trade guns, so it encourages you to either play through twice so both people can grab each weapon from each level, or else one person needs to buy that weapon from the shop. also on higher difficulties, it's a bit rough with an AI partner (though still not impossible if you do it right)
the story was ok, honestly after 8 years it seems a bit lackluster now lol, but at the time it came out i remember connecting dots in the Resident Evil plot and being excited.
if you're looking for survival horror with a spooky atmosphere and lots of tension, this won't do much for you, but what it will do is give you an awesome action shooter zombie experience, and if you've got a friend willing to go along for the ride, it will be an absolute blast.

Tcheco in the Castle of Lucio. I found this while looking for cheap joke games to gift my friend for her 14th birthday. This was the cheapest I found. She declined two times. Out of spite I bought it for myself.
I was shocked when I found out it's really good. For just one buck, I expected something very low quality and memey. Tcheco may be a bit of the latter, but it's very high quality. The difficulty reminds me of old NES games, especially since there's no saving. There is a code to get extra lives (which again reminds me of those old NES games, like the Contra code), but even with it I still haven't beat this game. After a lot of tries, you can reliably get past the first stages without taking any damage, but the later stages are still very challenging, like the floating baby ???? thing. Still take at least 5 hits there. Another positive factor is the simplicity. Three buttons only. No weird mechanics (an argument could be made for the skateboard, but it gives you time to adapt). All of these things shape Tcheco into a perfect game in my opinion.
Overall, Tcheco was a pleasant surprise, and is definitely one of the best games I've ever played on Steam. If only regional barriers didn't stop me from gifting it to outside of South America, I would have bought this for all of my friends.
