If you are considering this game, take it from a guy who never considered it at all:
I played this game for roughly an hour with friends.  I want to say something about it.  First off, the graphics are not AMAZING.  The gameplay is not AMAZING.  The game has problems, but the Developer is here to address and fix the issues if they hinder the problem.  So when you see people yell, "YOU CLICKY ON THINGS AND CLICKY CLICKY DONT WORK!"  Just realize a majority of that has been fixed.
So my gameplay experience.  I run a youtube channel where we mostly drink beers and play games that look like fun and this game looked like a blast for somebody to play and the rest comment on.  What we found was a fun little game that is not what we expected.
First off, we did the continuous challenge which let's a ATC person control planes coming in, taking off, and where they need to go to unload passengers etc.  We had a guy who is a student pilot play the game while I mocked and made fun of him for his poor choices which ended up with multiple planes blowing up.  Obviously planes blowing up is not funny, but the game gives a light hearted feel to when you mess up and the explosion are fun if you have an audience judging your ability.
So where does the game lack?  I want to say that I enjoy the game, and we had a blast playing it.  I do feel that the $15 price tag may be a bit high, but after showing it to airplane enthusiasts, they said that price was well worth the admission.  So as a gamer, price is high.  If you enjoy simulators that have fun, price is right.  Second is the graphics.  The game isn't realistic, but it also doesn't claim to be.  So if you have a problem with the graphics, let's wait and see if the sequel makes it more awesome.
All in all, I feel this game is a fun little airport game.  Thing I hate the most?  Is I'm calling friends over asking if they want to try it while i drink beer and criticize them!  lol.  If you enjoy this type of thing, i strongly recommend you buy it.  If you are curious, wait for a sale, and try it out.  I promise you will have fun with it.

Shovel Knight is one of the best games ever made, period.
What makes Shovel Knight so good?
1. Music: The music in this game is absolutly stunning. Jake Kaufman did a amazing job on this sound track like his other works in games such as Shantea and Mighty Switch Force. Also Manami Matsumae, who made a lot of classic Mega Man music, made a few tracks in this game. Even if you dont like the game, it is near impossible not to love the soundtrack.
2. Level Design: Even in my favorite games, there is always a part or two that always make me wonder "Why was this made?" Luckily Shovel Knight does not suffer from this at all. Every part in this game is very well made and does not feel cheap at all. Whether you make a jump or not is all up to your skill. A few parts such as Propeller Knights stage provide the most challenge in this aspect. Those damn fans XD
3. Boss: Rarely do you see a game where every boss is heart pounding and unique. Shovel Knight again somehow preforms this very well. The Order of No Quarter, the 8 villians in the game, all have a different aspect and provide the player a challenge. Whether its the robot mech of Tinker Knight, or the phycotic fight against Plague Knight, no game has ever made boss battles so fun
4. Basic Elements: Shovel Knight as often noted, takes insperation from many NES classics such as Ducktales, Castlevania and Mega Man. Some of these things are Shovel Knights down spike ability, which alows him to bounce of enemy without taking damage, and the side weapons.
All in all every aspect of this game is near perfect. I dont care whether it is on sale on not, but this game is a MUST PLAY

One of the most unique driving games available. However, note this is not at all a racing game. There isn't any reward for finishing quickly, though some challenges are timed. This game is just about drifting around corners and doing fancy donuts. You get points for drifting a lot, or in specific places.
The controls feel great (though they may take a while to get used to). The graphics match what you see in the screenshots. There is a nice library of songs that cycle while you play, and the car engine noises are useful and pleasant.
The challenges are tough at first. It took me an hour or two to really understand what the game wanted me to do.
Some suggestions: "easy" mode makes the car slower and more stable. This actually makes much of the game harder (or at least feel harder, to me) because just about every goal in the game involves drifting. I recommend playing on medium or hard mode.
Also try out the manual shifting. It can be annoying to have to shift up and down all the time, but controlling your speed is important in this game. You don't always want to accelerate to top speed. Switching gears helps to control your speed without having perfect accuracy on the gas pedal.
I strongly recommend the game. The controls are some of the most fun driving controls I've played with in a while. While the game can be a bit rough at the start, the challenges are somewhat reasonable from there on out.

You run around a door, and close it. First you see its a dead end.  Then you realize there's nothing but 2 barells in the room. You begin to freak out and you sit there for a few seconds thinking- should I block the door or should I hide behind the barrels? you go to block the door, but you discover that the 2 barrels aren't enough to hold it back, and the door cracks open. I'm sure you already know if this is your kind of game or not, as an NES MegaMan clone. Stages are varied enough to be fun with interesting patterned boss fights at the end of each stage.
However, this is one of those games that wants you to "pick your own" difficulty level, because there is no traditional difficulty selection. The mid-stage checkpoints are all optional, and most of the health/mp upgrades as well. Personally, playing through it with using all of those, the game was far too easy, tallying up the deaths at the end most were from one specific boss fight and the bonus areas. If you get all the health upgrades as they become available, it becomes extremely hard to die due to running out of HP, most of my deaths came from bottomless pits. On top of that, some of the sub-weapons seem to give you invincibility when you use them, making them go-to weapons for every single boss fight afterward, but thats also part of your own difficulty level if you want to use it.
Having said that, the game feels great to play, the art is true to its NES style in pallet and always maintaining a 1:1 pixel ratio, with good slightly-better-than-NES music as well. I'd recommend to anyone that enjoys either MegaMan or platformers in general.

Performance wise it runs decently enough, nothing fantastic though, in my case with an AMD graphic card anything other than DX9 resulted in eventual crashes.
The music is passable, the radios are somewhat uninspired, but I can’t blame them for that much, when GTA hasn’t had a decent radio since San Andreas, and the only GTA clone that did something decent was Sleeping Dogs.
Secondary missions are the usual filler and repetitive slock, the main missions tend to be more interesting, however it has questionable moments. The worse of these is the mission where your character goes to “save” some women being sold as sex slaves from a boat, you get two options at the end of the mission: sell them back to Morning Star or give them to your underling pimp – as far as I’m concerned this just left a horrid taste in my mouth. At least the infamous torture mission in GTA V was sandwiched with an attempt of political commentary, this is isn’t, it’s just poorly handled and hands two terrible options to the player without necessity.
Killbane is by far the best villain in this game, and it’s obvious the writers understood what they had and milked him dry, which works well enough. However that is done at the expense of others like Cyrus, Sen. Hughes, Miller and Viola – all of them fairly wasted. On the positive side of this is that at least the writing avoids taking itself too seriously, which is to its benefit.
Handling is alright, cars are arcady which as far as I’m concerned is really good, but airplanes and helicopters feel rather off. And gunplay, unfortunately, is quite hollow.

Reached the 2000 hour mark so I thought I should give this game a review.
This has quite possibly been one of the most addicting games I've played, certainly not perfect but it does a lot of things right.
Team Fortress 2 is a team based shooter with a wide range of varied classes as well as weapons to go with them. Each class has a unique play style and serves a distinct role in game, ranging from classes like the Soldier, who is a good all round offense class, to the Engineer who is able to construct various buildings designed for support, offence and defence, or the Spy, who is well equipped to get behind enemy lines and take out valuable targets. All this not only offers a wide range of play styles to suit different players, but also makes the game very complex despite its simple appearance.
One question you may be asking is "why play this over other team based shooters?" well the best answer I can give is that this game has an emphasis on movement and shoot mechanics, similar to the mechanics seen in games like Quake (where this game originated from) and other "classic" style shooters. Things such as rocket jumping, air strafing and classes like the Scout are what really set this game apart from other team based shooters.
This game also features a very colourful community, ranging from a very dedicated competitive scene, all the way to players who don't take the game seriously at all. This is because the game has a lot of personality as reflected by each class and the lore it presents in various ways. This is on top of things such as taunts, cosmetics, halloween events, unique (and underrated) gamemodes, content updates and the large array of community servers and mods. There is something for just about anybody in this game.
The game is by no means perfect though. This game does lack a much needed tutorial, since a lot of players will join and have no idea what to do. There are also constant complaints about weapon and class balance as well as certain aspects of the game not being polished to an acceptable standard. Lastly this game does have a few issues with hackers, while they aren't as present in TF2 when compared to games such as CS:GO, you will be occasionally rudely interupted by such individuals.
Team Fortress 2 is a one of kind multiplayer experience that has yet to be overshadowed by any other team based shooter (despite what others claim). Best of all, it is free to play, so if you still aren't sure about this game, then you can try it without spending a single cent.

Summary: Grinding for characters is a chore, but most other aspects of the game are quite enjoyable.
PROS:
-Performance is great, graphics options allow for lots of fine-tuning
-Most guns are satisfying to use (ex: Twitch's 417)

CONS:

-Guns and gadgets are locked to characters, this limits customization and means you probably won't be 100% satisfied with any character's kit (I'm sure this is for the purpose of better game balance, but it's still annoying)
-AI killcams. Sometimes they'll just start shooting a wall for literally no reason and "just happen kill you"
-Like all competetive games, people in multiplayer live and breathe the game, expect to lose and get flamed
-Being forced to run the game from Uplay instead of Steam is still an annoying and unnecessary step

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

WARNING: This recommendation contains mild spoilers. I'll keep them to a minimum though.
I first heard about Amnesia: The Dark Descent when some of my friends were talking about it. They didn't tell much but it seemed interesting enough to have a look at it. I always had some really creepy games in my "Best games I've ever played"-list, but I had not played anything like Amnesia before.
So what is it about? Your name is Daniel and you're from London, Mayfair. That's all you know when you wake up from being unconscious. You are in a medieval-looking castle and have no idea how you got there. Nobody is around so you wander around the castle looking for answers. Eventually you find a note that is addressed to you and was written by - yourself. The information in this note is the only clue you have while wandering the castle of Brennenburg, in a desperate search for answers while trying to get away from whatever is trying to hunt you down.
Unlike many other titles that are labeled horror, Amnesia: The Dark Descent is not a hybrid type game like a horror shooter or a horror-RPG. You cannot simply blast your way through the castle using fancy weapons or magic. Daniel hasn't got any kind of weapon and - surprise - he will never find one. Still there are enemies within the castle, and they are not the ones to be reasoned with. Your only means of self-defense are running and hiding. In most situations the latter one is preferable. Dark places are great if you don't want to be seen but hiding in the dark also exposes Daniel to the horrors within his own mind. You find yourself constantly wondering if you should light the candles in a room to avoid going crazy while being at risk of being found.
Amnesia: The Dark Descent is all about immersion. There is no HUD and your two most important resources - health and sanity - aren't represented by definite numbers. You have to keep both in mind, though. The game physics highly contributes to the immersive experience. If you want to open a drawer you don't simply click it. Instead you grab it using your mouse and draw it towards you. That also makes it possible to either open doors slowly and with great care or to slam them shut.
Amnesia not your generic horror-ish game, it's the real deal. It is not about fighting your way through hordes of enemies or being the hero who saves the world. The whole game is about nothing but atmosphere. If you can appreciate that Amnesia: The Dark Descent is a definitive must-buy.

If you are a fan of Assassin’s Creed II, you are going to absolutely love this gem! If you have not played Assassin’s Creed II, I highly recommend that you start there, as Brotherhood and Revelations are direct continuations of Ubisoft’s 2009 predecessor. While Brotherhood is a sequel of a sequel, it continues to bring multiple quality elements to the table. This game is, without a doubt, my personal favourite in the series. Like the original installment, Brotherhood is an atmospheric historical fiction action-adventure sandbox. One that you will not be disappointed in.
Brotherhood follows Assassin’s Creed II nicely, and cleanly picks up where the last left off. Desmond flees the scene of the latest Templar attack, and follows his team to Monteriggioni: their new hideout. Desperate to locate the Apple of Eden, in hopes of preventing a global disaster that had been predicted to happen later on in the year, Desmond rushes back into his genetic memory.
For Ezio, it is 1499, and he still cannot explain what he had seen inside the vault. Unfortunately, he is not given much time to mull it over before the actions of the Templars push him back into action. He spends most of the game struggling to cripple the Borgia influence in the capital, and then begins the process of training other Assassin’s to aid him.
Allow me to start off this section of the review by stating that Brotherhood is a huge game, offering more content than Assassin's Creed II. There are a lot of places to explore, both above and below ground. While some players share the mindset that "more isn't always better", I am a firm believer that the fans of the beloved assassin Ezio Auditore will have a blast checking out this game... Especially taking into consideration that there is a huge pool of returning characters, including Leonardo DaVinci and Machiavelli.
There are a number of recognizable, yet staple mechanics worth mentioning, that have been recycled in Brotherhood: The original (if not improved) free-running system, eagle-vision, hidden messages, looting, buying, and investing. Furthermore, Brotherhood keeps the modernized and improved quest system from its predecessor, which permits Ezio to hire courtesans, thieves or mercenaries.
The combat aspects of Brotherhood are mostly recognizable from Assassin's Creed II. You can still cycle through your weapons, and choose whether or not you want to execute a clumbsy public chase, or a stealthy and well-planned kill. Combat aesthetics are gorgeous, and make just about any fight seem brutal and bloody. Like it's predecessor, weapons and armor can be both obtained and repaired at blacksmith shops - Each offering their own selection of kill animations.
However, there are also new aspects of combat. For instance, mounted combat is possible. While running through crowds and across rooftops is entirely possible, Brotherhood now offers the option of horseback riding through cities (once the stables have been purchased), permitting the player to jump from a horse, and straight into an assassination.
Leonardo DaVinci has a bigger role in this game, along with optional DLC. In fact, he offers stand-alone quests that require Ezio to go after his four war machines in order to lessen the Borgia's military strength. While getting to each of Leonardo's inventions might seem a bit repetitive at times, the objective following locating the machine is always exceptionally diverse. No two missions to destroy Leonardo's inventions are the same.
Finally, I  saved the best implementation for last. The Assassin's Guild. Ezio is eventually able to recruit civilians, and train them up by sending them on their own quests, to become assassins. Once they have been obtained, they can be called upon to assist Ezio in combat so long as they are not deployed on a mission. While they are extremely powerful, I thought it was a lot of fun to recruit and train them, and I guarantee that you will likely feel the same.
If I am not mistaken, the controls are entirely identical to the setup in Assassin’s Creed II. You still cannot re-arrange your buttons, though I guarantee that playing with a gamepad will be much more friendly than playing with a mouse and keyboard.
Like the previous establishments, Brotherhoods targeting remains a bit on the tricky side. You can’t ever be 100% certain that you will hit your target, but it is something that can still be worked around. However, from time to time you might still end up changing your camera angle, and inadvertently kill a civilian or something, oops!
Brotherhood offers beautiful graphics that focus heavily on its environment. Virtually every area has been polished to reflect the games atmosphere. I’ve said it a million times before, and I’ll say it again: It is really hard to nit-pick this aspect of the game, because the visuals are so fine-tuned.
Having played II, Brotherhood, and Revelations - It is my firm opinion that Brotherhood offers the best of music and voice tracks. Ubisoft continues to uphold the tradition of combining dramatic scores of music to assassinations, making the experience more enjoyable for the player. Subtitles are still an option, and a huge help when it comes to fully understanding what is being said - I encourage you to use them for your own benefit. As always, the sounds only add to the atmosphere of the game, and in the case of Brotherhood: It is extremely well done.
In my own opinion, Brotherhood has the highest replay value in the entire series. It introduces so many miscellaneous objectives, that the game never truly feels boring. While replay value is entirely dependent on the player, I am confident enough to say that any fan of Assassin’s Creed will want to play this one again.

I recently purchased Shovel Knight and it was one of the best purchases I ever made. From start to finish the game was a excellent experience. It's a 2D sidescrolling platformer that is a tribute to old-school platformers like those from the NES era. You play as Shovel Knight a knight whom uses a shovel as his weapon and can swing it to attack enemies or jump with it and bounce off of enemies using it. You select a level from the world map and then play through it acquiring checkpoints along the way. Eventually, you fight a boss at the end of the level. Once you finish all the levels you then face the final boss like any other platformer out there. This game is so amazingly good because of the great level designs. Each level plays drastically different from the others and every level is incredibly fun. Shovel Knight also is challenging and you will die a few times, but there's no nonsense like you die and have to do a ten minute level all over again. The music in the game is also nothing short of exceptional. This is one of the better game soundtracks out there and the composer deserves a congratulations along with the level designer. Overall, if you're a fan of 2D platformers you would be foolish to pass on this outstanding platformer.

Apocalypse: Party’s Over:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Up in Heavens and sitting comfortably on a soft, sparkly white cloud, G-ZUS is playing his favourite console game . . . “Fighting Angels.” He really enjoys this game but shall we say, G-ZUS is not a natural in this genre of arcade games. After missing an endless set of “Hadoken’s,” he decides to check if his popularity among humans has been increasing.  G-ZUS nearly had a heart attack when he saw the newest statistic which showed that his greatness is now at the bottom of the list. It is time to cleanse the world of these petty humans by creating his greatest game ever. . .  Apocalypse: Party’s Over! Hold on, he is not finished yet - he needs to pick up three janitors from the crowd! Oh G-ZUS, me, me, please me. Oh bugger, I missed out!
Apocalypse: Party’s Over is a 2D side scrolling Beat’em up game where you play one of three janitors selected by the all mighty G-ZUS! Each one has an interesting set of weapons, to say the least. The first one is minister Tommy-Gun who shoots fire balls with is fingers and an explosive cross (this is how I describe it) for his main attacks (light and heavy) and a special attack which involves our mighty saviour. Our second Janitor is Psycho Bobby who is really very handy with a knife and a cleaver for his main attacks, and a tornado of trowing sharp objects for his special attack, - a total freak of a character! And our last and probably the funniest character is Sticky Dicky, who fights with his Willie (quite long and hard) and a sex toy for his main attack. His special attack is something to do with his appendix, oh G-ZUS what am I writing!
The gameplay is actually fun - enemies appear from both sides of the screen and you will have to dispatch them. Some will explode due to the ferocity of Dicky’s appendix and some will leave a coin to pick up. You can use the light attack all the time but you need to have mana to use the heavy one. As you eliminate your enemies, the special bar attack will grow and as soon as you reach the other end, you will be able to use this attack. Don’t forget to kill all the pigeons within the level. If you do so, you will be rewarded with coins on the summary at the end of the level. Also, you will have to tip your greatness. You will fight interesting bosses, the likes of Monster Jackson, in a rather groovy level. I promise you, he will do his famous moves! Plenty of other fun enemies to dispatch too. If you are daring, you can test your skills in the Junk Norris Arena where you will have to eliminate a certain number of enemies before the times runs out!
You can visit the poorshop and spend your hard coins to upgrade your character weapons and purchase abilities. Each time your character levels up, you will be rewarded with lightning can which you will be able to use on your character at the end of the level to increase his attack, resistance, mana and special attack.
As you can tell above, this game is a bit crude with a lot of dark humour. If you do not mind this type of humour, you will enjoy the game.
One thing which is a bit annoying is the fact that when you hit enemies, they might go off-screen for a small amount of time and come back on the screen. It would be great if that did not happen.
In terms of graphics, the 2D graphics are fun and the animations are well done. I really like the soundtrack and the controls are responsive. I would definitely play this game with a gamepad.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Fun and addictive gameplay
-	Fun 2D graphics
-	Dark Humour
-	Three funny characters with they own specific weapons
-	Achievements and trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Enemies get kick out of the screen and come back after a short time
7.5/10

Some would call me a hardcore Airport Madness fan. They are probably right. I've poured hundreds of hours into this franchise from the PC browser days, to the mobile apps, to the standalone PC versions, and on to repurchasing and clocking hours on the other 4 titles here on Steam. The developer himself is an air traffic controller, and I've probably dealt with more digital aircraft than he's handled real planes. (Although he has a much better safety record than I do!).. So I openly admit that even as a 33 year old man, I giggled like a strange psychotic Schoolgirl when this game was announced.
So was I right to have an outburst that would have landed me in a padded cell? Oh yes I was!! Only one PC game could stop me playing Stellaris in my free time this year and Airport Madness looks like it will have done the job perfectly.. I know, I'm a filthy casual.. and a proud one at that!
So firstly, I would advise that you search for other 2 dimensional Airport Madness games on Steam and then also play this one too. Because Airport Madness 3D is not a simulation. It is a casual, fun, addictive Air Traffic Control game.. It causes my wife to ring the police and send out search parties every time I play it. That's how hooked you can become on these games.
Anyway.. Airport Madness 3D goes to an additional dimension, and unlike other gaming franchises such as Sonic the Hedgehog and a few others games that have made a transition from 2D to 3D.. this game is actually suceeds the giant leap and becomes all the better for it. The game is more difficult than before and a little slower paced in some respects. But the challenge it brings adds a new appeal to the game.
The single greatest feature for me though is to finally have the viewpoint of sitting in an ATC tower. The need to keep an eye on the ground and air radar, to search the skies for incoming aircraft to avoid collisions and judge when to push outgoing traffic is something I have been longing for. So if you do wish for an ounce of simulation somewhere in this game, that is where you'll find it. There are also sky, runway and cockpit cams. But these aren't nearly as fun as being lord of all you survey.
Good news is, if you are looking for a friendly developer who adds plenty of free content, bug squishes like he actually knows what he's doing and listens to his fanbase and community, you will find him here. So many developers neglect this basic requirement in aftersales, even if we are all rabid wolves who have tasted developer blood, and often look for more... No bloodthirst required here.
This review probably isn't helpful.. If it has been then great. I love this game, as I do it's predocessors. No I do not know the dev personally, I just apprieciate the time he finds to do this in real life, then come home and surround himself in his work until he sleeps. Not many people can do that, and it's certainly admirable. Airport Madness is the perfect mix of the real life and arcade style fun. Best of all, you will not fall asleep playing this like real ATC agents who get fired and then battered in the news like some pinata.
So if you have an interest in these types of games, aviation, or like me never knew something that seems so boring as a job could actually be so much fun, then buy this game already!

This game is based on characters and stories from Mundo Canibal, a brazilian comedy web site created in the 90's that also contains dark humor.

The game has an arena mode where you need to defeat enemies on a limited time.
The game has co-op local, but unfortunately lacks online multiplayer.
It would be nice if they release new characters and maybe new stages in the future.

This game is a parody but this doesn't mean we can't love it! The humour is immense with Apocalypse: Party's Over.
G-zus just lost his popularity and without it, he would need to close the company. This is what made him start the apocalypse on the world that we know! In the hope of ranking his company in top 5 again. Seeking to fulfill his goal, he created a team of three janitors to represent him and his cause: Minister Tommy-gun, Psycho Bobby and last but not the least, Sticky Dicky, the attraction of the squad. You can choose between them at any time between the levels. Alongside them, you will receive different abilities and atributes. You won't find the same shop items at two of them. The player will find a lot of variety to keep him playing for more. All the levels have that thing that will keep you entertained until the very end. You will find stages with different mechanics like skate-sliding, elevators levels, new foes, obstacles, traps and let's not talk about all the fun the game includes with it. While leveling you also get new combos or even powers to help you butcher your enemies.
What I can't believe is how this game is not even more popular than it actually is! This is that type of game that will let you sit on your chair and forget about your problems, even while you're having a sad day. It's a hidden gem.
- The game includes Achievements, Trading Cards and Steam Cloud.
- A friend or family member can enter the fun and play with you! Split screen action at full fun.
- If you ever had fantasies about fighting foes with your♥♥♥♥♥♥ now is your chance to achieve it! The main character has the best abilities I've ever seen in a video game.
- The graphics of the game may look a bit wierd but you'll get a lot of fun off it's back.
- You can choose between two difficulties described as 'Half-boner' and '♥♥♥♥in' Manly'.
- 3 playable characters with different and unique atributes.
- The comedy in this game is superb!
- An survival mode which will have you fight for the best score out of the leaderboard.
- The grinding, while it may be slightly negative, it will keep you close to the monitor at least 8 hours before finishing the game.
- A character customization to make your character look fashionable and fabulous.
- Unique equipments to buy from the store for for each character.
- The game is easy to get into. Funny, simplistic and easy for people who are new in the genre.
- When I first started playing Apocalypse: Party's Over, I've had some difficulties with the game. But I've contacted the developers and they've helped me go through them. If anybody has problems with the resolution, try Alt+Enter a few times, this really made miracles in my case.
- Not many options in the settings menu. You can only turn on/off the music/sound, check the controls (but they are not customisable) and change the main language of the game.
- Enemies go off the screen. And you can still attack them, especially if you've chosen the range janitor. May get a bit frustrating at times.
- The game includes only local co-op, sadly, you won't find online multiplayer in it.
- I've had some problems with the Steam Overlay.
- Sometimes you have to replay the stages several times so you can advance further.
Even though Apocalypse: Party's Over may look a bit simple, it does everything in it's power to entertain you. I can't recommend this game more for you to try it out. The gameplay within Apocalypse: Party's Over is very enjoyable and the 3 different characters provides a good amount of variety and laughs. If you like beat-em-up side scrollers, this could be the game for you, just be ready for the crude humour, don't take the game jokes too seriously, just relax and have fun playing it. Most likely it will be a funny and enjoyable experience for you.
The developers are responsive and willing to help you with any support if you have problems with the game. Developers like these really deserve our money!

Saints Row 3 is but a pale, sad shadow of Saints Row 2, which is one of my favourite games. Actually SR3 is guilty of a pretty silly sin- trying to fix something that wasn´t actually broken.
Ok, the graphics are better, but it is missing the terrific customization options, the great writing and the memorable characters of SR2. Actually they even modify the characters from SR2 in SR3- pretty much to the worst, i.e. Shaundi, who has a completely different design, personality and voice (really missing Eliza Dushku there!). I can´t understand why they didn't simply create a totally new female character.
Regarding the customization, I managed to make my character in SR2 pretty similar to myself, which was a lot of fun to me specially because of how nicely your character is integrated in all those cool cutscenes. You could also make literally thousands of things regarding the clothes. In SR3, I could only get a ripped, let´s-be-honest-too-unreal version of myself, and the clothes are way more limited and boring.
Regarding the gameplay, SR2 felt way more exciting, having more "realistic" and cinematic firefights and even katana showdowns. SR3 is, initially, more espectacular but soon it becomes obvious that that aspect of the game was also way better in SR2.
Regarding the missions, as I mentioned before not only the main story is far superior in SR2- the side missions have way more variety and are better integrated as another part of the story.
I played SR2 for 63 hours in my first playthrough and I enjoyed every second of it- I am sure I will play it again someday.
Regarding SR3, I gave it what I think was a more than fair chance (24 hours of gameplay) to prove itself- and it simply failed. I found myself getting bored as hell, comparing it more and more to SR2 and even starting to hate the stupid, not-funny-at-all "sense of humor" of SR3.
In case I didn't make myself clear, this is my advise: Just don´t waste your time with SR3 and enjoy SR2.

Ok! Assassins Creed Brotherhood review!
This game is the second of 3 in following the story of Ezio Auditore. It's a few years after AC2, and so there's a few of the same characters and a bunch of new ones. There's even a few flashback missions that take place in Firenze. I was in it for the story for the most part, so I tried to beat the story missions as in order as possible. The combat is pretty much identical to AC2 but with much cleaner mechanics. I didn't play around with the weapons much and mostly just stuck with the hidden blades. The combos are always satisfying when they connect especially when landing an execution chain on multiple enemies.
As usual, the voice acting and dialogue is excellent as AC goes . The cutscenes and scenery in general is awesome, with great attentions to detail in reconstructing the textures and landscapes. It really feels like being in the renaissance! The maps were very detailed and well put together so you rarely take the same paths twice, if ever. The ability to call and ride horses instantly everywhere makes getting around on roads and sidewalks a breeze no matter how many npc's are walking around.
There's still a lot of repetition in mission events, go here, go there, stab someone, run away, hide etc. That aside, it's definitely a game series worth playing and I'm gonna get on AC Revelations tonight!

I recently purchased Shovel Knight and it was one of the best purchases I ever made. From start to finish the game was a excellent experience. It's a 2D sidescrolling platformer that is a tribute to old-school platformers like those from the NES era. You play as Shovel Knight a knight whom uses a shovel as his weapon and can swing it to attack enemies or jump with it and bounce off of enemies using it. You select a level from the world map and then play through it acquiring checkpoints along the way. Eventually, you fight a boss at the end of the level. Once you finish all the levels you then face the final boss like any other platformer out there. This game is so amazingly good because of the great level designs. Each level plays drastically different from the others and every level is incredibly fun. Shovel Knight also is challenging and you will die a few times, but there's no nonsense like you die and have to do a ten minute level all over again. The music in the game is also nothing short of exceptional. This is one of the better game soundtracks out there and the composer deserves a congratulations along with the level designer. Overall, if you're a fan of 2D platformers you would be foolish to pass on this outstanding platformer.

This game... Fun but very crude in its humour. I will add a TL;DR at the end.
The gameplay within Apocalypse: Party's Over is very enjoyable. The 3 different characters provide a good amount of variety and laughs. It's also easy to laugh or cringe at the enemies. The game itself is not for those who can't take a joke, mostly because of it's content and entire style. There is fun beat-em-up gameplay which is honestly a blast and of course I only played on ♥♥♥♥in' Manly mode (I’m no Half-boner).
The problem starts when enemies will sometimes get knocked off screen and especially in some stages will have you waiting even up to 10 seconds just for them to come back! There is also the fact that when I used my special ability on a certain mini-boss he would take the damage, of course, but then he would start his special attack rhythm when I am doing my special! This lead to me dying multiple times on the level because he would have his attack hit me just as my special finished.
Apocalypse is simply an offensive game, no other way to put it. If you can get past its sense crude humour, it has a good base. The enemies have variety and actually make you try, because sometimes if you are not careful they can easily do combos consisting of different types of enemies which can do devastating damage to you.
The game also contains a shop where it is possible to purchase better weapons and as the stoner version of superman calls it "the items for wussies". Each character can upgrade their light and heavy attack weapons twice and also has different skins (four for each character) to try. The game has two different kind of playable areas as I see it. First the main story areas and then "Junk's Mother♥♥♥♥ing Challenge".
The graphics are smooth and polished, although some of the models used for characters in the game made me question if we really should start the Apocalypse on humanity.
The music is actually nice to listen too but some of the enemy voices are just.... I wish I could specifically mute enemies voices, ok let's say that.
+ Offensively Funny (this could be a pro or con depending on how offended this game makes you)
+ Good gameplay/structure
+ Easy to get into
+ Character Diversity
- Enemies go off-screen (I absolutely hate this, especially the one mini-boss who waits at the side off-screen and fires at you and if you get close he simply hits you or does his special move)
- Only local co-op
Suggestions I feel would improve the game
- Stop enemies from going off-screen so much / taking so long to get back (and attacking when still off-screen for ranged)
- Allow English subtitles with the Portuguese version (honestly like the Portuguese since that is the original language of the game but I can't understand unless I'm in English)
- Online multiplayer
Apocalypse is a good game, but for a specific taste. You really need to come into this game with a certain attitude or you're going to have a bad time. I found the game quite fun, but very challenging in some levels, especially the last level. I wasn't able to try out any of the co-op since I usually play online with my friends and online co-op was not a feature.
Containing fun gameplay alongside it's rather crude humour Apocalypse: Party's Over is a game for a centered taste. If you like beat-em-up side scrollers this could be a game for you, just be ready for the crude humour, don't take the games jokes or characters too seriously, and most likely it will be a funny and enjoyable experience for you.

Apocalypse:  Party's over is surprisingly a fun game.  If you can look past the crude humor, which honestly is not that bad if you watch crude shows.  After a while you forget about it anyways and start enjoying the gameplay.
The gameplay mechanics are solid (no pun intended), pretty standard beat-em-up, you have light attack, heavy attack, jump, and specials.  As you play the game and gain levels you learn different combos and specials.  You will also gain stat points that you can use to customize your character.  You go from stage to stage and pretty much beat up the enemies and fight bosses.
Some gripes is how the heavy attack is tied to a mana bar, which is a bummer, I guess it is to prevent spamming attacks.  Some combos are a teeny bit strict on the timing you can pull off, not a huge deal, but when you start panicking you will notice it.
Overall this is a decent game, a very fun beat-em-up.  I feel the price is good you'll get your money's worth.

Alright after a couple of hours I feel I can place some of my thoughts here along with some things that need to be added or fixed.
First off the game is very similar to the previous Airport Madness games but with the aspect of real 3D geometry. Overall it is a fun game with the same goals and feel of the previous game but it certainly could use some fixes. Below are some missing or questions I have for the game. I am however 100% suggesting you buy this game if interested because it is unique and fun.
1) Would love a distance to airport added above each plane.
2) Visuals of the ground need a serious upgrade. This game could look amazing with this part updated.
3) Some bugs / glitches are there like plane icons getting stuck floating. I am sure this will be fixed.
4) No esc option in game? At least my system would not pause or anything while hitting this key.
5) Would love a free cam option.
6) Clicking planes can often be a problem when they are stacked up. Not sure what the solution is but at certain angles you can click the wrong plane and give orders.
7) Highest overall quality asset is the fake twitter images that pop up.
8) Speaking of the fake twitter, it is often totally wrong. People complaining about delays when the airport is running as smooth as possible. This part annoys me because it if was accurate it could be a cool addition. As it stands now it seems to just be the same thing over and over no matter what is happening on screen.
9) The game does take a while to nail down the best view for your playstyle. Not really a knock on the game but an FYI, do not give up if you do not like the controls or view. Adjust in the settings.
10) Would love an overall passengers moved stat. Planes moved is nice but lets go a step deeper.
11) Stress meeter? Not sure what this means as I was flying along moving planes like an ace with no stress and it just kept growing.
12) Obviously more content. Only 4 airports at launch and I know more are promised but it is info that people need to know.
Overall the game is still super unique and fun and I will easily get my value out of it but there is a TON of potential that I hope we see in a future release.

"Amnesia: The Dark Descent" is one of the few games tha I can seriously call a horror game. While many games are able to provoke dishust, tension, or even brief moments of fright, Amnesia brings dread.  Several times I had to pause the game and wait for my hands to start shaking, and many of these times I've had to exit the game and return after adrenaline had worn off. There are two reasons for this.
The first, and probably the most interesting part of this game, is that your character, Daniel, is utterly unable to defend himself. Your only methods of defense against the creatures of the castle is running, hiding, and putting as much as possible between your pursuers and yourself. Honestly, there's a good chance you'll never get a good look at any of your enemies; enemies notice you if you stare too long at them, only further encouraging for you to turn tail, don't look back, and hide crouched in a dark corner or closet.
Second, the game is masterful in its patience when providing suspense. For the first hour or so, you will only catch glimpses of danger. Even late in the game, encounters with enemies are fairly uncommon and brief. Instead, most of the time you will walk through dark hallways, the fantastic sound (seriously, use headphones) will have  you listening to the squeaks of the rats in the walls and the roars of....something....stomping through the castle, dreading an encounter that will never come. In fact, several levels have few or no encounters with creatures at all, instead opting to just fill you with the always-uncomfortable anticipation of one.
Amnesia works because it knows horror is not about what you see. Instead, its about  what you think you might see. And what I think I might see is usually some guy with his head split open with a rusty knife where his hand might be. There's a bonus campaign now, Justine. I hear at one point an insane cannibal chases you through a dungeon. I think I'll play it eventually....but first, a few games that don't provide so much cardiac stress.

Fishing Planet was a game with tons of Potential when it first released.
The game has since initially grown in popularity and success, at first the dev's
did some unique things, like tournaments where they actually ponied up and payed
out real life cash for the winners.
They released more content more places to fish, they brought out competitions etc.
At first glance it seemed like a game heading in all the right directions.
And then you started to see the true end goal.  To make money!  However, why should a game
making money be that big of a deal its sorta the purpose of a game is to make its developer's money!
Well its how they have done it,  at every turn they make the economy more brutal.  They introduce wear and tear on your rods and reels, now they have even started to nerf DLC content, yes stuff people already spent money on is being rebalanced???  Why so they can sell a new replacement for it!!!  Your premium currency formerly Gold has been readjusted to baitcoins...  and they same things you could have purchased with you gold 10 times over you can now only afford once after the transition from gold to baitcoin.  Even the tournements are broken, 2 fishermen do not have equal odds to win, it depends on who has spent more money and has the better gear?!?
Fishing Planet is a game that had tons of potential that is now nothing more then a slow agonizing grind, you need to be an accountant with HR Block in order to navigate all the travel fee's and licensing fee's and then you have to have a plethera of time on your hands in order to catch enough fish to pay off all those fee's.....  There is no casual fishing as any fishing trip in the game demands a commitment of time just to break even.
It possible things could change in the future, the game seems to change and update frequently, but most of the changes have been in the wrong dirrection.  And for that reason I cannot recommend this game and suggest you check out IceLakes instead....  while its only Ice Fishing its a fair more enjoyable experience!

For those of you who are wondering, this is an emulation of a Sony PS1 game that was released by XS Games in 2002. For those of you who don't know who XS games were, they were responsible for porting over some games that came over from Japan. Their first attempt at marketing a game from japan was Mobile Light Force I believe. While the Charlies Angels theme for that game did not go so well gamers immediately liked the ability to play Gunbird. The company took note and did not alter games again and released games in their original themes.
This game does play well compared to it's counter part and while there are some frames of animation that are missing from this version of the game it still plays smoothly and well. There are no instances of where the game says "Now loading" which makes the game even more fun to play. If you are not an expert in this game, you can button mash your way through the first few levels and continue right in the middle where you left off, even in boss battles. But once you get to a certain stage and you get defeated by a certain boss, you can continue, but it sends you back to the beginning of the level. I think this was intentional by the developer for a challenge, even if you put it on the easy level.
There are some minor hitches to this game that I did not understand at first. I did not know how to tell if I was truly in full screen mode or not and found out there was a check mark next to Windowed to tell me I was there. But once I unticked that box I was in full screen. The visuals did look nice in Full Screen.
Also.... When the audio transitions to another track, you can hear a slight popping noise. While not annoying it does show the effects of emulation. Don't hate the game because of it.
Finally I'm not happy at the fact that I can't take screenshots. The emulation technology they use has to use some form of Open GL or Direct 3D instead of software rendering etc. If they can implement a way to get screenshots for the game working it would be nice to share with my friends who don't have the game yet so they can see more of it in action then the screenshots and video that is on display in the store.
Overall a wonderful effort from Console Classics to legally revive a generation of classic gaming we once thought was dead minus some very tiny inperfections.

Update (5.25.16) - Adjusting some details to accommodate for newly added features. And as a side note, this only covers the standard campaign.
If this landed on the NES way back as it is (sans modern-era features like achievements and Streetpass), it would have been GOAT. As it stands, it's my personal GOAT.
Gameplay: Absolutely fantastic. The controls are designed for a NES-style platforming experience, and on Wii U it's pretty simple. However, on PC you have a variety of different options. The physics and actions are what you'd expect from a 2D 8-bit platformer, and unlike most platformers I've played (that aren't Mario), Shovel Knight makes them near-perfect. As far as what this game has going for it, it doesn't try to directly copy from Mega Man or Mario. Rather, it takes inspiration from the better games of its era and crafts something original while still keeping within the restrictions of the era. 10/10
Graphics: It, like many, MANY pixel-art games these past few years, boasts an "8-bit retro aesthetic"; notably it's become one of my pet peeves. However, out of all the games that try to claim authenticity (forgive me for misspelling), Shovel Knight comes incredibly close. In fact, graphics-wise it's one of the very few games that deserves the title (the others being Mighty Gunvolt, Mega Man 9 and Mega Man 10; not even the recently-released Axiom Verge deserves this due to a crapton of visual effects more suited to a modern game despite having really solid foreground art). From there, a great visual style and some top-tier NES animation makes for a great-looking game overall. (Special mention goes to the Xbox One version, which near-perfectly emulates the Battletoads style in both Turbo Tunnel and Wookie Hole) 9/10
Difficulty: Standard gameplay isn't quite challenging. I'd say it's about as difficult as Super Mario Bros. 3, to give a direct comparison. It ramps up around the third area (Flying Machine, Standed Ship, and Clockwork Tower). The bosses, on the other hand, are pretty difficult until you get used to them. Once you beat the main game, you unlock New Game Plus, which is by far more difficult than you'd expect. Enemies deal double damage, reduced number of checkpoints, barely any health recovery...oof! (XB1 only - you fight the Battletoads in a level that is basically a clone of the Wookie Hole and the infamous Turbo Tunnel. Expect that to be pretty difficult.) 10/10 it's fair.
Music: Jake Kaufman is no stranger to chiptune composition. One of his most famous works outside of Shovel Knight was Shantae for the GBC. Here, he doesn't mess around. Together with Manami Matsumae, Shovel Knight boasts an impressive soundtrack composed entirely in authentic NES chiptune with very catchy tunes that wouldn't feel out of place in the NES era. (Special mention goes to the Village theme and "The Forlorn Sanctum", which successfully implement a variable mix.) 10/10
Writing: The story itself is standard-fare for a video game. Your girlfriend has been captured, go save her! Defeat a multitude of bosses along the way! However, the dialogue in this game is wordy, and although it's definitely quirky there's so much of it that I felt it wasn't really all that authentic. Granted, I liked it, but considering not many NES games had that much text unless it was an RPG, it felt jarring. 8/10
PSN Exclusive Features: It features a three-stage boss battle against Kratos, from God of War, and gain armor that lets you play like Kratos does. As I have not purchased nor played the PSN version, I an unable to give this a score as of writing. N/A
XBL Exclusive Features: You fight the Battletoads in a three-part level: One in a level resembling and playing just like the Wookie Hole, another in a level that's straight-up Turbo Tunnel, and then all of them in one final showdown. It's crazy-hard (though probably easy compared to the original, which I have not played), but it's fun and it's probably the best throwback to the Battletoads I have ever seen. Although I criticize Microsoft's usage of Rare IP sometimes, I would argue this is the best use of it to date. After the boss battle, you get Toad Armor, which lets you play almost exactly like a Battletoad (controls, moves, and all), and you get to talk with the various characters (including, surprisingly, Professor T. Bird); and you even get to play the original Turbo Tunnel all you want. Kudos to Yacht Club Games for making this happen. 10/10
Wii U Exclusive Features: It incorporates Miiverse on the bottom screen, which you can use to view tips or general posts. It's pretty nifty, but I never found it all that useful. On the plus side, it allows you to use the Wii Remote to capture that authentic NES style of control. Edit: It also sports amiibo, which either allows you to have co-op multiplayer (which why would they lock that to an amiibo?) or lets you customize your own "Custom Knight" and use a variety of different abilities and relics, most exclusive to the amiibo mode. It's decent enough, but I only fully recommend it if you're going for a challenge run and/or New Game Plus, and the $12.99 paywall may deter you if you don't have the money to spare. Thus, I felt it unnecessary to raise the score. 7/10
3DS Exclusive Features: Outside of it being 3D, it has a Streetpass Arena, which lets you record gameplay and fight other players with that recorded gameplay. It's a silly little throwback to Mario Bros, and I found this pretty well done. Edit: Much like the Wii U, it also has "Custom Knight" mode, which functions the exact same as it does on home console. It lacks the co-op multiplayer aspect, however. 9/10
Steam/PC Exclusive Features: N/A
Conclusion: Shovel Knight solidified its place as my favorite game of 2014, and is up there among my favorite games of all time (the others being Super Mario Bros. Deluxe, Paper Mario, its direct sequel, and Splatoon as of 5/25/16). If you're looking for an authentic retro throwback, this game is for you. If you're not looking for that and are instead looking for a good platformer, then you'll find, as I have, that this game transcends nostalgia and treats the player with a genuinely great game.
Overall: 10/10
PC: 9/10
PSN: N/A
Wii U: 10/10
3DS: 10/10
Xbox One: 10/10 (recommended platform)

This is a third-person shooter in which you take control of an Earth Defense Force soldier defending against aliens, robots, bugs, dragons, dinosaurs, and versions of all of each which increase in size. You can select from a regular soldier, a wing diver which has low armor stats but is super fast and has some powerful weaponry, a person who can summon various vehicles, and a big lug who moves slowly and has more difficult controls, but is quite the powerhouse once you learn how to utilize it properly. Each unit has hundreds of weapons to choose from, from machine guns and shotguns to rocket and missile launchers (and that only scratches the surface in terms of number and variety), and you can even change unit color. The dialogue is hilarious and you can destroy literally everything, including buildings and your own teammates (and there is one exception: pedestrians).
This version of the game is the ultimate version, with content added and graphics updated from its prior release (Earth Defense Force 2025). It is one of those few games in which, even after hundreds of hours of play, is still loads of fun, with some of the highest replay value you'll find in all of video gaming, whether with or without co-op but especially with co-op. For this reason, I find it to be one of the very best video games ever made, one of my higest recommendations. The game has a decent fun/challenge ratio, but can be frustrating at times, mostly when you're ragdolled around, or really late in the game especially with the DLC missions (pro tip: just keep practicing prior levels, on higher difficulties even, and gain more armor and weapons). It plays well enough on weaker PCs, but even then I'd recommend a decent enough PC because it can easily have some slowdown; some have reported problems with AMD Phenom 2 processors.

6/10
Summary: addictive, arcade-style in 3D, clean environment, minimalistic interface, can be relaxing. Lot of good points but I also have some bones to pick.
AUDIO
~ PRO: I spend 99.99% of my time in games with music turned off. Turning off music is the first thing I do the instant any game gives me access to its Settings menu. Absolute Drift (AD henceforth) is an exception. The only other game in recent memory (and by recent I mean the past two decades) where I have tolerated having game music playing for more than a half hour at a stretch is Gunpoint. The soundtrack in AD is kind of repetitive, not many songs to choose from, but they are randomized and if you don't like the current one you can skip ahead to another track without letting your hand off the "steering wheel". Genre is Chill Electro with a side of downtempo DNB so if that's your dish then I'd recommend getting this game for the music if nothing else.
~ CON: Game's sound effects are annoying and distracting. I finally muted them completely. AD goes out of its way to put the player in a Zen state of mind, then it ruins that experience with auditory distractions all the while you're trying to learn how to drive, like bass-notes that push through my headphones every time I hit one of the red bonus block fragments which have a despawn timer that operates on a geologic timescale.
CONTROLS
~ PRO: Supports keyboard, Xbox & PS4 controllers. KB can be used simultaneously with a controller (not that you'd want to). Multiple schemes/layouts for the controllers but these include only minor variations.
~ CON: KB ctrls cannot be remapped. If you're like me and still have a keyboard from the Stone Age that plugs into a PS/2 port, this game might be seriously frustrating to play since PS/2 only allows two simultaneous signals yet AD necessitates that you be managing three inputs concurrently for smooth execution of many maneuvers. USB KB's may work better. I finally plugged in my Windows Xbox controller and now I'm blissfully relearning how to drive.
~ SHRUG: The camera is locked. I have no consistent point of reference to my car. I have to keep shifting my perspective, both visually and mentally, as my car traverses through each consecutive 90 degrees of orientation onscreen. This presents an undesirable and artificial challenge to learning to drift in AD.
PROGRESSION
The game has two modes of driving accessible from the main menu: Free-Roam and Events. Free-Roam is a sequence of "worlds" like Mario worlds.
~ PRO: Progress through the Free-Roam is automatically saved and any time you return to Free-Roam your car is automatically placed at the starting point of that world. Events includes everything you've driven past so far in Free-Roam, including Tutorials, so you can return to practice and perfect any event you please at any time.
~ CON: "Free Roam" is nothing of the sort. It is a false moniker for what would be called "Campaign" in an RTS or "New Story" in an RPG. There is no way to learn how to drive in this game other than blundering your way through the worlds with their myriad obstacles and ceaseless demands. Growing tired of a world and want to move on? Too bad! You must complete nearly 100% of the hand-holding immersion-breaking paint-by-numbers content in any given world before the next world becomes unlocked to you. Just like Mario, you will probably have some worlds you like and some you don't. I had just about lost my patience with World 4 (narrow and twisty) and was considering uninstalling the game when I finally came to World 5 and found more open expanses and a couple of nice zig-zaggy canyons in which I could get a feel for how to throw my car's weight around.
FEATURES ACCESS
~ Map: There isn't one. Nope. Notta. Nuthin'. Wondering what missions (tasks) you've missed? Keep driving until you find them. Forgot where that sweet drift spot or kickass jump was? Keep driving until you relocate it. The lack of a map adds gruelling minutes and mounting frustrations to an otherwise peaceful cruise through the park. Sure, a map is not necessary and players who are familiar with the worlds won't feel they need one, but it would have been a nice feature for a new player.
~ Backtrack through worlds: If you want to revisit an old world, there are only two ways to do it: reset your campaign progress, or turn around and drive back through the intervening worlds between where you are and where you want to be. This game's replayability could have benefitted *GREATLY* from having a jump-to-world option at the main menu. As both a Pro & Con, there are only 5 worlds, so your backtrack drive won't take you very long.
~ Play/Practice area: Want a free open space (a true free roam) in which to play and learn how to handle your car and the controls? Too bad! The only place to do this is in the first "room" of Free-Roam and that is a very small room indeed. I was (and still am) hoping for a totally free practice area with maybe a grid overlay and few or no terrain features wherein I could not only practice but also enjoy just doing endless drifts without concern for obstructions, much like the Stunt track in N64's Rush 2 (1998).
INSTRUCTION/LEARNING CURVE
~ New Cars: Each time you complete a Free-Roam world the game rewards you with a new car. Sounds great. But there are no onscreen statistics to tell you how the cars differ from each other. Only way to know is to take them out for a test drive at which time you discover the differences are subtle, ie. borderline non-existent.
~ Time limits: Most events have a time limit even if it is not overtly displayed. Just when you are starting to get the hang of something, time runs out and you have to restart the event. Time limit does make sense in a scenario where you are trying to accumulate points as quickly as possible but most events focus on mechanics of driving which is irrelevant to time. Learning these mechanics is hindered by having your practice session interrupted about every 60 seconds or so.
~ The Donut: My biggest pet peeve is the Donut. The main developer for this game lives in Canada. Don't know what "donut" means north of the border but, in the USA, a donut is a ring of burnt rubber lain on the ground in concentric rings about a fixed point. In AD, a Donut consists of little more than maintaining white smoke from your car's tires without losing momentum as you casually pass by, drift alongside of, reverse past, or even spin in place adjacent to (not around) the objective location. There I was floundering for minutes at a time trying to do a perfect 360 concentric drift around every Donut objective I came across while the game refused to budge my %. Why? Because I would surrender my momentum, come to a halt next to the objective, and try maneuvering into a better drift circle with a handbrake start. The solution? Drive away and come back to try again in the sloppiest, most haphazard, most non-donut-looking driveby drift I've ever been ashamed to do. No explanation, no mercy, total aggravation.
~ Event Finish screens: The game has a plethora of patronizing critique messages to slam your confidence every time you exit a drift stage. My least favorite is, "Remember it's not about speed..."  YES IT IS!  Yes, holding a drift does not require continuous application of the throttle, but *starting* a drift most certainly does! Just who exactly do you think your target audience for this game is?! Any person who enjoys racing, has a driving license, and has taken a core curriculum Physics class -- or, as a substitute for those three, has watched any single season of the sacred "Initial D" -- already has an abundant comprehension of the concept of momentum. You can't start a drift without momentum, and gathering momentum requires speed. STOP TRYING TO TELL ME OTHERWISE YOU CONDESCENDING MONSTER!!!   *breathe... breathe...*

making money be that big of a deal its sorta the purpose of a game is to make its developer's money!

They introduce wear and tear on your rods and reels, now they have even started to nerf DLC content, yes stuff people already spent money on is being rebalanced??? Your premium currency formerly Gold has been readjusted to baitcoins...  and they same things you could have purchased with you gold 10 times over you can now only afford once after the transition from gold to baitcoin. If you enjoy playing Tower Defense games, and you don't mind that hands off approach, this is the game for you.  Nothing is more enjoyable than setting your fleet in motion and watching it annihilate the forces of your enemies.
However, there are a few drawbacks.  The first drawback is that the game tries to encourage you to limit the size of your fleet by rewarding you with "honor" in exchange for sending out a cheaper fleet.  It doesn't care about how many survive their encounter with the enemy, only that yours is the only side left standing.  So there isn't  a point in trying to keep your fleet alive.  Another drawback is that the ship save system gets a bit complicated, leading to a huge swathe of ships made for specific scenarios and set ups.
So again:  Like designing your ships and sending them into combat, go for it.  Looking to fly them yourself or be rewarded for your brilliant tactics?  Move on.

This may be the best LEGO game I've played since the Lego Star Wars prequel trilogy on Xbox Original, but WB spared expenses on this port big-time.  We're up to three crashes and a BSoD so far, and keep in mind, this is the supposdely MORE stable version (DX9), with D3D11 completely unsupported on 32-bit systems.  If you're still on 32-bit OS's, steer clear.  As for 64-bit?  Moving on!
I felt like Malcolm was sitting in the room repeating "chaos theory" every minute with the launch of this game.  For such a simple game, a new engine and rushed deadline led to a rather unstable and broken PC launch.  However, the issues have been smoothed out, so we can look past it.  The stories of the four Jurassic Park movies are told very well in the LEGO format, altering the script for more humorous situations and making the most of every situation.  It feels like a real improvement over previous games, and you still have to give Traveller's Tales credit for making one of the only E rated AAA releases this year.
My biggest problem with the game is that at times, it felt a little
childish.  Namely, I'm talking about flat-out censoring a lot of scenes, or rewriting them with cop-out happy endings.  The original LEGO games were at least a general audience, but what kills a lot of the humor in this game is how they suddenly cut back to ruin the punchline with "but see!  He's actually perfectly fine and not in any danger whatsoever!  Nobody died!"  Moments like these really kill it.  It feels like that ending scene to the Muppets reboot, where they showed a rather interesting plot-twist just to ruin it after the credits.
Also, the puzzles are a bit too simplistic, making this more of a beach-read than a game... though I can overlook that bit, given the audience.  Still, "Simon Says" is about the most challenge you'll ever get from it, and it's more of an interactive movie than anything.
Unlike other LEGO games, 70% of the combat has been replaced with chase scenes... which makes sense, since y'know, they're dinos and not 5-foot robots, but it still tarnishes a large part of the game by leaving almost no unscripted events.
My biggest complaint, by far, has to be the voices.  I've had this problem with all of the recent Lego games; I don't like the fact that they're using actual movie lines.  In the older titles, they were speechless, and got along with gibberish and grunts.  Tt used this to their advantage, to take a humorous spin on many scenes.  For example, in the original Lego Star Wars, there was a scene where battledroids blew up a ship, and the pilots sat there in mid-air before looking at each other, then the ground, and yelled at the same time before falling and exploding into legos.  Here, they're cutting audio directly from the movie.  If you've watched it, you already know it, and they don't do anything special with it.  They don't even have actual files, they just cut the audio directly out of the films, and the audio quality suffers for it.  I really wish Tt would go back to the old ways with this.
Other than that, I still recommend the game.  As one of the last franchises to bear a kid-friendly rating, Tt still delivers a rather entertaining spin on the movies, and let's face it, I've always wanted them to take a stab at the original three Jurassic Park movies.  I had a lot of doubts as to whether or not they could pull it off without it falling short, but it pleasantly surprised me.  Besides, Arkham Knight was garbage anyway, what else was I supposed to get?

GSB is a unique take on the strategy genre. Unlike most strategy games, you don't directly control your troops (or in this case, capital ships and fighter squadrons). In fact, you have no say at all once the battle's begun, but that's not a bad thing.
The idea is that you're the "fleet commander" and you give your orders to whatever ships are going into battle.  The ships' captains and fighter squadron leaders are then left to make their own decisions during combat. Sometimes things don't go as intended, but that's war.
You get to purchase new items for your ships with "honor points" (based on how few ships you needed to win a battle) and these upgrades can make a major difference.  Best of all, the game is designed with modding in mind.  You can find tons of mods already available -- many of which are based on Star Wars, Star Trek and so on -- and it's not too difficult to make your own.
In closing, I'd definitely recommend buying this game. There's a demo to try, too.

With

None other contemporary neo-retro game looks and feels so close to a NES real hardware as
. And none other game has understood so well some of the design premises of japanese most beloved classics, even in subtle and almost insignificant aspects related to its sound construction.
For years another brazilian neo-retro creation,

is an incredible leap forward respect to

One of the aspects on which
truly shines in its attempt of recreating a NES original hardware, is in its almost perfect CRT simulation. In the past, we have seen a lot of games trying to mimic the look of the old fat televisions using modern LCD panels. But a lot of times, seems as the developers had never seen a game running in a real vintage television. With too much accented horizontal lines and overdramatized special effects ruining the experience.
Until

Perhaps part of the problem is the fact that I'm not innately familiar with the character, but despite my usual affinity for surreal and/or silly games this one just didn't do it for me. It's about as simple as you could ask for, play-wise - you can only run and jump, and that's all you need to do to grab a floating key on each screen and move on to the next one. There are various enemies and obstacles in your way, of course, but despite their varied nature they exist to frustrate you above all else: it's frequently difficult to tell which onscreen elements will hurt you at a glance, and unclear which background pieces you can jump on until you take a leap of faith. You can take a fair number of hits before dying, but you only get one life and energy refills are scarce, so expect frequent trips back to the very beginning as you execute the necessary trial-and-error banging of one's head against a wall until you figure the nastier parts out.
I can appreciate the game's efforts to recall the 8-bit days in terms of both presentation and challenge (and its cheap asking price too), but losing precious life points due to design uncertainty and nickel-and-diming hit detection over and over again just doesn't make me eager to see this one through to the end. I certainly can't say I lost a huge amount of time or money on Tcheco, but I also can't say I enjoyed what I did experience of it, and thus can't recommend it to others either.

Shovel Knight is a game that pays homage to many classic NES games.  It borrows gameplay elements from the likes of Mario, Zelda, Metroid, and Castlevania to name a few.  To the outside observer, this game could easily be believed to have come out in the late 80s.  However, the game has many modern elements that keep it from feeling dated in the least bit.
The game is stupendously fun.  There is no real difficulty setting (aside from New Game+), however players are able to set the difficulty for themselves, in ways like deciding whether to buy upgrades, which armour to use, what weapons to use, and even being able to destroy checkpoints in stages for a little extra money at the penalty of starting further back.  The music in this game is expertly composed, being some of the best I've heard recently in games. Each tune fits every level perfectly, my favourite being Propeller Knight's stage (appropiately titled "Flying Machine").
Shovel Knight to me stands out as a shining example of the amazing things crowdfunding can produce.  It also shows the quality and attention to detail modern indie games should all aspire to have.
Yacht Club Games did a fantastic job with this game, and I am excited to see what they bring in the future, whether that be Shovel Knight related or not.
This game is definitely worth the buy.  It's a little short, but the quality of play time is higher than that of most AAA-games that have budgets and teams that are more than a hundred fold of what this game had.

Anyone that has played a classic NES game like Super Mario Bros. or The Legend of Zelda will tell you that there was a certain charm and atmosphere to those games. The hardware limitations forced developer to get creative with how they went about making memorable titles. Shovel Knight is the modern equivalent of that feeling, embodying everything that made that system so great. It combines the best elements from a handful of classic NES games to create something that is truly unique and worth any platformer fan's time and money.
With the level design and enemy placement of Mega Man, the mechanics of Ducktales, and a sense of humor that's all its own, Shovel Knight is a triumphant accomplishment in the world of indie games. The best way to describe the aesthetic of Shovel Knight is "authentic." Every pixel of it feels like it would've been right at home on the NES in 1985. Even the concept of a knight that uses a shovel for a weapon hearkens back to the days when a band of "Battletoads" were perfectly acceptable protagonists.
Each level is masterfully designed with a heavy emphasis on the where enemies are placed. As you progress, you'll get additional weapons like an arching throwing anchor and a helpful long-range fireball.  These tools will help defeat the many enemies and bosses, but knowing the best opportunity to attack is key. If you're impatient and just want to get through the levels like me, you'll be frustrated with how the enemies function. Most of them require patience, which was pretty frustrating to me. I eventually memorized how each of them attack and utilize the secondary weapons, but it took a lot of trial and error.
It's really worth mentioning the outstanding soundtrack. Every track stands alone as memorable and fits each stage incredibly well so that it is the perfect embodiment of how the stage plays out. I was seriously humming some of these tunes for weeks afterward; they're that catchy. The story is also similarly engaging. Shovel Knight must save his beloved from the Order of No Quarter and the Enchantress. It's simple, but the dialouge that the knights exchange hints at a much deeper lore.
Despite having so many ties to NES, Shovel Knight understands that it doesn't need to be bogged down by the conventions of that era. Lives are no longer a factor in today's gaming culture and this game gets that. Instead, you lose some of your collected treasure, which you can then pick up again if you make it back to the place where you died before.
Shovel Knight is a lovingly crafted throwback that gets it all right. The gameplay is great, the music is amazing, and the whole package is a blast to play. It's not an incredibly long adventure, but definitely one worth digging into.
