When I first saw this game, I thought given the name it’d be an awesome little indie RPG/Rogue like with great customisation from loot. However, I was quickly disappointed to find out it was hardly anything like the name of the game and here’s why:
Pros:
♦ Sound is decent (For what it is, the sound is decent)
♦ Storyline is great (For the limited storyline that is in the game, it is great)
♦ Has Steam Features such as Cards and Achievements (This is awesome as every game on Steam should be making use of Steam Features)
Cons:
♦ Doesn’t live up to the name of the game (There is limited loot, customisation and upgrades)
♦ Graphics is blurry (8-bit retro style graphics is a nice touch, but to me they look more blurry than what they should)
♦ No real options menu (The game doesn’t really have much to it to warrant an options menu, but should have an actual menu as the game is on PC)
♦ Expensive as its $4 USD on Steam when it’s 100% free on other platforms (It’s free on kongregate as a flash game, Android and IOS etc. I haven’t played the mobile versions but the only difference between the Steam and free flash web version is one or two extra monster levels, miners, Steam Trading Cards and 1 or 2 extra grindy achievements which all these added features for the paid version isn’t really anything worth paying the high price for)
♦ Hero levelling pointless (I say this as when you level up, no matter if you’re level 2 or 50, you get the same one or two points to your skills. This gives you no incentive to level up other than for Steam Achievements)
♦ Steam Achievements too grindy (To make the game worth playing, all the developers have done is add time consuming and grindy achievements. I say this because you can get all the achievements relatively quick except two, the level up achievements. This is annoying as they take ages to get due to being grindy. These achievements don’t add anything to the game and just make it feel more like a grindy and pointless drag)
♦ Very repetitive and grindy (This is because once you’ve slayed the dragon the first time and got all the upgrades (Which can be done in around 15minutes), there is nothing new added to the game beyond difficulty increases if you repetitively defeat the dragon)
♦ Developers became lazy (I say this as they stopped adding new animations to your hero when you upgraded it, capped gold at 99999 which is way too easy to reach, capped store purchases relatively quickly and didn’t bother to add anything new past the first time you killed the dragon)
♦ Can still purchase critical upgrades even though it’s at 100% (This shouldn’t be the case as you can keep purchasing it and it does nothing. It should be greyed out or removed or something etc)
♦ No incentive to clear any stages other than the dragon (Once you’ve beaten the game once, there is nothing making you want to clear any stage other than the dragon. Only reason you play any stage other than dragon is to grind gold to level up)
♦ Game gets to a point where you only need to purchase defence upgrades to win (Once you’ve gotten every skill to max aka 9999 gold per purchase, all you need is to buy defence to win)
♦ Miners are pointless as gold is capped to 99999 (Miners are in the game to get gold whilst afk. However, once you have 3 or so miners it’s easy for them to get max gold in a few hours. Also, as it’s easy to grind max gold in the game, the miners seem pointless as you don’t really need the afk gold at all)
♦ Glitch where you can run past the end bosses without killing them (You run too fast and end up on the right side of the boss. This isn’t much of a problem but it shouldn’t happen)
♦ Glitch where if you're not entirely a strong enough level to instantly beat a wave, you can get stuck behind the side of the screen and constantly keep fighting the same enemy and not doing any damage until you die (This shouldn’t be the case at all)
♦ Replayability is weak (There is nothing worth replaying for except harder difficulty, which really isn’t much of an incentive as the game could have had highscores and so much more to make you want to replay it etc)
Things the developers could have added:
♦ Auto next level (Needs this feature as going back to the main menu every time after clearing a stage is very pointless and annoying)
♦ Highscores (Could easily added highscores where you can judge the highest player level, furthest level and, highest attack, defence, speed etc. This would give the game competitiveness and add a reason to keep grinding and playing to become number 1)
♦ More Customisation (Such as more loot, items, more upgrade animations etc. This would have given the game more of an exciting edge and would add new things beyond seeing everything in 15minutes and defeating the dragon the first time)
♦ Worlds (This would have added an edge to the game to make it even better. Instead of doing the same levels over and over, it could have had themed worlds)
Overall, as the game has way more cons than pros, it is free on any other platform other than Steam and the fact Steam makes you pay a high $4 USD for Steam Achievements and Cards, the fact the game is 100% grindy and has no new gameplay past the first 15minutes and the fact devs could have added so much more to the game, I cannot recommend this unless it’s heavily on sale.

EDF is a Japanese alien invasion B-movie, basically transposed into a series of games.  Most of the gameplay is comprised of ridiculous ragdolling, getting swarmed by spiders and shouting "EDF!" Uncontrollably.  In general production values are a bit low, but the games tend to be scenario-driven stage to stage, intentionally ridiculous and quite visceral.
Local co-op has always been one of the main draws of the series, but this time the Online Multiplayer is quite good as well.  With four different classes that play quite differently (including one that's almost entirely team-oriented), there's enough variety that not everyone will necessarily call the same roles.  Multiplayer is the majority of the fun, as you collaborate while trying to parse how your friend is wearing a tank as a hat, why most of the city is missing or why half of the vehicles are out and out terrible.
You collect weapons that generally all have a strength and weakness, but gradually become stronger over time.  Not unlike diablo, the higher difficulties allow stronger weapons and let you obtain them through crate drops from enemies.  You end up getting a trickle of interesting guns and death machines, but if you need to get a shiny new toy every mission, this might not work out for you.  On the flip side, there are a lot of missions, so that may appeal to you instead.
All in all, unless you're really dedicated to so-bad-it's-incredible bug squashing on your own, or plan to play split-screen co-op, make sure you can convince some friends to get their own copies and play with you.  If you can't, I definitely can't recommend this enough, but if you can- you're all going to have a really good time.

I like it. It is obviously the same type of game as Gnomoria, inspired by Dwarf Fortress. I don't care if it is considered "abandonware" by the community. Back in the day, you bought software as-is. Any updates after release were at the discretion of the dev, not at the demand of the end-user.

TL;DR
Recommend cause:
- It's LEGO
- It includes all 4 Jurassic Park movies
- You do not get (too many) spoilers, so you can even enjoy the movies after playing the game first
- Collectibles and Replayability (like any LEGO game :P)
- You can play as a Dinosaur xD
Like any LEGO game, I can only recommend it (okay, I admit, I wasn't too pleased with LEGO Marvel Heroes... somehow that game was more of a... drag... than enjoyment, at least for me xD).
Playing through all 4 Jurassic Park movies was pretty awesome and that combined with the typcial LEGO game humor was really fun.
Though I found that 5 level per movie cut it a bit short, at first I was a bit disappointed how fast I played through a movie story, but after playing it a 2nd time, I relized it just had the right length.
Also, because of the LEGO humor they add and how the stories are cut, you can experience a basic of the Jurassic Park movies without actually getting too many spoilers for anyone who hasn't seen the movies yet, and watching them will still excite you.
The voice acting from 1-3 sounds like it was directly cut out of the movies and inserted into the game, which was a bit strange at first, but I actually like that.
They fixed some things which annoyed and frustrated me in the other LEGO games, like jumping on a small pillar to reach another point... how often I fell off and had to run up against cause my character just didn't land EXACTLY on the spot which the game wanted you or cause the camera wasn't in a good position.
Now you just have to press the jump button and the character hops from one pillar to the next, making it quite easy (some might say too easy...) but a lot less frustrating.
They added some others things which became frustrating to me at some points - like turning a handle via the analog stick on your controler (not sure what that would be like on keyboard :S).
It's just unresponsive at times and even if you're circling your analog stick perfectly, it sometimes dropped the progress and you had to start again... it felt like I had to figure out a pace for each handle in which the analog stick was supposed to be turned. Some handles wanted veeeery slow circles, others you could do normally, that was very annoying.
And like any other LEGO game you have your lil glitches, which can be frustrating, but not game ruining.
For example, one worker and some gold bricks were not shown on the map area to collect, in the first HUB (1st Jurassic Park).
I thought the game glitched (like in LEGO LotR) and I had to restart everything to get 100%... which I did and then I came accross that worker in my 2nd playthrough and saw it wasn't displayed on the map. Went back to my old save and look there... he was there, including 2 gold bricks. Got 100% then -.-
But like any other LEGO game from TT Games, you can expect that it will never get a patch and you just gotta live with with. (thanks TT for taking good care of your games after release... maybe something to invest money it from all the DLCs? hmmm)
Anyways, the game is still good and fun and the price okay.

Until this game receives a patch, I cannot recommend purchasing this. I'll go over what I liked first:
- The gameplay is exactly what you'd expect from Lego games. Run around, break things, collect studs, solve puzzles, collect bricks, grind your way towards 100% completion. If you've been liking past Lego games, you'll feel right at home with the gameplay here.
- Like all Lego games of this type, it's a very faithful and humorous re-telling of the four movies it covers. There are a lot of humorous moments, and a lot of the cracks it makes at the movies had me laughing a fair bit.
- The graphics are gorgeous. It's colorful and detailed, as you'd expect from Lego games.
- The free roam areas are pretty awesome. Though they are a bit linear, they are full of things to do, and the amount of detail put into them is incredible. There's a free roam map for each movie, allowing for a good amount of variety.
All-in-all, the game itself is great. However, it's held back by an awful amount of bugs. Here's just a few of what I've encountered:
- In one level, a couple of the NPCs simply floated off into the sky for no particular reason.
- A few chase levels have the dinosaur chasing you glitch out, so it disappears, and you're left with nothing chasing you.
- One red brick wouldn't appear until I restarted my game.
- One red brick DID appear before I even attempted to do a puzzle because my AI partner somehow squeezed himself into the final part of the puzzle.
- In a couple of levels, I randomly fell through the floor, falling forever.
- Several times, I got stuck in some of the background, making progress impossible without restarting the level.
- There have been some invisible walls in various areas, particuarly in the green tubes that the small dinos use. Some have literally been impossible to exit because of random invisible walls.
- Some of the raptor jump levers literally will not let you all the way up onto the platforms you're trying to reach, so you have to fight the controls and the background a bit to finally push yourself up.
- In one bonus level where you play as the Indominous Rex, it literally does not appear, so you can't do anything.
- I rescued a Worker In Peril, but it didn't count towards the peril count for some reason, and now the game is acting like she's there when she's not, rendering 100% completion impossible.
- The game has crashed on me several times.
That's just what comes off the top of my head. There may be more I'm forgetting. One or two glitches, I can understand, but this game is literally plain unfinished. The developers rushed this through the gates without even so much as doing a simple bug-test. A lot of these bugs are things you'll find just through doing a normal playthrough of the game.
I've nearly completed the game, but I can't get 100% because of the missing worker. This playthrough has had its moments of fun, but it's also been nothing short of irritating and mind-boggingly tedious.
If and when a patch comes out, I'd say get this game, but until then, save your money.

*UPDATE*
I finally managed to launch the game with my new gaming laptop since it has NVidia graphic card. The game is surprisingly made really well and I love it! So I decided to remove completely my old review and write a brand new one, a simple pros and cons.
Pros:
+ Completely unique and cool storyline. I don't think any other game has ever thought about stories like this. This kind of story has been my dream for a pretty long time and I never thought someone actually made a game like this
+ Chosen war era is very unique. Other game developers rarely make any games about World War I, Civil War, and the American Indian war, since I know most people will hate sitting on trenches waiting for a head to pop up or having to reload for a long time after every shot while their enemies can hide in trees with bows. But I love it because it is different.
+ Great storyline, not epic but it is really cool and people would be able to make a movie out of this game.
+ Mediocre, but still acceptable graphics. Not much to expect from an old low-budget game. But it is still acceptable for me and I think it is pretty good.
+ Challenging gameplay. Just don't play on the easiest difficulty. With increased difficulty you will receive more damage and it will feel much more tense. Imagine having to reload your musket with the enemy charging you with bayonets.
+ You can use modern assault rifle in civil war era. That's fun LOL.
Cons:
- Cannot run on computers with AMD graphic cards
- Laser weapons, all weapons has 100% accuracy when you aim down the sight and 100% damage on all range. But it has no multiplayer so I don't care about OP weapons
- Abandoned by developers
- Invisible walls
- Bad voice acting
- Character dialogues tend to overlap
- Random crashes, but not too often
- Terrible soundtrack. Almost no soundtracks in-game
- No stealth element. Enemies will easily see you from far away and you get no silenced weapons. You will also move way too slow when you crouch.
Overall, you will easily notice this game is pretty crude since I heard it is a low budget game. Square-ish no expression face, bad voice acting, bad animation, no melee animation, etc. But the storyline is very unique and the war era is really not like other FPS games. There may be other FPS Civil War/American-Indian War/World War 1 game out there like Verdun, but as far as I know, people rarely make games in this war era and it makes this game worth buying and playing. The campaign itself isn't too long and it's just like finishing CoD and Battlefield's single player campaign. But I really like this game for its unique storyline and war era. However, I decided not to change my recommendation status since I personally think this game is overpriced. Wait for a discount or something. It's not worth the price for its short campaign and little to nothing replay value.

: Traveller's Tales
: Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment
==========
LEGO Jurassic World is the newest installment in the acclaimed LEGO series of games. It covers all 3 Jurassic Park films and the new Jurassic World film, recreating iconic moments from each film in LEGO style. It's been released on nearly every currently available console and PC. Let's dive right into it, shall we?
==========
Being a LEGO game, there are a number of things to do and collect in each level. You play as one of many feature characters from each film, each complete with their own unique special abilities. Some characters are equipped with certain tools, and others have weapons and other miscellaneous abilities. For example, Dr. Grant has a spade which he can use to dig up things, and also a raptor claw, which can be used to cut through obstacles. Nearly everything you see is breakable and rewards you with studs. You can then use these studs to unlock new characters, vehicles, and dinosaurs. There are also Minikits, Gold Bricks, and Amber to collect. Some of these are very cleverly hidden as well, as each stage encourages repeat playthroughs with different unlocked characters to find every secret. All of the fun is playing through each stage and trying to collect as many studs as you can while reliving all the epic moments from the Jurassic Park/World films.
==========
As with all LEGO games, the films were recreated nearly entirely out of LEGO blocks and shapes. The characters and dinosaurs are all LEGO built, as well as the environments, vehicles, and other items. Some of the background sets are more realistic pieces, such as landscape views and large clusters of trees and foliage, but for the most part nearly everything is built from LEGOs. This is by no means the most graphically intense or impressive game out there, but it has it's "Wow!" moments, which is impressive considering the blocky and oftentimes clunky nature of LEGOs.
==========
John Williams' familiar groundbreaking compositions abound in LEGO Jurassic World, including the
. When the doors of Jurassic Parks swing open and that theme plays, you will undoubtedly remember your first time experiencing the film and the awe-inspiring feeling the music gave you. All of that is here in the game, and more! If you aren't familiar with John Williams, he has composed some of the most popular and recognizable themes in cinematic history, including
,
,
, and of course
. For the Jurassic World segments of the game, the music is instead done by Michael Giacchino, using the tracks from the film.
Almost every character is fully voiced, and has lines taken directly from the films. However, some of them sound like they were directly ripped from the films and jammed into the game instead of using new, clean recordings. For those with a keen sense of these things, it's VERY noticeable, but it should not bother most players whatsoever.
==========
My current PC specs are an AMD FX-8320 8 Core processor, with 16 GB of RAM, and a NVIDIA GeForce GTX 750 Ti. With this system I experienced no problems with framerate and no stuttering at all. Everything ran very smoothly, even while recording my gameplay demo video, which I will post at the end of this review. I personally did not experience any bugs or glitches, but I have read about a very few people who experienced a few game-breaking glitches and were unable to progress because of them, one of them as early as the second level.
==========
LEGO Jurassic World is a great installment for the LEGO series of games, which perfectly captures and recreates the wonder and majesty of Jurassic Park/Jurassic World even while being completely made of LEGOs. Traveller's Tales has once again taken a beloved franchise and done it great justice transforming it into a veritable playground for people of all ages to enjoy. It deserves a spot in your library, alongside other LEGO titles such as LEGO Batman, LEGO Star Wars, and LEGO Harry Potter.

Shovel Knight is a challenging, yet very rewarding platformer in old-school pixel graphic style. It is famous for a reason, if I may say, and let me show you why...
- - - - - Commence argumentation - - - - -
Controls:
+easy to understand
+extremely responsive
Game Feeling:
+old-school pixel graphics for the retro-game enthusiasts out there
+awesome soundtracks
+superb storytelling
Story:
+easy to follow
+makes the player feel involved
+short and understandable sections of story text (prevents "too long to read" attitude)
-feels like a framework put together to give a reason to the story
Gameplay:
+great overworld map in style of Super Mario Bros. 3
+challenging, yet fair difficulty
+various items to assist your quest (varying from projectile weaponry to short-lived invulnerability)
+several items and skills to buy for in-game money
+great replay value
-short game (I'm only saying speedrun achievement with 1 hour 30 minutes or less)
- - - - - Commence results - - - - -
Shovel Knight is more than meets the eye. It is an experience everyone should make over the course of their gaming life. If you don't, you're at risk of missing out on one of the best indie titles out there. So steel thy shovel, and journey onward to dig deep into this game, because it's content is one of the greatest treasures in the game library Steam is able to offer.
Results:
Gameplay: 10/10, despite the short story
Feeling: 10/10 for retro-game enthusiasts like I am, 8/10 for anyone else
Story: 8/10
Difficulty: 8/10 (hard, but not Dark Souls levels of hard)
Final result: 9.5/10 for retro-gamers and 8.75/10 for regular players
- - - - - Commence final comment - - - - -
This game is a must-have in any old-school player's library and a great recommendation for any experienced player willing to put himself through the challenge that is Shovel Knight.

Sometimes in your haste to enjoy a game, you don't give it a good chance. My first time playing this game (well, maybe my first hour) was me being really frustrated at not being able to drift, not being able to control my car, and generally not being able to make it the way I wanted. I pictured a game that was more about relaxing and leisurely drifting through tracks or endless highways, but was wrong.
The thing is, I don't mind being wrong; Absolute Drift has a great mechanics system that rewards you for putting time in and learning how your car works. This is likely as close to it comes to the real world, too, as no one is necessarily a Drift King the first time they try. The more time I spent tweaking the settings (note: you may find Hard controls with 100% steering sensitivity better if you're used to drifting in other Arcade-y racers) the more I felt myself gradually getting better.
The cool thing is, every time I boot the game up now I genuinely need to warm up, as my first ten minutes are me reacclimating to how my car controls. This isn't a
thing at all; again, it rewards patience and persistence, and the first time you actually
pull off something awesome (be it a chain drift, or even a drift that's challenging things a little too far) you feel amazing.
Essentially this game rewards mastery of the mechanics and the time it takes to learn them. My main complaints are that I could do without the time limits, objectives and feedback during some event courses: I would love to be able to turn it off and just practice drifting (or just doing it therapeutically) without the game telling me I'm dropping combos or running out of time.
I also think this game (especially when it's called a Zen Edition) could use some procedurally-generated endless highway that either has a difficulty you specify or one that changes organically; I LOVE the mountain and midnight courses in this game, but find them woefully too short.
Great game, but you need to be patient with it. If you do, you'll find awesome, rewarding moments.

EDF is a Japanese alien invasion B-movie, basically transposed into a series of games.  Most of the gameplay is comprised of ridiculous ragdolling, getting swarmed by spiders and shouting "EDF!" Uncontrollably.  In general production values are a bit low, but the games tend to be scenario-driven stage to stage, intentionally ridiculous and quite visceral.
Local co-op has always been one of the main draws of the series, but this time the Online Multiplayer is quite good as well.  With four different classes that play quite differently (including one that's almost entirely team-oriented), there's enough variety that not everyone will necessarily call the same roles.  Multiplayer is the majority of the fun, as you collaborate while trying to parse how your friend is wearing a tank as a hat, why most of the city is missing or why half of the vehicles are out and out terrible.
You collect weapons that generally all have a strength and weakness, but gradually become stronger over time.  Not unlike diablo, the higher difficulties allow stronger weapons and let you obtain them through crate drops from enemies.  You end up getting a trickle of interesting guns and death machines, but if you need to get a shiny new toy every mission, this might not work out for you.  On the flip side, there are a lot of missions, so that may appeal to you instead.

Absolute Drift is a game about drifting.
It emphasizes timing, focus, reflex, and a nuanced comprehension of steering and gearshifting mechanics. However, this game does not have any technical stats or car-classes that allow you to tailor a car or course to your style. One engine and suspension type, cosmetic chassis, locked top-down view. The real nitty-gritty aspects of Drift Racing are left out of this simplified expression of the art.
Absolute Drift is a game about Zen. Revelations abound as you learn by tooling about in an openworld-style drifting playground, where you are enticed to push your skills and remove the training wheels in exchange for more precision and direct control. This teaches you patience and encourages clear-minded serenity to tackle multiplier challenges and exceptionally long drifts. Letting go, both of your ego and your break, transforms each turn into a slice of transcendent meditation. But there is more to Absolute Drift than letting go.
Absolute Drift is a game about drive. The drive to turn each course into a masterpice, one gear-shift at a time. Rather than listed names and a ladder leaderboard, you are given global player percentages, and where you fall in the over all community based on each course and event you complete. More than that, the urge to paint the tarmac with sublime compass-curves and deft switch-back transitions. It motivates you so effortlessly that time and anxiety fade away in the clouds of rubber smoke trailing behind you.
It's a good game.

Mechanically, it's not very different from other games in the series - it is a third person open-world historical fiction action game, where you play as an assassin in 16th century Italy, working to improve the standing of your faction and reduce the power of your opposing faction.
Like seems to be the case in this series, controls are improved over predecessors in that it makes combat easier, but that also serves to transition the game from being a stealthy assassin and more into being the sort of person who just jumps into combat and runs rampant. The primary change in this game is the ability to summon other assassins to help with combat/kills, which actually is pretty fantastic.

(Got this game for free courtesy of a Mamilos Club giveaway.)
Welcome to
, a game about perhaps the most over-powered lance-wielding knight in existance (moreso than your favorite lance unit in a
title...yeah, I said it...).  Begin your charge and slaughter enemies.  Collect the loot they drop and power yourself up to kill more monsters until you ultimately slaughter the evil dragon that's causing all the evil...evilness in the world.  Of course, after destroying the dragon, you are granted stackable New Game +'s.
I personally enjoy the feeling of being over-powered, but there's a massive issue with balance in
.  You'll eventually run into a point where you feel like you cannot proceed because you're too weak and you keep dying.  If you cannot proceed, you'll find yourself briefly grinding a previous level for some loot to spend on powerups.  If you cannot go to a previous level (and it's the first level), you'll benefit by continuous rushing until you grab a yellow flask, which grants you invincibility....I.E.  Super-Cheap potion.  Sometimes you'll find yourself to be too weak.  Other times (especially after grinding for 10-15 minutes), you'll find yourself to be too strong.
Aside from the balancing issue, there is an issue with the in-game score where some numeric tweaking is definitely in order.  Though your maximum stated purchase price is 9999, you can exceed it to become even more powerful, but it will still say it's at state that the maximum purchase price is 9999 (and a max state of about 49).
I LOVE the music and the spritework, but the gameplay is only good if you're looking for a casual experience.  You'll find yourself bored after a few hours.  I personally found myself stopping at 4 hours out of sheer boredom after completing every achievement's objective.  Sadly, the replayability is low, unless you simply want to boot up a new profile...in which case, would you want to after completing the game in an over-powered state?
Yes, I recommend
, but not for asking price ($3).   For about $1, I'd feel the price would be justified, especially given the incredible shortness of the game you'll be getting in return.  Though you'll end up over-powered, you'll end up feeling like Saitama...sans the comedy...
7/10  A fun game about Saitama's past life...until the balancing dissonance kicks in.

I know... 1.2 hours. But I've played this game over a dozen times many years ago on the old PS3 days, so I can review this perfectly.
Despite I am one of those who grew up with the classic Resident Evil titles, and despite RE5 was a bit overhyped and became a bit of a disappointment on release, I must admit that after playing it through a couple of times solo, and then co-op, I realized how great of a game this is.
Sure, it comes short to its predecessor, RE4, but what you get is one very well-made action third-person shooter. Short, yes, but it will keep you to the edge of your seat from beginning to end. Wonderful graphics, improved controls over RE4, a somewhat competent A.I partner and lots of things that make this a great AAA title from back before 2010.
It's not the best RE... But considering what it offers, it is a great game. And where it really shines it's in the co-op aspect. This game was disigned around co-op in mind, and let me tell you it is still the best co-op I've played. IT was also the last co-op split screen game I played, and certainly one of the last made. This made it such an amazing game. Nothing like sitting next to your buddy and sharing the screen like the old times. Replay value is infinite, adding to it the mini games which can also be played co-op.
Give RE5 a chance for what it is and you won't be disappointed. This game was the pinnacle of the "Action" Resident Evil games, even surpassing RE6 in many aspects.
As for the PC port:
Honestly, I didn't expect it to look so damn great, and to be so well optimized. Having just finished RE4, that game has a lot of issues with Win10. RE5, with the very few graphic options maxed out, running at a solid 120fps at 1080p it looks gorgeous for being 8 years-old. It really caught me off guard. Aiming is a breeze at these high frames and crisp resolution. Didn't bother playing on keyboard and mouse (my usual contols of choice) since this game wasn't designed for it. My Xbox One controller feels smooth, as a good old Dual Shock 3.
Not the best RE, again, but extremely underrated title.

Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood is an action-adventure stealth game with open world environment from Ubisoft. Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood is a sequel to the previous game Assassin's Creed 2.
Desmond is on the run again. This time, Desmond, Lucy, Rebecca and Shaun visit the ruined Auditore villa on Monteriggioni and make it as their new hiding place. Desmond has learn much from Ezio, but he still need to uncover more information from Ezio, so there he goes again, and again, to the Animus.
Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood gameplay is pretty much the same with Assassin's Creed 2, but is now focused on the city of Roma, where Ezio battle his way to eliminate Cesare Borgia and liberate Roma in the process. Ezio needs to liberate each sector in the city of Roma by destroying the Borgia towers. Doing so will free the sector and let Ezio rebuild the sector, such as reopening blacksmith shops, doctor shops or banks, gaining income in the process. The game also let Ezio to recruit Assassins by helping troubled civilians who can then help him to fight guards or kill his mission target. Recruited Assassins can gain experience as they are being called by Ezio or by completing contracts. Also, for the first time in Assassin's Creed franchise, Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood feature multiplayer game.
The graphics of the game still pretty much the same too. There may be some slight improvements but we won't notice it somehow. At least there is no downgrade.
Overall, Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood has taken the next step in Assassin's Creed franchise by introducing recruitable Assassins, while retaining the open world feature. I recommend this.

Shovel Knight is a challenging, yet very rewarding platformer in old-school pixel graphic style. It is famous for a reason, if I may say, and let me show you why...
- - - - - Commence argumentation - - - - -
Controls:
+easy to understand
+extremely responsive
Game Feeling:
+old-school pixel graphics for the retro-game enthusiasts out there
+awesome soundtracks
+superb storytelling
Story:
+easy to follow
+makes the player feel involved
+short and understandable sections of story text (prevents "too long to read" attitude)
-feels like a framework put together to give a reason to the story
Gameplay:
+great overworld map in style of Super Mario Bros. 3
+challenging, yet fair difficulty
+various items to assist your quest (varying from projectile weaponry to short-lived invulnerability)
+several items and skills to buy for in-game money
+great replay value
-short game (I'm only saying speedrun achievement with 1 hour 30 minutes or less)
- - - - - Commence results - - - - -
Shovel Knight is more than meets the eye. It is an experience everyone should make over the course of their gaming life. If you don't, you're at risk of missing out on one of the best indie titles out there. So steel thy shovel, and journey onward to dig deep into this game, because it's content is one of the greatest treasures in the game library Steam is able to offer.
Results:
Gameplay: 10/10, despite the short story
Feeling: 10/10 for retro-game enthusiasts like I am, 8/10 for anyone else
Story: 8/10
Difficulty: 8/10 (hard, but not Dark Souls levels of hard)
Final result: 9.5/10 for retro-gamers and 8.75/10 for regular players
- - - - - Commence final comment - - - - -
This game is a must-have in any old-school player's library and a great recommendation for any experienced player willing to put himself through the challenge that is Shovel Knight.

So basically what you're getting with this mod is a free DLC that valve never made. The voice acting, plot, animations, concept for this game are all outstandingly well done. The puzzles are on part if not harder then the base game so be ready for that, this mod has some similarities to the base game but it doesn't shove it in your face and is not obvious at all.
Unlike Chell (the main protagonist of portal 1 and 2} we actually get a small backstory to the main protagonist, that i won't spoil.
The length is that of a DLC and just about shorter then the base game, or it might just be the same length it just depends on how good you are at the tests. The gameplay hasn't changed one bit so no need to worry about that just in case you were.
So overall this is probably the best mod i've ever played,  if you love or even like portal and want to know what apature looks like before it all went wrong, or if you want to know what events took place before portal 2 then this is the perfect lore friendly story telling mod that you must download.
seriously though this mod is so fun and has such a good story, if you own portal 2 then there is no reason for you to not own this mod, and there is no exuse because it is free, so do yourself a favour and get this mod!
But to point out some negatives there are some minor glitches and the occasional lag spike but this can forgiven as it doesn't happen to often and when it does it's not for that long, if it was in the main game this would be an issue but being a massive free mod and knowing this doesn't happen to often, this can be forgiven.

-Audio design is terrible, and the depth of it is dreadful. For example, A big formation of bombers and escort fighters 50ft above you, are drowned out by the nosie of a gas grenade going off 10 ft away from you, as well as the sond from the planes having no bass at all, just a flat noise that is unreasonably quiet.
-They claimed this game was going to be very historically accurate, which it really isn't.
-Expensive for being what it is. I am aware that it is a Call of Duty game, but in this case it doesn't justify the pricetag.
Campaign:
-Short length, while the level of detail put in to each mission is somewhat high, it's rather short and uninteresting.
-Very cliché, the campaign is not imaginative in the slightest, and very predictable.
-Russian weapons on the western front whilst weapons like the g43 have been left out entirely.
-Extremely frustrating on-rail sections on higher difficulties.
-Only one somewhat likeable character.
-Pretty samey missions and where they get unique it gets really clunky and unrealistic, and quite frankly, not really interesting.
-The inability to select weapons when going into a mission, which has been present in at least one Treyarch title that I know of.
-The rate of fire on all of the light machine guns available in the campaign. The Browning m1919 shoots at the rate of a 50.cal, and deals the damage equivilent to a BB gun.
-The anti-aircraft guns in the game are single-barreled 20mm flaks with ugly flash hiders/compensators(?), where they could have put in a little variation, or outright replaced them with Flakvierlings or 3,7cm flak guns, which were more likely to be mounted on the vehicles used in game.
-No MG tripods, and MG's generally have a very low ammunition capacity.
-No Sd.Kfz 222's :(
-A lot of unskippable cutscenes and in-game scripted sequences.
-Random framedrops, despite having a decent rig and lowering graphics to avoid it.

-You can finally use the sd.kfz 251's mg42 without having to parkour on top of it. (Referring to CoD2)
-You can finally pick up MG's that were stationary in previous games.
-Nice graphics
Multiplayer: oh where to start.
-Extremely hectic.
-small maps (except for the war maps) that highly favors shotguns, smg's automatic rifles, and quickscoping.
-The majority of the sniper rifles are a one hit kill to the torso, and these rifles (Lee Enfield, Springfield M1903, Karabiner) can't use their ironsights, probably due to the fact they are OHK's, which makes the most common weapons of the war unusable.
-The Division system takes attachments, and restricts them to certain classes, which results in the B.A.R and the Fg42 being unable to have bipods, which makes me want to puke. The B.A.R with a bipod is so beautiful, it makes me really happy.  :^(
-The Fg42's scope is placed on top of the foregrip, when in actuality, it is located on the magazine well. This also makes me very sad, as it loses a big chunk of its charm. You can also not remove the bayonet if you choose the rifleman division.
-A distinct lack of weapons from the singleplayer campaign, such as the M1919 LMG and the revolver from the campaign is not available in multiplayer for some reason, plus the fact that there aren't really many weapons in general.
-Toxic playerbase, as per usual, but I just mute chat and all the people by default.
-Due to the maps being small, people have a tendency to spawn behind you, specifically when you're using an LMG with a bipod hunkered down somewhere.

-You can acquire loot boxes without actually paying for them, which is alright.
Zombie mode:
-Only 1 map (not counting the tiny very uniform prologue map)
-Said map has special enemies that cannot be disabled, which can make the game very hectic, and doesn't allow for chill play due to the ever increasing difficulty.
-The Bazooka, Panzerschreck, and flamethrower are now unobtainable from the mystery box, and can only be used temporarily if you activate a one-time-use ability that you can only acquire randomly through lootboxes. I really don't like that.
-They claimed to have tried to make the zombie mode scarier, and the only scary thing about it is the ridiculously low amount of effort they put in to make it so.
-If you join a game in progress you won't get any achievements for the duration of that match, which I noticed after a 4 hour long session beating the hardcore easter egg, where I told them to go ahead and start without me, and I joined on round 2.
-No sort of setting for this game mode whatsoever, apart from map selection, which is a shame since it's a PvE game mode, and modifying it as you see fit would be really fun.
-Really ugly and generic animated camo applied to your weapon when you Pack-a-punch it. Wish you could disable it somehow.
-Certain areas you're forced to be in if you follow the main objectives are very cramped and difficult to navigate in considering zombies pop out from everywhere.
-As mentioned above, zombeis pop out everywhere, which triggers a sudden noise. An attempted jumpscare which falls very flat when you get stuck on him and promptly die due to your massive zombie following.

-Something fresh to entertain me for a few hours, and probably more to come once some maps are actually released.
-Nice and intricate level design with many puzzles and objectives to figure out
-Very gruesome and detailed zombies
-Despite being annoying sometimes, the new zombie types do freshen the game up quite a bit.
-A zombie mode exclusive multi-shot rocket launcher based on the
that was a pleasant surprise when I first obtained it.
-I greatly appreciate the sense of progression in the zombie mode now.
If you, ten years from now, during a cozy winter sale when this game is  95% off, want to play a pretty good zombie game, buy this.
Note: I could go on bashing even more of the guns and smaller details, but even at the length this review is at right now, I doubt anyone will read it through.
Thank you if you did though :^)

Sheer uncomplicated fun and comical over-the-top action is what Saints Row: The Third delivers. Its light-hearted story is absurd and the missions are even more so. Overflowing with activities and customisation options SR3 throws the player into a bizarro world where almost everything is possible.
Steelport is full of things to do and never leaves the player bored. The quest design is varied and the scenarios range from typical shoot-outs and car chases to wrestling fights, Tron-like hacking and tiger escorts. Some of the quests can be a little tricky but in my experience not too difficult to get right after a few tries. Character progression feels meaningful and boosts the player's abilities noticeably. By the time most quests are done the character usually is about to hit the maximum level which can grant almost complete invincibility.
There are a few minor glitches and bugs that can be irritating. Faulty collision detection, not the most intelligent combat AI and at times lunatic NPC drivers are somewhat expected in an open world game like this. These incidents can be amusing at best and annoying at worst.
Overall though SR3 is highly polished. If you're looking for a good time, here it is.

This game had Potential.
More often than not for a game like this, you see it simply labled "It's S@$&!" and they walk away. But the truth is this game had potential, and sadly that potential never got off the ground.
I bought into this game during its early access state, sometime in alpha 13 I believe. During that time, I was big into Dwarf Forttress like games that had more graphics, and this game was amazing in that regard. A mixture of minecraft style view with dwarf fortress rouge-like hardness; the game was a shoo-in to take the market in my opinion.
Sometime after alpha 14, the game's dev simply stopped updating it all together. SInce then, the game has been abandoned.
I believe this game still has some potential as both a learning tool and a testimate; a testimate that such games are necessairy to bring hope and inovation to our industry. So please, don't review this game as being terrible becasue its incomplete, or unbalanced; review it as learning-game, one that was used to learn how to fail faster (make mistakes so you don't do it again), and how to make more awesome games.

Once again, it's a cool game concept. Travelling through time, the possibility of playing through different eras of history and even pre-history, while occasionally bringing in weapons from a different time period to help you out, all within a first-person shooter seems like it would be hard to screw up.
HOWEVER. This game doesn't capitalize enough on its own ideas. For example, in total there are only four points in history you visit: The American Civil War, both World Wars, and Pompeii at the end. Why can't we go visit the Roman Empire? Or see the Peloponnesian Wars? Hell, why not go investigate Ancient Egypt? Or if you really want to go nuts, take the player back to pre-historic times, like the Jurassic era. Running away from a T-Rex because you're armed with nothing but a tree branch and some rocks could make for an interesting chase sequence!
On top of that, I noticed that a lot of the time, NPCs kept walking straight through walls, sometimes even getting stuck in them. Another time, an enemy was actually shooting me through a ROCK.
And if THAT weren't enough, the game ends on a friggin' cliffhanger that is highly unlikely to ever be resolved, because I doubt the developers (if they're even still around) are going to release a sequel.
Overall, it's a mediocre title that could have been fantastic, had they simply gave it a bit more effort and imagination.

This is the best mod I have ever seen.
It is clear throughout the mod that a lot of care and effort had been put in place to make this mod possible. The story was extremely well-written (I liked the (very) end a lot) and the animations, modelling and voice-acting were very good too.
There were some negatives, however. For instance, at the beginning of the mod we have Cave Johnson walk us through even the simplest of tasks yet I got stumped for half an hour on the second test chamber. I'm guessing that the developers assumed the players would be very experienced portal veterans. Truth is, most people haven't touched portal since years ago. This made the tests increasingly frustrating and often made me quit the game through confusion.
The level-design, although clever and well-thought, out had too many elements inside each room. I often didn't notice where the cubes were as there were too many other distractions. The developers also seemed to like emancipation grills very much, placing on average about 3 in each level. I usually wouldn't have a problem with this but I personally dislike emancipation grills. I find that they are the most difficult element to work with in a test and I would've preferred more levels with turrets/conversion gel.
There were more positives though. I thoroughly enjoyed the chambers when I could figure them out and as mentioned above, the very end was nicely done. Also, it's free! So there's practically nothing to lose (except the time it takes to solve the puzzles :P)

Short review: Portal 2 is easy mode. PS: Mel is hard mode.
long review:
The only complaint I have about Portal 1 and 2 is that by necessity, so many of the levels just feel like tutorials for the next level, which really limits the replayability of those two games.  You can replay for commentary, easter eggs, and achievements, but once you've solved a puzzle once, you'll never have to think your way through it again.
Portal Stories: Mel avoids that issue by skipping the training levels, and making all the puzzles really hard.
I finished Portal 1 in two hours and Portal 2 in six hours.  They're games you finish in one or two sittings.
One playthrough of PS: Mel kept me busy for an entire week.  I frequently had to take breaks partway through test chambers.  I frequently worked my way to the end of a level only to realize I needed to come up with another solution that would allow me to bring along the cube I left sitting on a button, way back.  It's a challenging game. Hint: always find a way to bring the cube with you.  You'll need it later.
The quality is about what you'd expect from a paid game from a professional game studio, which is to say better than you'd expect from a free game from a mod team.
The story fits perfectly into the continuity established in Portal 1 and 2.  It's well written and lends a nice sense of urgency to the puzzle solving.
The voice acting sounds clean and professional.
There's a decent boss fight at the end.
There's a lot of attention paid to visual detail.  The levels have a lot of atmosphere and really recapture the feeling of exploring Aperture that made Portal 2 so much fun.  I love the way the beat up, old, prototype portal gun looks.
There's only one thing I found disappointing about this mod and that is visual cues could have been better.  There are locations where the environment details seem too dense, and it becomes difficult to locate the clean surfaces that you can attach portals to.   Having to spend five minutes searching for the one white spot in a very cluttered, dirty room hurts the pacing of the game.  The glowing dotted lines connecting switches to puzzle components often cross each other, or travel around corners making it hard to tell which switch activates which object.  Sometimes I was just pushing buttons to see what happens, when I felt like I should have been planning.  Towards the end, the personality core that guides you actually starts telling you where to look, because the rooms don't really draw your eye where it needs to go.
Can't beat that price tag.

I have played every LEGO game to date and will probably continue to do so. This game is another good addition to the series. Why only good? Well here are the few problems I had.
1. The raptor pounce ability is by far the most frustrating bug. It literally can halt your progress on a mission and prevent you from continuing.
2. Playing a dinosaur = AWESOME. Being limited to only a few of the smaller dinosaurs for the majority of the game = not awesome. Seriously you aren't going to roam around as a T-Rex or fly over the landscape as a Pteradon. Those are only usable in specific areas that are designed for them (And there aren't many of those areas)
3. STOP PUTTING COLLECTIBLES IN CHASE SCENES. Sorry that is a pet peave of mine, nothing I hate more than playing the same chase scene 5 times in a row just to try and get a collectible (Especially since you can only see behind you and not where you are going most of the time. And even when it is a sideview chase you have no control over camera to determine depth so aiming for the object is just as difficult sometimes.
4. Bring back the 1,000,000 stud challenges. (Never mind. After 100% the game there is a bonus level on Isla Nublar.)
That is essentially the drawbacks to the game. So then why do I give it a positive review? Well let me tell you.
1. Hybrid dinosaurs
2. Just as much fun in Open Roam as there is in the story line.
3. Advancement on the buddy up system from LOTR Lego (No buddy up attacks, but buddy up puzzles)
4. collectibles weren't nearly as frustrating as some of the earlier titles.
5. Even with the above drawbacks it provided me over 30 hours of game play and I was able to 100% the game.
6. The usual LEGO humor is still rampant.
All in all it was worth the money if you are a fan of the LEGO games.

ArmA 3 is one of the most versatile games in my library, within the military simulation genre of course. Though, if I’m being honest, there really is no competition from other titles; so even compared to other games the statement remains true. That speaks volumes for this title, at least individually.
Though the game is solid it its ‘vanilla’ state, the modding community is what really propels this game forward. ArmA 3 is a highly moddable game, from advanced sound scapes to modern high quality unit packs, the majority of the time there will be a mod to what you’re looking for.
Want to fend off a zombie horde from invading your small village, armed with an outdated M1 Garand? It can be done, combining mods together to make your experience better. .
Want to recreate the iconic nuclear explosion and following cutscene from Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare? Well you can, but I warn you it takes a little bit to code!
Vanilla doesn’t offer a lot of replayability, but the inclusion of mods into the title have introduced a game that is four years old and still being updated actively by the developers. Yes, you read that correctly, ArmA 3 is still being actively developed despite its age.
Over the past two years, the developers have introduced an advanced editor, 64 bit executables, new graphics, new sounds, better optimization, new lighting effects… just to name a few free updates that everyone received.
The developers continue to support their game, which is always a bonus for me.

It's hard to give a thumbs down to something that's both free and presented so well, but alas, the more I play, the more I dislike it, even as a get better at solving the puzzles as I've learned what's expected of me and the typical tropes. Seriously, I'm practically flying through the levels now, and yet still feel more exhausting than fun. This is compounded by the poor humor that's an inferior version of the original, coupled with bad voice acting that you're absolutely bombarded with, and also boring, amateurish music that in some cases doesn't even loop properly. I'm actually amazed at the effort though, that a free fan made mod actually went to such lengths to write new (albeit unoriginal and amateur) lines and have them acted out, but once the novelty wears thin you'll begin to find each line of dialougue more and more grating.
Plenty of other thumbs downers have touched on the difficulty in solving the puzzles, all the while managing to make themselves sound like maybe they're the ones who are just bad at puzzles. I think it's more that the bar that this franchise has set is incredibly high, and this feels poorly designed in comparison. It isn't only that, it's in the way the puzzles are challenging that makes them feel like drudgery. Almost every puzzle has you reaching the exit only to have you turn around and realize you need to bring with you all those boxes that got you there, which just feels cheap compared to the original where most of the time getting to the exit meant success. Puzzles here feel confined and super restricted to a very narrow way of solving, whereas in portal 2 you're having fun learning new puzzle mechanics and flying around playing with physics, here there are no new mechanics so what they've done is tried to up the challenge instead. The original also had excellent pacing, mixing up the puzzle solving runs with the story/adventure parts. In this, the puzzle sections seem to drag on, especially when you solved something tough and see that you're on puzzle 2 of 12.
Overall this is an awesome effort, I just really can't wrap my head around the fact they had multiple playtesters that were ok with the tediousness of the puzzles. It's a well presented addition to the portal story plagued by lackluster voicework/music and puzzles that just aren't fun.

This is the number one game in my library. For over a year, it was the only game other than Spore and the contents of the Orange Box. Five years later, I still go back to it every now and then. I've had many a 14-hour marathon day playing Rome Total War, quite often back to back. I'm pretty sure I got a chance to play as every civilization before I switched computers and lost my progress. I've even gone through the Barbarian Invasion campaign a few times. Honestly, if I'd never bought Civ V, I'd have well over 1,000 hours racked up by now.
This is strategy at its purest. Not only do you have the strategy of "How do I move around my armies and generals and funds to best maintain and expand my empire?" you also have the battles themselves. Many games do only one or the other, and those games can go hang. I'm not going to go into detail about the games mechanics and why they're good or bad; instead, I'm going to regale you with but a few of the ridiculous stories that have come out of my 800+ hours.
*My British faction leader, supported by two other armies, slaughters a quarter of the entire Brutii force over ten years, littering Poland with heroic victories. He eventually meets his end, known as "the Legendary," defending a town against a Roman force three times his size. Succesfully.
*An elite squad of Berserkers sacrifice themselves on the walls of Rome itself, eliminating two entire legionary cohorts and flanking the wall's other defenders.

If you have just finished ACII and jump right into Brotherhood, you may feel a bit weird at first. Part of this weirdness feeling is good: Ezio “feels” older – he should be. The patchy beard, the slight comments from NPC’s here and there, the louder noise he makes when he drops from a height, it all adds to the feeling that the character you have played with since his teenage days in Firenze is now close to or in his  40’s – but don’t worry; he can still do all the good stuff. This, ageing, is not an easy thing to convey in a game and many developers will not do it at all, keeping their character closer to a young aged audience, but for a story like AC it is both needed and, in this case, well executed.
The other part of the weirdness is perhaps not so good. AC Brotherhood needs time. In the beginning you feel a bit thrown into the game world without much to go on, no real idea where to begin. Perhaps that is a good thing. Ultimately, the small pieces of your “work” here and there begin to consolidate the picture and you start to tread on more solid ground. One point of complaint is the map and menu navigation which Ubisoft for some reason messed with from the previous game, with not so good results.
Ultimately, Brotherhood continues the story from ACII nicely, deepens the plot, creates more questions but is all in all enjoyable. The recruitment of assassins adds a nice touch to the feeling that you are part of something larger and eventually – at its head.

TL;DR, Arma is a military game that sides with realism and isn't for everyone, but is fantastic for those who appreciate what it is.
Arma 3 is a game that is great. For various reason that you may not understand if you don't create bonds with those you play with. Arma 3 isn't Call of Duty, or Battlefield. Its closer in nature to Operation Flashpoint in its focus on realism and military simulation. The guns function like real guns, traveling takes time, and doing so takes energy away from your character making combat more difficult with exhaustion.
Single player is interesting and has a story that keeps you going enough in the world that you are apart of. You're not the hero of the game, you're another soldier, a cog in the machine. It is just as easy for you to die at any given point in the game as it is for anyone else.
The multiplayer is entirely based on what you end up playing. King of the Hill modes are great modes that let you run around in an area trying to stay in cover and hunting down other players while working with team mates is entirely optional. Each server has an experience system and money system that rewards you for your actions and allows you to purchase more items and vehicles to use to transport others to the fight.
There are various coop multiplayer servers pitting you, and a platoon of soldiers made up of other players, against an army of AI forces scattered throughout the massive map. Objectives vary and missions can be anywhere from 10 minutes, to 4 hours, and beyond. Teamwork is a must and most servers require you join a teamspeak server to participate in squad play. This is highly advisable as communication is extremely necessary. You will make friends. That is not an option. Many groups are open to new players, just accept that you will be hitting a learning curve.
Once you get done with basic play, coop or otherwise, the Mod experience is where it is at. Massive mods, enhancements to the physics system, sound enhancers, multiple maps can all be used in the game. Because of this, finding a group to play with is key. They will help you grow to understand things. Which mods they use, which systems enhancers they run, all vary as to which group and server you play on. There are things that I have grown used to, that make the vanilla game just plain and not as exciting. The enchanced medical systems makes saving a team mate the most exciting moments. Their lives are in your hands. Your failure means them having to travel 5-10+ minutes to rejoin the fight in some missions. You have to succeed. The pressure is on. Save their life.
But this game is extremely fantastic, for various reasons, but it does have its low points. There are physic glitches, getting caught on walls or doors sometimes is annoying at various times, even getting you killed some times. But there are ways to escape them if you have time. Because of the nature of the game, you have to get used to the massive keyboard setup, controller is almost not an option. Mods only exponetially make that problem worse, but learning them is a process that is made easy with others. Another reason why communication is key. Again, reinforcing the fact that you need to communicate. Which will mean you will need a microphone and the lack of fear to speak up. You'll grow used to it in time.
Overall the game is great and is as good a game today as it was early on. If you can appreciate a slow, worthwhile experience, the game is worth every dollar.

Arma 3 represents an aesthetic overhaul of the series. Unbelievable dynamic lighting, a volumetric cloud system, genuine vehicle physics, 3D weapon optics, ragdoll, noticeably improved weapon audio, and other grainy, eye-level details await scrutiny inside Arma 3's macro elegance. The best improvement is the merciful cutting of Arma 2's rigid, Tin-Man-without-oil combat animations, which makes infantry combat more responsive in your hands.
A half-year in paid pre-release has given Arma 3 time to gestate, but the final build is far from being a comprehensive reinvention of the series, and some long-standing blemishes that arise from its nature as a gargantuan simulation linger. Even on high-end hardware, my framerate dips under the spectacle of some multiplayer missions. Friendly AI units, though marginally better-behaved, still depend on the player to be their brains, an issue that's circumvented by playing Arma the way God intended it: cooperatively. Altis life for example. Shovel Knight... Where do I begin with Shovel Knight?
Well, first off, it's a platformer. There's somethin'. Oh, and did I mention that it's FREAKING SWEET?!
No, seriously; this game is awesome! Shovel Knight puts you into the role of - you guessed it - the shovelrous blue burrower himself, Shovel Knight! (And yes, the game is full of puns like that)
As for the level design, it's nearly flawless! Each level puts you into many different environments each with their own different enemies, traps, and platforming! Did I mention there's also powerups? The difficulty inches up so little that you'll think the levels aren't even getting harder, but in reality, you're just getting better.
The boss fights are difficult at first, but with a learning curve that's just low enough so you can go "hmm.. I think I'll try that again" and totally own the boss's face. The dialogue is different for each boss, and - oh yeah, there's dialogue too. Everything is all medieval-ey, and I love it. Back to dialogue, each boss has their own personality that fits their name quite well. Take a boss named King Knight for instance. He's selfish, arrogant, and the typical stereotype of a bad monarch. THIS IS HOW I WANT EVERY BOSS FIGHT EVER TO BE. (I also think this is what every boss fight ever WANTS to be XD)
Still 3tough5u? Well, there are numerous items and armors you can buy and equip using the absolute mountains of gold you pick up on your journey to help you along the way. For example, the Phase Locket. It makes you invulnerable to enemies and traps (But not pits!) for a short amount of time. Combine these powerups with a limited but fair magic meter and you've got yourself a delicious Megaman sandwich. Now let's add some more awesome to that super fighting sammich. As I said before, there are armors! Each is fairly expensive, but with its own special perks. One gives you more magic, but increases the amount of damage you take, another prevents knockback but hinders your mobility, etc.
Now the currency system. Oh, the currency system. Thought this game couldn't get any better? Well, take those creative levels and awesome boss fights and stick loads of muddatrukkin money in them. I'm pretty sure you don't have to be good at the maths to know how cool this is.
Badass bosses + epic levels + fair difficulty increments + truckloads of dolla dolla gems = You made a good game.
Not to mention, there are no lives in Shovel Knight. You can die as many times as you like, there's no such thing as a game over here. Instead, I'm going to have to quote Caddicarus here: "You don't lose lives... you lose f***ing money!" Yes. If you die even once in Shovel Knight, the game will take away your hard earned cash. But all is not lost! You can reclaim your money by finding the floating bags that it flies around in. I agree with Caddy in the fact that this adds to the drive to get back to where you died to reclaim what you've lost, and you feel oh so good when you get it back.
The soundtrack?
.....
MARRY ME JAKE KAUFMAN! (No homo)
Ahem, sorry. Got a bit weird there. What I'm saying is that I have rarely heard a retro soundtrack as great as Shovel Knight's. Every piece perfectly fitting into it's assigned level while you dig around looking for trouble. There are good soundtracks. There are great soundtracks. Then there's Shovel Knight's soundtrack.
Most people think that the story in this game is short, and that is why Shovel Knight gets some flak from the community, but once again, I'm right there with you, Caddy. I don't care! The game was so insane up until the credits that I'm just too happy to give this game a bad rep just for the story not being long. Besides, there's a new game plus for all the Completionists out there. As for the Plague of Shadows update, I will update this with what I think of it once I have finished it.
Do I recommend Shovel Knight? Well, lemme check my pulse for a sec..
YES! I recommend this game to high heaven! If you're a fan of platformers - heck, even if you're not - buy this game. Go on. It's ok. I'm right here just.. just click the freaking purchase button already. JUST DO IT!

I don't even know where to begin with this review. By now, it's safe to assume that most people who would be interested in this game have had a chance to play through some or all of it on one platform or another, but just in case there are those who have not...
The premise is simple... You have a yard that seperates your house and ultimately your brain from a bunch of zombies who want to invade it and eat said brain. You must plant a line of defense on your yard...a line of defense made up of plants.
Plants cost sun power, which periodically falls from the sky, and can also be obtained through sun-producing plants, which you will plant (assuming you want to keep your brain intact). Different plants have differing strengths and weaknesses, and likelwise so do the zombies. The elements of the stages change (sometimes it's night, sometimes there's a pool, sometimes there's fog, sometimes there's all of the above). You must find the right combinations of plants to defend your yard in any situation, and that is literally it!
Sounds ridiculous, and it is, but it is far and away one of my favorite games - and I'm not someone who ever really liked casual games all that much. I have played through this game countless times on various platforms, and I still do if I need a quick time waster or something to cheer me up a bit.
Give it a shot. It is recommended.

A very good ‘free to play’ experience for a casual dip. Though ultimately a game which loses itself between visions of a great Fishing Simulation and just a Fishing Game.
Akin to a Hollywood movie, which having employed a quality writer, director and cast, is sabotaged by producers and editors imposing a 'lollypop' formula upon it.
Having lost sight of the fact that fishing is the most popular sport on the planet, the producers decided to change direction mid project. Distancing themselves from an audience seeking a long term relationship they opened the door on a casual fling. This compromise will leave both the non fisher and fisher feeling unfulfilled. Great promise replaced by short term gratification.
‘Lollypops’, in the form of paid DLC, throw balance out the window. They provide a short term ‘hit’ for those not seeking a simulation, though hardly encourage any hopes of longevity for the project.
To continue the Hollywood theme. Here we have a movie which will benefit from a ‘Directors Cut’ sometime in the future.
Meanwhile, enjoy the initial free to play part and don’t grieve too much over the producers missed opportunity.
Their loss, my disappointment.

This game was very fun to play, and felt like an official Portal installment for the most part.
I'll begin with my criticism of the game and then get to my praise: For being a separate game, this one used a lot of the items from Portal 2, and there didn't seem to be a ton of new distinct objects in the levels (beyond the red emancipation grid, which was a great touch). And some of the dialog felt like it was maybe pushing a bit too hard towards the solutions. If you disliked using the gels in Portal 2, I'm sorry, but you have to use them quite a lot here, even in the first chamber. A bit of the pacing of the story felt a bit off, particularly in the ending, which I think might have been a bit more effective if Mel was never shown (it threw off the "realness" and feeling of being the player). But then again, I finished this right after Portal 2, which we all know has a perfect ending. ;) And if you're looking for something with dialog as memorable as in the other two games, you probably won't find it here, particularly since most of the speech is spoken by characters who are far too nice or formal for the snarky comments that you'd get form GLaDOS or Wheatley.
And now, my praise. In general, this game was great. Most of the puzzles were very interesting and well designed, and the difficulty was perfect for someone who has played at least one of the other games. To someone who has never played either it might be a bit difficult, but definitely not impossible. And a couple of the puzzles were pure genius. (I'm looking at you, hard light ramp.) I liked that there were some callbacks to the other games, especially Portal 2, but in general everything felt original and fresh. I was very happy to see that the fight against the final boss, an enemy quite different from the typical cores, also played out very differently. The developers did a great job making sure that nothing in the story contradicted any canon parts of the Portal storyline, meaning that it could potentially be considered canon should Valve for some reason decide to make it so. Also, the new art/designs in here are just awesome. I actually like Virgil's vintage wood and metal design better than any of the cores in the official games. Finally, for being a free game this is incredible. I would have been happy to pay at least the price of the first game.
So in summary, I highly recommend Portal Stories: Mel to anyone who liked Portal and Portal 2 (or actually just anyone in general).

Back to the roots, at least the latest installment of the CoD franchise was marketed this way. Does it hold up? The answer is as boring as it can be: it depends on what you were expecting.
Singleplayer:
In the single player campaign your are put into the shoes of Private Daniels, an US soldier who fights his way through various European theatres of WW II. If you have watched the HBO series "Band of Brothers", much of the story will be very familiar. The devs cannot deny that the series was the largest inspiration for the story of this game. Many locations are similar, characters like your fellow soldiers are corresponding to characters from TV. No innovation prices there, but it's not really bad either.
In terms of gameplay we were (again) promised rather signifcant changes and innovation. Of course Sledgehammer doesn't excatly deliver. It is still CoD as it has been for 15 years. You fight your way through hordes of mindless AI opponents until you trigger the next script. There is always something happening, one explosion is followed by the next, one wave of enemies is followed by another. You find the obligatory MG sections, tank sections, AA gun sections, car chases and even a hideous plane section. The game is still very linear, eventhough it opens up sometimes and leaves room on small decisions. Smaller adjustments were made: automatic regeneration is a thing of the past, you get to collect healthpacks; no more jumping around between different protagonists, the focus is on Daniels and his guys. They implemented a stealth mechanic that you have to use in a few sections - but all "stealth" levels turn into a CoD typical shootout in the end.
Multiplayer:
I haven't seen too much of it yet. But after a few hours I think it's ground solid experience that is more similar to the experience in MW I and MW II than to the last few installments. The matches feel a bit slower, because all the jumping and wallrunning of recent CoDs is missing.
Really new is the inclution of a new game mode "War". Basically it's similar to "Rush" in the Battlefield franchise. One team has to fulfill certain objectives, the opponents have to prevent this. After one objective is completed the map expands until every assignment is done or the timer for the attackers reaches 0.
Sledgehammer / Activision also jumped on board the lootbox train. They even had the really stupid idea create a social space in which you can move around and watch others opening their lootboxes and see what they get. You even get "social experience points" for doing that. Lootboxes drop on Normandy beach. What the hell ...
Nazi-Zombis:
didn't really try so far.
Final Verdict:
CoD WW II tries to make something new in taking a very old setting. It's not a great game, but it's not bad either. It more of the same old in new clothes. This is not bad in itsself, but doesn't make a really good game either.
If you like CoD anyway you probably have bought it already. If you haven't played a CoD game in the last few years, but generally liked the franchise, I think WW II is worth taking a look. Waiting for a sale is an option, eventhough it may take a while until the pricetag drops signifcantly.
If it was possible I would "maybe" recommend this game. So I leave it with a "yes". Buy it if you like CoD style games and are not sure if it is worth your while - leave it if you do not like CoD or look for a FPS that also teases your brain.

Overall, a very solid and enjoyable game, even if I enjoyed II a little more. 8/10 compared to AC II's 9/10.

I've been playing the EDF series since the very first game in 2003.
EDF 4.1 is one of the best games ever made when it comes to pure fun, and now it's even better on the PC with a incessant 60 frames per second, a first for the series.
If you're new to the series, here's a quick rundown:
Giant alien insects and robots/aircraft are invading the earth to exterminate all human life.
They are all several magnitudes larger than a tank, and there are an insane number of them. Seriously, there are anywhere between 30 to over 100 enemies in a group at a time.
It's up to you, faceless soldier, to destroy them all. It's essentially B-Movie, the game.
You've got 98 missions, 800 weapons, 4 classes, and 5 difficulties.
About 20 different enemy types including giant ants, spiders, hornets, 30ft tall robots, 50ft tall tripods, and a 300ft tall transformer robot, the Motherships, alien aircraft, and so on.
Don't listen to other people when they say the game is a 'mindless shooter.'
Sure, it can be on the lower difficulties, and that's fine.
But once you try Hardest/Inferno with 4 players online, EDF is far from mindless. Only players with peak reaction speed, communication, situational awareness and tactical planning will succeed.
One word of warning, the first 10 missions of the game are slow and not representative of the whole game.
The progression starts off small with giant ants and boring weapons.
To really understand what EDF is like, you're likely going to have to play way past the 2-hour refund mark to have access to orbital satellite strikes, fight Godzilla, pilot Pacific Rim Jaegers, use laser snipers, napalm grenades and a whole slew of bad♥♥♥♥♥content.
It is well worth it.
EDF is a testament to the fact that most of the time, the simplest games are the best ones.
Nothing since Doom has demonstrated that better than EDF. It's a beloved series, and if you're even slightly interested, you simply owe it to yourself to give it a try.
Get this game. There is HUNDREDS of hours of entertainment, especially online with 4 players.
Just ask any newcomer to the series and 99% of the time, you'll see their unbridled, quickly attained burning love for it.
